Ekegusii: Ere agasaba, agateeba: “Aye Omonene, Nyasae bw’omonene one Aburaamu, nagosabire, onsesenie ase amang’ana aane a reero, okorere omonene one Aburaamu obwanchani.

English: Behold, I am standing by the spring of water. The daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.
Kiswahili: Tazama, nimesimama karibu na kisima hiki cha maji, nao binti za watu wa mji huu wanakuja kuteka maji.
Ekegusii: Rora, ninteneine aiga ase ensoko y’amaache, na abaiseke b’omochie oyo ngocha bare kobuucha amaache.

English: Let it happen, that the young lady to whom I will say, ‘Please let down your pitcher, that I may drink,’ then she says, ‘Drink, and I will also give your camels a drink,’—let her be the one you have appointed for your servant Isaac. By this I will know that you have shown kindness to my master.”
Kiswahili: Basi na iwe hivi, nitakapomwambia binti mmojawapo, ‘Tafadhali tua mtungi wako nipate kunywa maji,’ naye akisema, ‘Kunywa, nitawanywesha na ngamia wako pia.’ Basi na awe ndiye uliyemchagua kwa ajili ya mtumishi wako Isaki. Kwa hili nitajua umemhurumia bwana wangu.”
Ekegusii: Tiga ebe iga; Kondaborie oyomo obo: Koranche obeke enyongo yao inse, inche inywe amaache, na ere karang’iranerie: Ee, kanywe aye, na nimbuuchere chingamia chiao nachirochio; otige oyio abe nere gwachoreire omosomba oo Isaka, na inche erio nimanye ng’a aye Omonene one gwankoreire amaya ase obwanchani.”

English: Before he had finished speaking, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, with her pitcher on her shoulder.
Kiswahili: Ikawa kabla hajamaliza kuomba, Rebeka akatokea akiwa na mtungi begani mwake. Alikuwa binti wa Bethueli. Bethueli alikuwa mwana wa Milka aliyekuwa mke wa Nahori ndugu wa Abrahamu.
Ekegusii: Ritang’ani atarakoora ogosaba kwaye, akarora Rebeka ogocha obogoretie enyongo yaye mareko. Ere nomoiseke o Betueli, na Betueli nomwana o Milka, moka Nahori, momura omwabo Aburaamu.

English: The young lady was very beautiful to look at, a virgin. No man had known her. She went down to the spring, filled her pitcher, and came up.
Kiswahili: Huyu msichana alikuwa mzuri sana wa sura, bikira, ambaye hakuna mtu aliyekuwa amekutana naye kimwili. Aliteremka kisimani, akajaza mtungi wake akapanda juu.
Ekegusii: Na omoiseke oria nigo areenge omonyakieni, naende nomwekuungi, otaraba na mosacha onde. Agatirimboka gochia ase ensoko, agaichoria enyongo yaye amaache, agatiira.

English: The servant ran to meet her, and said, “Please give me a drink, a little water from your pitcher.”
Kiswahili: Ndipo yule mtumishi akaharakisha kukutana naye akamwambia, “Tafadhali nipe maji kidogo katika mtungi wako.”
Ekegusii: Erio omosomba oria akaminyoka bwango gochia komoorotota, akamosaba: “Koranche, ong’e amaache inywe.”

English: She said, “Drink, my lord.” She hurried, and let down her pitcher on her hand, and gave him a drink.
Kiswahili: Yule msichana akasema, “Kunywa, bwana wangu.” Akashusha kwa haraka mtungi mkononi mwake na akampa, akanywa.
Ekegusii: Ere akamoiraneria akamoteebia: “Kanywe, omonene one!” Agatoora enyongo yaye bwango, akayebeeka koboko kwaye, akamoa, na ere akanywa.

English: When she had finished giving him a drink, she said, “I will also draw for your camels, until they have finished drinking.”
Kiswahili: Baada ya kumpa yule mtumishi yale maji, akamwambia, “Nitateka maji kwa ajili ya ngamia zako pia mpaka wote watosheke.”
Ekegusii: Gakoorire komoa amaache, akabora: “Ne chingamia chiao boigo ninchibuuchere, na chirochio chinywe.”

English: She hurried, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again to the well to draw, and drew for all his camels.
Kiswahili: Akafanya haraka kumimina maji kwenye birika ya kunyweshea wanyama, akakimbia kisimani kuteka maji mengine na akateka ya kuwatosha ngamia wake wote.
Ekegusii: Akaayerera, akaumora amaache aria areenge ase enyongo ase orotuba ime, akaminyoka bwango ase ensoko naende, agachibuuchera chingamia chiaye chionsi.

English: The man looked steadfastly at her, remaining silent, to know whether Yahweh had made his journey prosperous or not.
Kiswahili: Pasipo kusema neno, yule mtumishi akamtazama kwa makini aone kama Bwana ameifanikisha safari yake, au la.
Ekegusii: Erio omonto oria akamobeta amaiso, akaba okirete kiri, erinde amanye gose Omonene osesesenirie orogendo rwaye, gose taibo.

English: As the camels had finished drinking, the man took a golden ring of half a shekel weight, and two bracelets for her hands of ten shekels weight of gold,
Kiswahili: Ikawa ngamia walipokwisha kunywa wote, yule mtumishi akampa huyo msichana pete ya puani ya dhahabu yenye uzito wa beka moja na bangili mbili za dhahabu zenye uzito wa shekeli kumi.
Ekegusii: Ekero chingamia chiakoorire konywa amaache, omonto oria akamoruseria ekegera gi’etaabu, kiare noborito bwe chigiramu isano na isato, na ebitange bibere bie chitaabu ase amaboko aye, ebiare noborito bwe chigiramu rigana erimo, na emerongo etano.

English: and said, “Whose daughter are you? Please tell me. Is there room in your father’s house for us to stay?”
Kiswahili: Kisha akamuuliza, “Wewe ni binti wa nani? Tafadhali uniambie, je, kuna nafasi katika nyumba ya baba yako tutakapoweza kulala?”
Ekegusii: Akamobooria: “Nomoiseke o ng’o ore? Naende onteebie gose ribaga ndire mwa iso toranyare koraara botuko.”

English: She said to him, “I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor.”
Kiswahili: Yule msichana akamjibu, “Mimi ni binti wa Bethueli, mwana wa Milka aliyemzalia Nahori.”
Ekegusii: Ere akamoiraneria: “Inche nomoiseke o Betueli, oyo Milka aiborerete Nahori.”

English: She said moreover to him, “We have both straw and feed enough, and room to lodge in.”
Kiswahili: Akaendelea kusema, “Kwetu kuna majani mengi na malisho, tena kuna nafasi kwa ajili yenu kulala.”
Ekegusii: Naende akamoteebia: “Seito obonyansi mboreo, na aase tokorisia aisaine, na enyomba y’abageni bakorara nereo.”

English: The man bowed his head, and worshiped Yahweh.
Kiswahili: Yule mtumishi akasujudu na kumwabudu Bwana,
Ekegusii: Erio omonto oria agatugama inse, agasasiima Omonene,

English: He said, “Blessed be Yahweh, the God of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken his loving kindness and his truth toward my master. As for me, Yahweh has led me on the way to the house of my master’s relatives.”
Kiswahili: akisema, “Atukuzwe Bwana, Mungu wa bwana wangu Abrahamu, ambaye hakuondoa wema na uaminifu wake kwa bwana wangu. Mimi nami, Bwana ameniongoza safarini akanifikisha nyumbani kwa jamaa za bwana wangu.”
Ekegusii: agateeba: “Omonene, Nyasae bw’omonene one Aburaamu, atogigwe! Ere tatigeti koorokia omonene one obuya na obwegenwa. Omonene ondaaire enchera, naikire enka y’abamwabo omonene one.”

English: The young lady ran, and told her mother’s house about these words.
Kiswahili: Yule msichana akakimbia akawaeleza watu wa nyumbani mwa mama yake kuhusu mambo haya.
Ekegusii: Erio omoiseke oria akaminyoka, agaika inka sobo, agateebia abanto ba nyomba mwa ng’ina amang’ana ayio.

English: Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban. Laban ran out to the man, to the spring.
Kiswahili: Rebeka alikuwa na kaka aliyeitwa Labani, huyo akaharakisha kukutana na yule mtumishi kule kisimani.
Ekegusii: Rebeka nabwate momura omwabo ore korokwa Labani. Ekero Labani arooche ekegera na ebitange ase amaboko ’omoiseke omwabo, na kaigure amang’ana omonto oria ateebetie Rebeka, agasoka, akaminyoka gochia ase ensoko ase omonto oria areenge, akamorora oteneine ase chingamia chiaye,

English: When he saw the ring, and the bracelets on his sister’s hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, “This is what the man said to me,” he came to the man. Behold, he was standing by the camels at the spring.
Kiswahili: Mara alipoiona ile pete puani, na bangili mikononi mwa dada yake na kusikia yale maneno Rebeka aliyoambiwa na huyo mtumishi, alimwendea huyo mtumishi, akamkuta amesimama karibu na ngamia wake pale karibu na kisima.
Ekegusii: akamoteebia: “Inchuo, aye osesenirie n’Omonene! Naki oteneine isiko aa? Inche nakoroiseirie enyomba ase ogochia koraara, na aase e chingamia chiao.”

English: He said, “Come in, you blessed of Yahweh. Why do you stand outside? For I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.”
Kiswahili: Akamwambia, “Karibu nyumbani wewe uliyebarikiwa na Bwana, kwa nini unasimama huko nje? Mimi nimekuandalia nyumba na mahali kwa ajili ya ngamia.”
Ekegusii: Erio omonto oria agasoa nyomba, na Labani agasibora chingamia chigurube chiabo, agachia obonyansi, na chirochio chikaria. Naende akarentera omonto oria amaache, akarentera na abwo baarenge komo, bagesibia amagoro.

English: The man came into the house, and he unloaded the camels. He gave straw and feed for the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.
Kiswahili: Hivyo yule mtumishi akaenda nyumbani, mizigo ikaondolewa juu ya ngamia. Majani na malisho yakaletwa kwa ajili ya ngamia na maji kwa ajili yake na watu wake ili kunawa miguu.
Ekegusii: Erio akaariganigwa ase endagera, korende agateeba: “Tinkoria endagera, goika ndateeba amang’ana ane.” Erio Labani akairaneria: “Gaki, yakwane!”

English: Food was set before him to eat, but he said, “I will not eat until I have told my message.” Laban said, “Speak on.”
Kiswahili: Ndipo chakula kikaandaliwa kwa ajili yake, lakini akasema, “Sitakula mpaka niwe nimewaambia yale niliyo nayo ya kusema.” Labani akasema, “Basi tuambie.”
Ekegusii: Erio agateeba: “Inche nomosomba o Aburaamu.

English: He said, “I am Abraham’s servant.
Kiswahili: Hivyo akasema, “Mimi ni mtumishi wa Abrahamu.
Ekegusii: Omonene osesenirie omonene one mono, na ere obeire omotenenku. Omoeire amaicho e ching’ondi, na aye chiombe, chifeta ne chitaabu, na abasomba, abamura na abaiseke, chingamia ne chitigere.”

English: Yahweh has blessed my master greatly. He has become great. Yahweh has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male servants and female servants, and camels and donkeys.
Kiswahili: Bwana amembariki sana bwana wangu, amekuwa tajiri. Amempa kondoo na ngʼombe, fedha na dhahabu, watumishi wa kiume na wa kike, ngamia na punda.
Ekegusii: Na Sara, moka omonene one, akamoiborera omwana omomura ekero amenyire omogotu; na omonene one oeire omwana oyio bionsi ebi abwate.

English: Sarah, my master’s wife, bore a son to my master when she was old. He has given all that he has to him.
Kiswahili: Sara mkewe bwana wangu amemzalia mwana katika uzee wake, naye amempa kila kitu alichokuwa nacho.
Ekegusii: Omonene one akamboria ntiane, aganteabia: “Torigeria omwana one omokungu korwa ase abaiseke b’Abakaanani, aba imenyete ase ense yabo;

English: My master made me swear, saying, ‘You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I live,
Kiswahili: Naye bwana wangu ameniapisha na akasema, ‘Kamwe usimtwalie mwanangu mke katika binti za Wakanaani, ambao ninaishi katika nchi yao,
Ekegusii: Korende ogende ase omochie o tata, ase eamate yane, orentere omwana one omokungu korwa aroro.

English: but you shall go to my father’s house, and to my relatives, and take a wife for my son.’
Kiswahili: ila uende mpaka kwa jamaa ya baba yangu na ukoo wangu mwenyewe, ukamtwalie mwanangu mke huko.’
Ekegusii: Na inche ngateebia omonene one: Aande omokungu oria atancheraneti gocha amo nainche.

English: I asked my master, ‘What if the woman will not follow me?’
Kiswahili: “Kisha nikamuuliza bwana wangu, ‘Je, kama huyo mwanamke hatakubali kurudi nami?’
Ekegusii: Korende aganteebia: Omonene oyo ngendererete ase obosio bwaye, natome omomalaika oye amo naye, asesenie orogendo rwao. Naye orentere omwana one omokungu korwa ase eamate yane, korwa ase omochie o tata;

English: He said to me, ‘Yahweh, before whom I walk, will send his angel with you, and prosper your way. You shall take a wife for my son from my relatives, and of my father’s house.
Kiswahili: “Akanijibu, ‘Bwana ambaye nimetembea mbele zake, atatuma malaika wake pamoja nawe, na kuifanikisha safari yako, ili uweze kupata mke kwa ajili ya mwanangu katika ukoo wangu na kutoka jamaa ya baba yangu.
Ekegusii: erio nosiborwe korwa ase eira eyio nakoboririe otiane. Ekero oraike ase eamate yane, onye tibagokoa omoiseke oyio, aye rirorio nobe gwasiboirwe korwa ase ogotiana kwao.”

English: Then you will be clear from my oath, when you come to my relatives. If they don’t give her to you, you shall be clear from my oath.’
Kiswahili: Kisha, utakapokwenda kwenye ukoo wangu, utakuwa umefunguliwa kutoka kiapo changu hata kama wakikataa kukupa huyo binti, utakuwa umefunguliwa kutoka kiapo changu.’
Ekegusii: “Inche igo nacha reero ase ensoko, nasaba iga: Aye Omonene, Nyasae bw’omonene one Aburaamu, koranche onsesenie bono ase orogendo rwane nkogenda.

English: I came today to the spring, and said, ‘Yahweh, the God of my master Abraham, if now you do prosper my way which I go—
Kiswahili: “Nilipokuja kisimani leo nilisema, ‘Ee Bwana, Mungu wa bwana wangu Abrahamu, ikikupendeza, naomba uifanikishe safari niliyoijia.
Ekegusii: Rora ninteneine aiga ase ensoko y’amaache. Tiga ebe iga: Omoiseke onde omo orache kobuucha amaache, na inche imosabe oyio: Koranche ong’e amaache make korwa ase enyongo yao inywe.

English: behold, I am standing by this spring of water. Let it happen, that the maiden who comes out to draw, to whom I will say, “Please give me a little water from your pitcher to drink,”
Kiswahili: Tazama, ninasimama kando ya kisima hiki, kama mwanamwali akija kuteka maji nami nikimwambia, tafadhali niruhusu ninywe maji kidogo kutoka kwenye mtungi wako,
Ekegusii: Onye ere okong’iraneria: Ee, kanywe, na nimbuuchere chingamia chiao nachirochio; otige oyio abe nere omokungu Omonene achoreire omwana bw’omonene one.”

English: then she tells me, “Drink, and I will also draw for your camels,”—let her be the woman whom Yahweh has appointed for my master’s son.’
Kiswahili: naye kama akiniambia, “Kunywa, nami nitateka maji kwa ajili ya ngamia wako pia,” basi huyo awe ndiye mke ambaye Bwana amemchagulia mwana wa bwana wangu.’
Ekegusii: “Ritang’ani ntarakoora ogosaba ase omoyo one, narora Rebeka ogocha obegete enyongo yaye mareko, ogotirimboka gochia ase ensoko kobuucha amaache.” Na inche namosaba: “Koranche, ong’e amaache inywe.”

English: Before I had finished speaking in my heart, behold, Rebekah came out with her pitcher on her shoulder. She went down to the spring, and drew. I said to her, ‘Please let me drink.’
Kiswahili: “Kabla sijamaliza kuomba moyoni mwangu, Rebeka akatokea, amebeba mtungi begani mwake. Akashuka kisimani akateka maji, nami nikamwambia, ‘Tafadhali nipe maji ninywe.’
Ekegusii: Ere orusia enyongo yaye bwango korwa ase amareko aye, oyebeeka inse, onteebia: Kanywe, ne chingamia chiao ninchibuchere boigo. Erio ong’a, nanywa, oa ne chingamia, nachirochio chianywa.

English: She hurried and let down her pitcher from her shoulder, and said, ‘Drink, and I will also give your camels a drink.’ So I drank, and she also gave the camels a drink.
Kiswahili: “Akafanya haraka kushusha mtungi wake begani na kusema, ‘Kunywa na nitawanywesha ngamia wako pia,’ basi nikanywa, akawanywesha na ngamia pia.
Ekegusii: Erio namobooria: “Nomoiseke o ng’o ore?” Ere ong’iraneria: “Inche nomoiseke o Betueli oyo Milka aiborerete Nahori.” Agwo namobekera ekegera chimioro chiaye, na ebitange ase amaboko aye.

English: I asked her, and said, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ She said, ‘The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor’s son, whom Milcah bore to him.’ I put the ring on her nose, and the bracelets on her hands.
Kiswahili: “Nikamuuliza, ‘Wewe ni binti wa nani?’ “Akasema, ‘Mimi ni binti wa Bethueli, mwana wa Nahori, Milka aliyemzalia.’ “Ndipo nilipotia pete puani mwake na bangili mikononi mwake,
Ekegusii: Erio natugama inse nasasiima Omonene. Naende namotogia Omonene, Nyasae bw’omonene one Aburaamu, oyontang’anete ase enchera endonge, erinde imorentere omwana bw’omonene one omokungu korwa ase eamate yaye.

English: I bowed my head, and worshiped Yahweh, and blessed Yahweh, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me in the right way to take my master’s brother’s daughter for his son.
Kiswahili: nikasujudu na nikamwabudu Bwana. Nikamtukuza Bwana, Mungu wa bwana wangu Abrahamu, aliyeniongoza katika njia sahihi ili nimtwalie mwana na bwana wangu mke katika jamaa zake.
Ekegusii: Bono rende, onye morigetie gokorera Omonene one amaya, na ayare boronge, monteebie; onye taibo, monteebie, ngende ensemo ende eng’ao korigia.

English: Now if you will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me. If not, tell me, that I may turn to the right hand, or to the left.”
Kiswahili: Ikiwa mtaonyesha wema na uaminifu kwa bwana wangu, mniambie, la sivyo, mniambie, ili niweze kujua njia ya kugeukia.”
Ekegusii: Erio Labani na Betueli bakamoiraneria, bakamoteebia: “Amang’ana aya nigo arure ase Omonene; intwe titokonyara gokwana ande, amabe gose amaya.

English: Then Laban and Bethuel answered, “The thing proceeds from Yahweh. We can’t speak to you bad or good.
Kiswahili: Labani na Bethueli wakajibu, “Jambo hili limetoka kwa Bwana, hatuwezi kukuambia jambo lolote baya au jema.
Ekegusii: Rora, Rebeka oyio ore ase obosio bwao, moire, mogende komo, achie koba omokungu bw’omwana bw’omonene oo, buna Omonene konya ateebire.”

English: Behold, Rebekah is before you. Take her, and go, and let her be your master’s son’s wife, as Yahweh has spoken.”
Kiswahili: Rebeka yuko hapa, mchukue na uende, awe mke wa mwana wa bwana wako, sawasawa na Bwana alivyoongoza.”
Ekegusii: Ekero omosomba o Aburaamu aigwete amang’ana abo, agatugama inse ase obosio bw’Omonene.

English: When Abraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed himself down to the earth to Yahweh.
Kiswahili: Ikawa huyo mtumishi wa Abrahamu aliposikia waliyosema, alisujudu mpaka nchi mbele za Bwana.
Ekegusii: Erio omosomba oria akarusia ebinto bi’ogwechabera bie chitaabu, na ebie chifeta, amo ne chianga, akaa Rebeka. Naende akaa momura omwabo amo na ng’ina ebiegwa bi’erigori rinene.

English: The servant brought out jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and clothing, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave precious things to her brother and her mother.
Kiswahili: Ndipo huyo mtumishi akatoa vitu vilivyotengenezwa kwa dhahabu na kwa fedha pamoja na mavazi, akampa Rebeka, pia akawapa zawadi za thamani kubwa nduguye na mamaye.
Ekegusii: Ere na abanto baria baarenge komo bakaria na bakanywa, erio bakaraara aroro. Mambia kobwachia gokia akabateebia: “Ing’a ribaga ng’irane ase omonene one.”

English: They ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and stayed all night. They rose up in the morning, and he said, “Send me away to my master.”
Kiswahili: Kisha yeye na wale watu waliokuwa pamoja naye wakala, wakanywa na kulala palepale. Walipoamka asubuhi, yule mtumishi, akasema, “Nipeni ruhusa nirudi kwa bwana wangu.”
Ekegusii: Momura omwabo Rebeka na ng’ina bakamoteebia: “Tiga omoiseke oyo arabeere aiga koreng’ana amatuko ikomi; magega y’ayio mogende komo.”

English: Her brother and her mother said, “Let the young lady stay with us a few days, at least ten. After that she will go.”
Kiswahili: Lakini ndugu yake Rebeka pamoja na mama yake wakajibu, “Acha binti akae kwetu siku kumi au zaidi, ndipo mwondoke.”
Ekegusii: Ere akabateebia: “Timobaisa goteebania, ekiagera Omonene onsesenirie ase orogendo rwane; ing’a ribaga ngende ase omonene one.”

English: He said to them, “Don’t hinder me, since Yahweh has prospered my way. Send me away that I may go to my master.”
Kiswahili: Lakini yule mtumishi akawaambia, “Msinicheleweshe, kwa kuwa Bwana amefanikisha safari yangu, nipeni ruhusa nirudi kwa bwana wangu.”
Ekegusii: Bakamoteebia: “Tiga torangerie omoiseke, tomoboorie, toigwe buna agoteeba.”

English: They said, “We will call the young lady, and ask her.”
Kiswahili: Ndipo wakasema, “Acha tumwite huyo binti tumuulize, tusikie atakavyosema.”
Ekegusii: Bakarangeria Rebeka, bakamobooria: “Inee! Inabwanche ogende nomonto oyo?” Akairaneria: “Ee, nanchire, ngende nere.”

English: They called Rebekah, and said to her, “Will you go with this man?” She said, “I will go.”
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo wakamwita Rebeka na kumuuliza, “Je, utakwenda na mtu huyu?” Akasema, “Nitakwenda.”
Ekegusii: Erio bakaa Rebeka ribaga amo nomoreri oye bagende nomosomba o Aburaamu na abanto baye.

English: They sent away Rebekah, their sister, with her nurse, Abraham’s servant, and his men.
Kiswahili: Hivyo wakamwaga ndugu yao Rebeka aondoke, pamoja na mjakazi wake, mtumishi wa Abrahamu na watu wake.
Ekegusii: Bagasesenia Rebeka, bakamoteebia, “Oyominto, obe ng’ina abanto chilifu ne chilifu; ororeeria rwao inarobue emechie y’ababisa bao, royegambere!”

English: They blessed Rebekah, and said to her, “Our sister, may you be the mother of thousands of ten thousands, and let your offspring possess the gate of those who hate them.”
Kiswahili: Wakambariki Rebeka, wakamwambia, “Ndugu yetu, uwe wewe kumi elfu, mara elfu nyingi, nao wazao wako wamiliki malango ya adui zao.”
Ekegusii: Erio Rebeka akaimoka amo nabaiseke baye abasomba, bakariina chingamia, bagatunyana omonto oria. Naboigo omosomba oria akaira Rebeka, akagenda nere sobo.

English: Rebekah arose with her ladies. They rode on the camels, and followed the man. The servant took Rebekah, and went his way.
Kiswahili: Rebeka na vijakazi wake wakajiandaa, wakapanda ngamia zao wakafuatana na yule mtu. Hivyo yule mtumishi akamchukua Rebeka akaondoka.
Ekegusii: Bono Isaka konya orure ase ensoko ya Beeri‐Lahai‐Roi, ekiagera nigo amenyete ase ense ya Negebu.

English: Isaac came from the way of Beer Lahai Roi, for he lived in the land of the South.
Kiswahili: Basi Isaki alikuwa ametoka Beer-Lahai-Roi, kwa kuwa alikuwa anaishi nchi ya Negebu.
Ekegusii: Isaka nigo achiete mogondo ekero kia mogoroba, akaba ore nebirengererio. Agwo akaimokereria amaiso aye igoro, akarora chingamia chigocha.

English: Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the evening. He lifted up his eyes and looked. Behold, there were camels coming.
Kiswahili: Isaki akatoka kwenda shambani kutafakari wakati wa jioni, alipoinua macho yake, akaona ngamia wanakuja.
Ekegusii: Rebeka nere akaimokereria amaiso aye igoro, akarora Isaka; erio agaika bwango korwa ase engamia igoro,

English: Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she got off the camel.
Kiswahili: Rebeka pia akainua macho akamwona Isaki. Akashuka kutoka kwenye ngamia wake
Ekegusii: akabooria omosomba oria: “Monto ki oria ogotaara ase omogondo, ogocha koumerana naintwe?” Omosomba oria akamoiraneria: “Oria nere omonene one.” Erio omoiseke oria akabwata egietubo kiaye, agetuba.

English: She said to the servant, “Who is the man who is walking in the field to meet us?” The servant said, “It is my master.” She took her veil, and covered herself.
Kiswahili: na akamuuliza yule mtumishi, “Ni nani mtu yule aliye kule shambani anayekuja kutulaki?” Yule mtumishi akajibu, “Huyu ndiye bwana wangu.” Hivyo Rebeka akachukua shela yake akajifunika.
Ekegusii: Na omosomba oria agateebia Isaka amang’ana onsi, buna akorete.

English: The servant told Isaac all the things that he had done.
Kiswahili: Kisha yule mtumishi akamweleza Isaki mambo yote aliyoyatenda.
Ekegusii: Isaka agasoyia Rebeka ase eema ya ng’ina ime, akaba omonywomire, naende akaba omwanchete. Ase ogi, Isaka akaremigwa korwa ase omoichano bw’ogokwa kwa ng’ina.

English: Abraham took another wife, and her name was Keturah.
Kiswahili: Abrahamu alioa mke mwingine, ambaye jina lake aliitwa Ketura.
Ekegusii: Aburaamu akanyuoma omokungu onde, ore korokwa Ketura.

English: She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
Kiswahili: Huyu alimzalia Zimrani, Yokshani, Medani, Midiani, Ishbaki na Shua.
Ekegusii: Nere akamoiborera Simurani, na Yokisani, na Medani, na Midiani, na Isibaki, na Sua.

English: Jokshan became the father of Sheba, and Dedan. The sons of Dedan were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
Kiswahili: Yokshani alikuwa baba wa Sheba na Dedani, wazao wa Dedani walikuwa Waashuri, Waletushi na Waleumi.
Ekegusii: Yokisani akaibora Seba na Dedani. Na basinto ba Dedani nabwo aba: Ashurimu, na Letusi, na Leumi.

English: The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah.
Kiswahili: Wana wa Midiani walikuwa Efa, Eferi, Hanoki, Abida na Eldaa. Hawa wote walikuwa uzao wa Ketura.
Ekegusii: Basinto ba Midiani nabwo aba: Efa, na Eferi, na Hanoki, na Abida, na Elidaa. Abwo bonsi nabwo baarenge abana ba Ketura.

English: Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac,
Kiswahili: Abrahamu akamwachia Isaki kila kitu alichokuwa nacho.
Ekegusii: Aburaamu akaa Isaka ebinto bionsi ebi abwate.

English: but Abraham gave gifts to the sons of Abraham’s concubines. While he still lived, he sent them away from Isaac his son, eastward, to the east country.
Kiswahili: Lakini Abrahamu alipokuwa bado hai, akawapa watoto wa masuria wake zawadi, kisha akawaondoa waende kuishi pande za mashariki mbali na mwanawe Isaki.
Ekegusii: Korende abana b’abakuungu baria ba sere‐sere Aburaamu akabaa ebiegwa. Ekero are moyo, konya atarakwa, akabateebia barue ase omwana oye Isaka, bagende gochia moocha, ase ense ya Moocha.

English: These are the days of the years of Abraham’s life which he lived: one hundred seventy-five years.
Kiswahili: Kwa jumla, Abrahamu aliishi miaka 175.
Ekegusii: Aburaamu nigo amenyete emiaka rigana erimo, na emerongo etano na ebere, na etano (175), ase obogima bwaye.

English: Abraham gave up his spirit, and died at a good old age, an old man, and full of years, and was gathered to his people.
Kiswahili: Ndipo Abrahamu akapumua pumzi ya mwisho na akafa akiwa mwenye umri mzuri, mzee aliyeshiba siku, naye akakusanywa pamoja na watu wake.
Ekegusii: Nigo asogetie omoyo ase obogotu n’obuya, ore omogaka, oisanekire nemiaka emenge; agasangerekana amo nabaanto baye.

English: Isaac and Ishmael, his sons, buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron, the son of Zohar the Hittite, which is near Mamre,
Kiswahili: Watoto wake Isaki na Ishmaeli wakamzika katika pango la Makpela karibu na Mamre, katika shamba lililokuwa la Efroni mwana wa Sohari Mhiti,
Ekegusii: Isaka na Isumaeli bakamotindeka ase rikuruma agwo Makipela ase oboremo bwa Efuroni, omwana o Sohari, Omohiti, moocha ya Mamure,

English: the field which Abraham purchased from the children of Heth. Abraham was buried there with Sarah, his wife.
Kiswahili: Shamba ambalo Abrahamu alilinunua kwa Wahiti. Hapo ndipo Abrahamu alipozikwa pamoja na mkewe Sara.
Ekegusii: ase oboremo boria Aburaamu agorete korwa ase Abahiti. Agwo nao Aburaamu atindegetwe ase Sara mokaye nere atindegetwe.

English: After the death of Abraham, God blessed Isaac, his son. Isaac lived by Beer Lahai Roi.
Kiswahili: Baada ya kifo cha Abrahamu, Mungu akambariki mwanawe Isaki, ambaye baadaye aliishi karibu na Beer-Lahai-Roi.
Ekegusii: Magega y’ogokwa kwa Aburaamu, Nyasae agasesenia Isaka, omwana oye. Na Isaka akamenya ang’e nensoko yaare korokwa Beeri‐Lahai‐Roi.

English: Now this is the history of the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s servant, bore to Abraham.
Kiswahili: Hivi ndivyo vizazi vya Ishmaeli mtoto wa Abrahamu, ambaye mjakazi wake Sara, Hagari Mmisri, alimzalia Abrahamu.
Ekegusii: Oro narwo ororeeria rwa Isumaeli, omwana o Aburaamu, oyo Hagari, omosomba o Sara, amoiborerete.

English: These are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to the order of their birth: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
Kiswahili: Haya ndiyo majina ya wana wa Ishmaeli, yaliyoorodheshwa kulingana na jinsi walivyozaliwa: Mzaliwa wa kwanza wa Ishmaeli ni Nebayothi, akafuatia Kedari, Adbeeli, Mibsamu,
Ekegusii: Aya naro amarieta ’abana ba Isumaeli, ase omooroberio bw’okoiborwa kwabo: Nebayoti, nere omwana oye omotangi, na Kedari, na Adibeeli, na Mibusamu,

English: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
Kiswahili: Mishma, Duma, Masa,
Ekegusii: na Misima, na Duma, na Masa,

English: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
Kiswahili: Hadadi, Tema, Yeturi, Nafishi na Kedema.
Ekegusii: na Hadadi, na Tema, na Yeturi, na Nafisi, na Kedema.

English: These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their villages, and by their encampments: twelve princes, according to their nations.
Kiswahili: Hawa walikuwa wana wa Ishmaeli na haya ni majina ya viongozi wa makabila kumi na mawili kulingana na makao yao na kambi zao.
Ekegusii: Aba nabwo abana ba Isumaeli, na aya naro amarieta abo ase emechie yabo na ebitwori biabo, na barabwo nigo baarenge abagaambi ikomi na babere, ase ebisaku biabo.

English: These are the years of the life of Ishmael: one hundred thirty-seven years. He gave up his spirit and died, and was gathered to his people.
Kiswahili: Kwa jumla Ishmaeli aliishi miaka 137. Akapumua pumzi ya mwisho, akafa, naye akakusanywa pamoja na watu wake.
Ekegusii: Isumaeli nigo aigetie emiaka rigana erimo, na emerongo etato, na etano na ebere (137), erio erio agakwa; agasangererekana amo nabaanto baye.

English: They lived from Havilah to Shur that is before Egypt, as you go toward Assyria. He lived opposite all his relatives.
Kiswahili: Wazao wa Ishmaeli waliishi kuanzia nchi ya Havila hadi Shuri, karibu na mpaka wa Misri, unapoelekea Ashuru. Hao waliishi kwa uhasama na ndugu zao wote.
Ekegusii: Abana ba Isumaeli nigo baamenyete bagachaakera Havila, bagaika Suri moocha ya Misiri, ase enchera ekogenda Asuri; bakamenya babebekaine n’abamwabo bonsi.

English: This is the history of the generations of Isaac, Abraham’s son. Abraham became the father of Isaac.
Kiswahili: Hivi ndivyo vizazi vya Isaki mwana wa Abrahamu. Abrahamu akamzaa Isaki,
Ekegusii: Oro narwo ororeeria rwa Isaka, mosinto o Aburaamu. Aburaamu nere oiborete Isaka.

English: Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Paddan Aram, the sister of Laban the Syrian, to be his wife.
Kiswahili: Isaki alikuwa na umri wa miaka arobaini alipomwoa Rebeka binti Bethueli Mwaramu kutoka Padan-Aramu, nduguye Labani Mwaramu.
Ekegusii: Isaka nigo areenge nemiaka emerongo ene ekero anyuomete Rebeka, omoiseke o Betueli, Omoaramu o Padan‐Aramu, omoiseke omwabo Labani, Omoaramu.

English: Isaac entreated Yahweh for his wife, because she was barren. Yahweh was entreated by him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
Kiswahili: Isaki akamwomba Bwana kwa ajili ya mke wake, kwa sababu alikuwa tasa. Bwana akajibu maombi yake na Rebeka mkewe akapata mimba.
Ekegusii: Isaka agasabera mokaye ase Omonene, ekiagera nigo areenge omogomba. Omonene akaigwa ogosaba kwaye, na Rebeka mokaye akaba morito.

English: The children struggled together within her. She said, “If it is like this, why do I live?” She went to inquire of Yahweh.
Kiswahili: Watoto wakashindana tumboni mwake, akasema, “Kwa nini haya yanatokea kwangu?” Kwa hiyo akaenda kumuuliza Bwana.
Ekegusii: Abana bakaba bakomigana enda yaye ime. Ere akabora: “Onye nabo iga, okoba moyo kwane ninki korangwenere?” Akagenda koboori’Omonene.

English: Yahweh said to her, “Two nations are in your womb. Two peoples will be separated from your body. The one people will be stronger than the other people. The elder will serve the younger.”
Kiswahili: Bwana akamjibu, “Mataifa mawili yamo tumboni mwako, na mataifa hayo mawili kutoka ndani yako watatenganishwa. Mmoja atakuwa na nguvu zaidi kuliko mwingine, na yule mkubwa atamtumikia yule mdogo.”
Ekegusii: Omonene akamoiraneria, “Ebisaku bibere mbire enda yao ime, abanto babere orache koibora, na barabwo mbaatananekane korwa okoiborwa kwabo; oyomo nabe ne chinguru kobua oria onde, oria omonene omosomba bw’oria omoke.”

English: When her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb.
Kiswahili: Wakati wake wa kujifungua ulipotimia, walikuwepo mapacha wa kiume tumboni mwake.
Ekegusii: Ekero amatuko aye ay’okoibora achia goikerana, bakanyora ne chibarongo chiare enda yaye ime.

English: The first came out red all over, like a hairy garment. They named him Esau.
Kiswahili: Wa kwanza kuzaliwa alikuwa mwekundu, mwili wake wote ulikuwa kama mtu aliyevaa vazi lenye nywele; wakamwita jina lake Esau.
Ekegusii: Oyo bw’eritang’ani agasooka, ere nigo areenge omobariri, omobere bwonsi nigo orenge namarionya; bakamoroka Esau.

English: After that, his brother came out, and his hand had hold on Esau’s heel. He was named Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them.
Kiswahili: Baadaye, ndugu yake akatoka, mkono wake ukiwa umemshika Esau kisigino; akaitwa jina lake Yakobo. Isaki alikuwa mwenye miaka sitini Rebeka alipowazaa.
Ekegusii: Magega yaye oyomwabo agasooka, okoboko kwaye kobwatete egetingiro gia Esau na ere bakamoroka Yakobo. Isaka nigo areenge nemiaka emerongo etano nomo (60), ekero mokaye abaiborete.

English: The boys grew. Esau was a skillful hunter, a man of the field. Jacob was a quiet man, living in tents.
Kiswahili: Watoto wakakua, naye Esau akakuwa mwindaji hodari, mtu wa mbugani, wakati Yakobo alikuwa mtu mtulivu, mwenye kukaa nyumbani.
Ekegusii: Ekero abana abwo bakinire, Esau akaba omotwari bwe ching’iti, korende Yakobo nigo areenge omonto omotoereru, ore kobeera ase chiema.

English: Now Isaac loved Esau, because he ate his venison. Rebekah loved Jacob.
Kiswahili: Isaki, ambaye alikuwa anapendelea zaidi nyama za porini, alimpenda Esau, bali Rebeka alimpenda Yakobo.
Ekegusii: Isaka nigo amwanchete Esau, ekiagera areenge komorentera chinyama chi’obotwari bwaye; korende Rebeka nigo amwanchete Yakobo.

English: Jacob boiled stew. Esau came in from the field, and he was famished.
Kiswahili: Siku moja Yakobo alipika mchuzi wa dengu, Esau akarudi kutoka porini akiwa na njaa kali.
Ekegusii: Rituko erimo Yakobo naiyegete omosori gete. Esau agacha korwa orosana, konya orosire mono, ogoyire ase engencho y’enchara.

English: Esau said to Jacob, “Please feed me with some of that red stew, for I am famished.” Therefore his name was called Edom.
Kiswahili: Esau akamwambia Yakobo, “Haraka, nipe huo mchuzi mwekundu! Nina njaa kali sana!” (Hii ndiyo sababu pia aliitwa Edomu.)
Ekegusii: Na Esau agasaba Yakobo: “Koranche, ong’e omosori oyio omobariri inywe, ekiagera n akuure enchara.” Ase ayio bakamoroka Edomu (engencho yaye, omobariri).

English: Jacob said, “First, sell me your birthright.”
Kiswahili: Yakobo akamjibu, “Niuzie kwanza haki yako ya mzaliwa wa kwanza.”
Ekegusii: Yakobo akamoiraneria: “Ritang’ani ng’oonerie omwando oo bw’okoiborwa kw’obotangi.”

English: Esau said, “Behold, I am about to die. What good is the birthright to me?”
Kiswahili: Esau akasema, “Tazama, mimi niko karibu ya kufa, itanifaa nini haki ya mzaliwa wa kwanza?”
Ekegusii: Esau agateeba: “Rora, inche nigo inde ang’e gokwa, omwando oyo bw’okoiborwa kw’obotangi inki orankonye?”

English: Jacob said, “Swear to me first.” He swore to him. He sold his birthright to Jacob.
Kiswahili: Yakobo akamwambia, “Niapie kwanza.” Hivyo Esau akamwapia, akamuuzia Yakobo haki yake ya kuzaliwa.
Ekegusii: Yakobo akamoteebia: “Karatiana ritang’ani ase ’nde.” Esau agatiana, erio akaooneria Yakobo omwando oye bw’okoiborwa kw’obotangi.

English: Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew. He ate and drank, rose up, and went his way. So Esau despised his birthright.
Kiswahili: Ndipo Yakobo akampa Esau mkate na ule mchuzi wa dengu. Akala na kunywa, kisha akainuka akaenda zake. Kwa hiyo Esau alidharau haki yake ya mzaliwa wa kwanza.
Ekegusii: Erio Yakobo akaa Esau omogati na omosori bwe ching’ende, na ere akaria na konywa; erio akaimoka akagenda. Naboigo Esau achayete omwando oye bw’okoiborwa kw’obotangi.

English: There was a famine in the land, in addition to the first famine that was in the days of Abraham. Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.
Kiswahili: Basi njaa kubwa ikawa katika nchi hiyo, kuliko ile njaa iliyotangulia iliyotokea wakati wa Abrahamu. Isaki akamwendea Abimeleki mfalme wa Wafilisti huko Gerari.
Ekegusii: Bono enchara yachete ase ense eria, nenchara y’ogokumia, tari eria yachete ritang’ani ase engaki ya Aburaamu. Erio Isaka agachiera Abimeleki, omorwoti bw’Abafilisti, aria Gerari.

English: Yahweh appeared to him, and said, “Don’t go down into Egypt. Live in the land I will tell you about.
Kiswahili: Bwana akamtokea Isaki, akamwambia, “Usiende Misri, bali ukae katika nchi nitakayokuambia.
Ekegusii: Na Omonene akaorokera Isaka, akamoteebia: “Totirimboka gochia Misiri, korende omenye ase ense eye ndakworokererie.

English: Live in this land, and I will be with you, and will bless you. For I will give to you, and to your offspring, all these lands, and I will establish the oath which I swore to Abraham your father.
Kiswahili: Kaa katika nchi hii kwa kitambo, mimi nitakuwa pamoja na wewe na nitakubariki. Kwa maana nitakupa wewe na uzao wako nchi hizi zote na nitatimiza kiapo nilichomwapia Abrahamu baba yako.
Ekegusii: Obe buna omomenyi ase ense eye, na inche nimbe amo naye, ningosesenie; naki ninkoe aye na ororeeria rwao chinse echi chionsi, na ning’ikeranie eira yane eyio natianete ase Aburaamu iso.

English: I will multiply your offspring as the stars of the sky, and will give all these lands to your offspring. In your offspring all the nations of the earth will be blessed,
Kiswahili: Nitafanya wazao wako kuwa wengi kama nyota za angani, nami nitawapa nchi hizi zote na kutokana na uzao wako mataifa yote yatabarikiwa,
Ekegusii: Nimente ororeeria rwao robe oronge buna ching’enang’eni chia igoro; ne chinse echi chionsi ninchiee ororeeria rwao; na ase ororeeria rwao ebisaku bionsi bi’ense inabisesenigwe,

English: because Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my requirements, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.”
Kiswahili: kwa sababu Abrahamu alinitii mimi akatunza kanuni zangu na maagizo yangu, amri zangu pamoja na sheria zangu.”
Ekegusii: ekiagera Aburaamu naigwerete amang’ana aane, akabwata aya namochiigete, na amachiiko aane, na aya narigete, amo nogoteebereria kwane.”

English: Isaac lived in Gerar.
Kiswahili: Hivyo Isaki akaishi huko Gerari.
Ekegusii: Ase igo, Isaka akamenya Gerari.

English: The men of the place asked him about his wife. He said, “She is my sister,” for he was afraid to say, “My wife”, lest, he thought, “the men of the place might kill me for Rebekah, because she is beautiful to look at.”
Kiswahili: Watu wa mahali pale walipomuuliza habari za mke wake, akasema, “Huyu ni dada yangu,” kwa sababu aliogopa kusema, “Huyu ni mke wangu.” Alifikiri, “Watu wa mahali pale wataweza kumuua kwa sababu ya Rebeka, kwa kuwa alikuwa mzuri wa sura.”
Ekegusii: Ekero abanto b’aase aria baamoboretie amang’ana igoro ya mokaye, akabateebia: “Oyo ’mosubati ominto.” Naki nigo oboete goteeba ng’a ere ’mokaye, akarengereria ng’a abanto b’aase aria mbaabaise komoita ase engencho ya Rebeka, ekiagera ere areenge omonyakieni.

English: When he had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window, and saw, and, behold, Isaac was caressing Rebekah, his wife.
Kiswahili: Wakati Isaki alipokuwa amekaa huko siku nyingi, Abimeleki mfalme wa Wafilisti akachungulia dirishani, akaona jinsi Isaki alivyomkumbatia Rebeka mke wake.
Ekegusii: Ekero konya bamenyire aria engaki entambe, Abimeleki, omorwoti bw’Abafilisti, akarigereria korwa ase ekebao, akarora Isaka bakogosoria na Rebeka mokaye.

English: Abimelech called Isaac, and said, “Behold, surely she is your wife. Why did you say, ‘She is my sister’?” Isaac said to him, “Because I said, ‘Lest I die because of her.’”
Kiswahili: Abimeleki akamwita Isaki akamwambia, “Hakika huyu ni mke wako! Mbona uliniambia, ‘Huyu ni dada yangu?’ ” Isaki akamjibu, “Kwa sababu nilifikiri ningeweza kuuawa kwa sababu yake.”
Ekegusii: Erio Abimeleki akarangeria Isaka, akamobooria: “Amaene, oyo ’mokao? Naki gwakora ogateeba ng’a oyo mosubati omino?” Isaka akamoiraneria: “Nigo nareengereretie ng’a, aande nimbaise goitwa ase engencho yaye.”

English: Abimelech said, “What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt on us!”
Kiswahili: Ndipo Abimeleki akamjibu, “Ni nini hiki ulichotufanyia? Ingewezekana mtu yeyote akawa amekutana kimwili na mke wako, nawe ungeleta hatia juu yetu.”
Ekegusii: Abimeleki akamobooria: “Inki eke gwatokoreire iga? Aande monto onde oito areenge gochia araare na mokao, na aye anga nigo gwatobeka ase okomocha.”

English: Abimelech commanded all the people, saying, “He who touches this man or his wife will surely be put to death.”
Kiswahili: Hivyo Abimeleki akatoa amri kwa watu wote, akisema, “Yeyote atakayemnyanyasa mtu huyu au mkewe hakika atauawa.”
Ekegusii: Ase ayio Abimeleki agatianera abanto bonsi, akabateebia: “Monto onde bwensi aise gokuna omonto oyo ore aa, gose mokaye, goika aitwe.”

English: Isaac sowed in that land, and reaped in the same year one hundred times what he planted. Yahweh blessed him.
Kiswahili: Isaki akapanda mazao katika nchi hiyo, kwa mwaka huo huo, akavuna mara mia, kwa sababu Bwana alimbariki.
Ekegusii: Isaka agasimeka endagera ase ense eria, akagesa ase omwaka oyio ara rigana, n’Omonene akamosesenia.

English: The man grew great, and grew more and more until he became very great.
Kiswahili: Isaki akawa tajiri, mali zake zikaendelea kuongezeka mpaka akawa tajiri sana.
Ekegusii: Omonto oyio akaba ne chinguru, akagenderera komenteka gokina, goika akaba nokobua okonene.

English: He had possessions of flocks, possessions of herds, and a great household. The Philistines envied him.
Kiswahili: Akawa na mifugo ya kondoo na ngʼombe, na watumishi wengi sana, kiasi kwamba Wafilisti wakamwonea wivu.
Ekegusii: Nigo abeete nenibo y’amaicho e ching’ondi ne chiombe, na abasomba abange. Ase igo, Abafirisiti bakamororera ribero.

English: Now all the wells which his father’s servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines had stopped, and filled with earth.
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo visima vyote vilivyochimbwa na watumishi wakati wa Abrahamu baba yake, Wafilisti wakavifukia, wakavijaza udongo.
Ekegusii: (Ne chinsoko chiria chionsi abasomba ba Aburaamu ise Isaka baremete, Abafirisiti konya bachitichire namaroba.)

English: Abimelech said to Isaac, “Go away from us, for you are much mightier than we.”
Kiswahili: Ndipo Abimeleki akamwambia Isaki, “Ondoka kwetu, kwa maana umetuzidi nguvu sana.”
Ekegusii: Erio Abimeleki agateebia Isaka: “Karue ase tore, ekiagera aye kwamenyire ne chinguru chinyinge gotobua.”

English: Isaac departed from there, encamped in the valley of Gerar, and lived there.
Kiswahili: Basi Isaki akatoka huko akajenga kambi katika Bonde la Gerari, akaishi huko.
Ekegusii: Ase igo, Isaka akang’anya korwa aroro, agatoora ase ense eraire ya Gerari, akamenya aroro.

English: Isaac dug again the wells of water, which they had dug in the days of Abraham his father, for the Philistines had stopped them after the death of Abraham. He called their names after the names by which his father had called them.
Kiswahili: Ndipo Isaki akavichimbua tena vile visima vya maji ambavyo vilichimbwa siku zile za Abrahamu baba yake, ambavyo Wafilisti walivifukia baada ya kufa Abrahamu, akavipa majina yale yale ambayo baba yake alikuwa amevipa.
Ekegusii: Isaka akarubora chinsoko chiria naende, echio chiaremetwe ase engaki ya Aburaamu ise, ekiagera Abafirisiti konya bachitichire magega Aburaamu g akuure. Isaka agachiroka buna ise achirogete ritang’ani.

English: Isaac’s servants dug in the valley, and found there a well of flowing water.
Kiswahili: Watumishi wa Isaki wakachimba katika lile bonde wakagundua huko kisima chenye maji safi.
Ekegusii: Abasomba ba Isaka bakarema agwo ase ense eraire, bakanyora entuboka y’amaache.

English: The herdsmen of Gerar argued with Isaac’s herdsmen, saying, “The water is ours.” So he called the name of the well Esek, because they contended with him.
Kiswahili: Lakini wachungaji wa Gerari wakagombana na wachungaji wa Isaki wakisema, “Maji haya ni yetu!” Ndipo akakiita kile kisima Eseki, kwa sababu waligombana naye.
Ekegusii: Abarisia b’ensemo ya Gerari bakaba bakwomana nabarisia ba Isaka, bagoteeba: “Amache aya nayaito.” Ase igo, Isaka Akayeroka entuboka eria Eseki, ekiagera bamwomaneretie aroro.

English: They dug another well, and they argued over that, also. So he called its name Sitnah.
Kiswahili: Kisha wakachimba kisima kingine, lakini hata hicho pia wakakigombania, akakiita Sitna.
Ekegusii: Naende bakarema, bakanyora entuboka ende, nero bakayiomanera. Ase igo, akayeroka Sitina.

English: He left that place, and dug another well. They didn’t argue over that one. So he called it Rehoboth. He said, “For now Yahweh has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.”
Kiswahili: Akaondoka huko, akachimba kisima kingine, wala hakuna yeyote aliyekigombania. Akakiita Rehobothi, akisema, “Sasa Bwana ametufanyia nafasi, nasi tutastawi katika nchi.”
Ekegusii: Akaimoka korwa agwo, akagenda akarema akanyora entuboka ende; eyio ero tibayiomanera. Ase ayio akayeroka Rehoboti, akabora: “Naki Omonene otoeire ense engare, na toragenderere komenteka ase ense eye.”

English: He went up from there to Beersheba.
Kiswahili: Kutoka pale akaenda Beer-Sheba.
Ekegusii: Isaka akarua aroro, agatiira gochia Beeri‐Seba.

English: Yahweh appeared to him the same night, and said, “I am the God of Abraham your father. Don’t be afraid, for I am with you, and will bless you, and multiply your offspring for my servant Abraham’s sake.”
Kiswahili: Usiku ule Bwana akamtokea, akamwambia, “Mimi ndimi Mungu wa Abrahamu baba yako. Usiogope, kwa maana mimi niko pamoja nawe, nitakubariki na kuongeza idadi ya wazao wako kwa ajili ya Abrahamu mtumishi wangu.”
Ekegusii: Ase obotuko obwo obw’Omonene akamoorokera, akamoteebia: “Inche ninche Nyasae o Aburaamu iso, tibwoboa, ekiagera nigo inde amo naye, ningosesenie aye amo na ororeeria rwao, ase engencho y’omosomba one Aburaamu.”

English: He built an altar there, and called on Yahweh’s name, and pitched his tent there. There Isaac’s servants dug a well.
Kiswahili: Isaki akajenga madhabahu huko, akaliitia jina la Bwana. Akapiga hema lake huko, nao watumishi wake wakachimba kisima.
Ekegusii: Na Isaka akaagacha egesasiimero aroro, akarangeria erieta ri’Omonene, agatenenia chiema chiaye aroro. Na agwo abasomba baye bakarema, bakanyora entuboka.

English: Then Abimelech went to him from Gerar with Ahuzzath his friend, and Phicol the captain of his army.
Kiswahili: Wakati huo, Abimeleki alikuwa amemjia kutoka Gerari, akifuatana na Ahuzathi mshauri wake, pamoja na Fikoli jemadari wa majeshi yake.
Ekegusii: Erio Abimeleki akarwa Gerari, amo n’Ahusati, omosemia oye ase obogaambi, na Pikoli, oria omochiki omonene bw’abarwani baye, bagachiera Isaka.

English: Isaac said to them, “Why have you come to me, since you hate me, and have sent me away from you?”
Kiswahili: Isaki akawauliza, “Mbona mmekuja kwangu na ninyi mlinichukia na kunifukuza?”
Ekegusii: Na Isaka akababooria: “Inki mwacha korigia aa bwone, na ekero nare nainwe nigo mongechete, naende mwanseretie korwa seino?”

English: They said, “We saw plainly that Yahweh was with you. We said, ‘Let there now be an oath between us, even between us and you, and let’s make a covenant with you,
Kiswahili: Wakamjibu, “Tuliona wazi kuwa Bwana alikuwa pamoja nawe, kwa hiyo tukasema, ‘Inabidi kuwe na kiapo cha mapatano kati yetu, kati yetu na wewe. Na tufanye mkataba pamoja nawe
Ekegusii: Bakamoiraneria: “Amaene, twarorire maiso marore ng’a Omonene nigo are amo naye. Na nigo torengereretie ng’a totiananie na tokore okobwatana naye ng’a,

English: that you will do us no harm, as we have not touched you, and as we have done to you nothing but good, and have sent you away in peace.’ You are now the blessed of Yahweh.”
Kiswahili: kwamba hutatudhuru, kama jinsi nasi hatukuwanyanyasa bali tuliwatendea mema wakati wote na kuwaondoa kwetu kwa amani. Tena sasa umebarikiwa na Bwana.’ ”
Ekegusii: bono togotokorera bobe bonde, buna intwe totagokunete, gose totagokorerete bobe, otatiga amaya oka; tokagotiga okagenda bwoo nomorembe. Naye bono nomosesenigwa Omonene.”

English: He made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
Kiswahili: Basi Isaki akawaandalia karamu, nao wakala na kunywa.
Ekegusii: Erio Isaka akabakorera omoyega, bakaria na bakanywa.

English: They rose up some time in the morning, and swore an oath to one another. Isaac sent them away, and they departed from him in peace.
Kiswahili: Kesho yake asubuhi na mapema, wakaapizana wao kwa wao. Kisha Isaki akawaruhusu waende zao, wakamwacha Isaki kwa amani.
Ekegusii: Bakaimoka mambia chuni, bagatianania barabwo ase barabwo; na Isaka akabakooba, na barabwo bakarua asare, bakagenda nomorembe.

English: The same day, Isaac’s servants came, and told him concerning the well which they had dug, and said to him, “We have found water.”
Kiswahili: Siku hiyo watumishi wa Isaki wakaja wakampa habari kuhusu kisima walichokuwa wamekichimba, wakamwambia, “Tumepata maji!”
Ekegusii: Ase rituko riria riria abasomba ba Isaka bagaacha, bakamorentera amang’ana igoro y’entuboka eria banyorete, bakamoteebia: “Twanyorire amaache.”

English: He called it “Shibah”. Therefore the name of the city is “Beersheba” to this day.
Kiswahili: Naye akakiita Shiba, mpaka leo mji huo unaitwa Beer-Sheba.
Ekegusii: Ere akayeroka Seba; na ase engencho eyio omochie oyio nigo okorokwa Beeri‐Seba goika reero iga.

English: When Esau was forty years old, he took as wife Judith, the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath, the daughter of Elon the Hittite.
Kiswahili: Esau alipokuwa na umri wa miaka arobaini, akamwoa Yudithi binti Beeri Mhiti, kisha akamwoa Basemathi binti Eloni Mhiti.
Ekegusii: Ekero Esau gaika nemiaka emerongo ene akanyuoma Yuditi, omoiseke o Beeri, Omohiti, na Basemati, omoiseke o Eloni, nere n’Omohiti.

English: They grieved Isaac’s and Rebekah’s spirits.
Kiswahili: Hawa walikuwa chanzo cha huzuni ya Isaki na Rebeka.
Ekegusii: Barabwo babere bagakora obogima bwa Isaka na Rebeka koba nobororo obonge.

English: When Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, he called Esau his elder son, and said to him, “My son?” He said to him, “Here I am.”
Kiswahili: Isaki alipokuwa mzee na macho yake yalipokuwa yamekosa nguvu asiweze kuona tena, akamwita Esau mwanawe mkubwa, akamwambia, “Mwanangu.” Akajibu, “Mimi hapa.”
Ekegusii: Ekero Isaka konya abeire omogotu, nonya na amaiso aye konya amerire orotutu, atari korora buya, akarangeria Esau, omwana oye omotangi, akamoteebia: “Omwana one!” Ere agaitaba: “Nao inde aa Tata.”

English: He said, “See now, I am old. I don’t know the day of my death.
Kiswahili: Isaki akasema, “Mimi sasa ni mzee na sijui siku ya kifo changu.
Ekegusii: Akamoteebia: “Rora bono inche nagotire, gose timanyeti engaki y’ogokwa kwane.

English: Now therefore, please take your weapons, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field, and get me venison.
Kiswahili: Sasa basi, chukua silaha zako, podo na upinde, uende nyikani, ukawinde nyama pori kwa ajili yangu.
Ekegusii: Bono bogoria obota n’echinsara chiao, ogende borabu otware ching’iti, ondetere chinyama.

English: Make me savory food, such as I love, and bring it to me, that I may eat, and that my soul may bless you before I die.”
Kiswahili: Uniandalie aina ya chakula kitamu nikipendacho uniletee nile, ili niweze kukubariki kabla sijafa.”
Ekegusii: Erio ondoiserie endagera engiya, eria nyanchete, oyendetere indie, erinde ngosesenie konde moyo, ntarakwa.”

English: Rebekah heard when Isaac spoke to Esau his son. Esau went to the field to hunt for venison, and to bring it.
Kiswahili: Basi Rebeka alikuwa akisikiliza Isaki alipokuwa akizungumza na mwanawe Esau. Esau alipoondoka kwenda nyikani kuwinda nyama pori na kuleta,
Ekegusii: Ko bono, ekero Isaka are gokwana nomwana oye Esau, Rebeka nigo ategererete bobisi. Ase igo, ekero Esau agendete borabu gotwara ching’iti amorentere ise,

English: Rebekah spoke to Jacob her son, saying, “Behold, I heard your father speak to Esau your brother, saying,
Kiswahili: Rebeka akamwambia Yakobo mwanawe, “Tazama, nimemsikia baba yako akimwambia ndugu yako Esau,
Ekegusii: Rebeka agateebia Yakobo, omwana oye: “Naigure iso ogoteebia momura omino Esau:

English: ‘Bring me venison, and make me savory food, that I may eat, and bless you before Yahweh before my death.’
Kiswahili: ‘Niletee mawindo, kisha ukaniandalie chakula kitamu nile, ili niweze kukubariki mbele za Bwana kabla sijafa.’
Ekegusii: Ndetere chinyama chia borabu, ondoiserie endagera engiya indie, erio inyare kogosesenia ase obosio bw’Omonene, konde moyo, ntarakwa.

English: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice according to that which I command you.
Kiswahili: Sasa, mwanangu, nisikilize kwa makini na ufanye yale ninayokuambia:
Ekegusii: Ase igo, omwana one, ntegerera bono aya nkogoteebia.

English: Go now to the flock and get me two good young goats from there. I will make them savory food for your father, such as he loves.
Kiswahili: Nenda sasa katika kundi ukaniletee wana-mbuzi wawili wazuri, ili niandalie chakula kitamu kwa ajili ya baba yako, kama vile anavyopenda.
Ekegusii: Genda getii ase riicho, ondetere chimanwa chie chimbori ibere chingiya, na inche nimoroiserie iso endagera engiya, eria anchete.

English: You shall bring it to your father, that he may eat, so that he may bless you before his death.”
Kiswahili: Kisha umpelekee baba yako ale, ili apate kukubariki kabla hajafa.”
Ekegusii: Erio omoirere iso arie, erinde anyare kogosesenia ritang’ani atarakwa.”

English: Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, “Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.
Kiswahili: Yakobo akamwambia Rebeka mama yake, “Lakini ndugu yangu Esau ana nywele mwilini, mimi nina ngozi nyororo.
Ekegusii: Korende Yakobo agateebia Rebeka ng’ina; “Norooche Esau ominto nomonto omerete amarionya ase omobere oye, korende inche omobere one nigo ore omoterere.

English: What if my father touches me? I will seem to him as a deceiver, and I would bring a curse on myself, and not a blessing.”
Kiswahili: Itakuwaje kama baba yangu akinigusa? Itaonekana kwake kama niliyemfanyia ujanja na kuleta laana juu yangu badala ya baraka.”
Ekegusii: Aande, Tata nigo arantaba‐tabe, na inche imbe ase amaiso aye buna omong’ainereria, inyerentere okoragererigwa ribaga ri’ogosesenigwa.”

English: His mother said to him, “Let your curse be on me, my son. Only obey my voice, and go get them for me.”
Kiswahili: Mama yake akamwambia, “Mwanangu, laana na iwe juu yangu. Fanya tu ninalokuambia, nenda ukaniletee hao wana-mbuzi.”
Ekegusii: Ng’ina akamoteebia: “Okoragererigwa kwao tiga kobe igoro yane; igwa aya nkogoteebia rimo rioka, genda ondetere chimanwa echio chie chimbori.”

English: He went, and got them, and brought them to his mother. His mother made savory food, such as his father loved.
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo alikwenda akawaleta, akampa mama yake, akaandaa chakula kitamu, kama vile alivyopenda baba yake.
Ekegusii: Erio agwo akagenda, akarentera ng’ina chimanwa echio, na ere akaroisia endagera engiya, eria ise anchete.

English: Rebekah took the good clothes of Esau, her elder son, which were with her in the house, and put them on Jacob, her younger son.
Kiswahili: Kisha Rebeka akachukua nguo nzuri za Esau mwanawe wa kwanza, alizokuwa nazo nyumbani, akamvika Yakobo mwanawe mdogo.
Ekegusii: Erio Rebeka akabogoria eanga eria engiya mono ya Esau, omwana oye omotangi; eye nigo yagachire nyomba mwaye, akayebekera Yakobo, omwana oye omoke.

English: She put the skins of the young goats on his hands, and on the smooth of his neck.
Kiswahili: Pia akamfunika mikononi na sehemu laini ya shingo kwa ngozi za mbuzi.
Ekegusii: Na amasankwa aria e chimanwa chie chimbori akamoboyia ase amaboko aye ne rigoti.

English: She gave the savory food and the bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Jacob.
Kiswahili: Hatimaye akampa Yakobo hicho chakula kitamu pamoja na mkate aliouoka.
Ekegusii: Erio ababeeka ase amaboko ’omwana oye Yakobo endagera eria engiya aroisetie, amo nomogati.

English: He came to his father, and said, “My father?” He said, “Here I am. Who are you, my son?”
Kiswahili: Akamwendea baba yake akasema, “Baba yangu.” Akajibu, “Naam, mwanangu, wewe ni nani?”
Ekegusii: Yakobo akagenda agasoa nyomba mwaise, akamoteebia: “Tata!” Nere agaitaba: “Nao inde aa. Naye ng’o, mwana one?”

English: Jacob said to his father, “I am Esau your firstborn. I have done what you asked me to do. Please arise, sit and eat of my venison, that your soul may bless me.”
Kiswahili: Yakobo akamwambia baba yake, “Mimi ni Esau mzaliwa wako wa kwanza. Nimefanya kama ulivyoniambia. Tafadhali uketi, ule sehemu ya mawindo yangu ili uweze kunibariki.”
Ekegusii: Yakobo akairaneria ise iga: “Ninche Esau, omwana oo omotangi. Nakorire buna gwantebeetie; booka, oikaranse egere orie enyama y’obotwari bwane, erio onsesenie.”

English: Isaac said to his son, “How is it that you have found it so quickly, my son?” He said, “Because Yahweh your God gave me success.”
Kiswahili: Isaki akamuuliza mwanawe. “Umepataje haraka namna hii, mwanangu?” Akajibu, “Bwana Mungu wako amenifanikisha.”
Ekegusii: Isaka akamobooria: “Omwana one, naki gwakora kwanyora ching’iti bwango iga?” Yakobo akamoiraneria: “mboora Omonene, Nyasae oo, ochindetera.”

English: Isaac said to Jacob, “Please come near, that I may feel you, my son, whether you are really my son Esau or not.”
Kiswahili: Kisha Isaki akamwambia Yakobo, “Mwanangu tafadhali sogea karibu nami ili nikupapase, nione kama hakika ndiwe Esau mwanangu, au la.”
Ekegusii: Erio Isaka agateebia Yakobo: “Inchuo aiga ang’e ase ’nde, ngotabatabe, erinde imanye gose naye omwana one Esau, gose tari ere.”

English: Jacob went near to Isaac his father. He felt him, and said, “The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.”
Kiswahili: Yakobo akasogea karibu na baba yake Isaki, ambaye alimpapasa na kusema, “Sauti ni ya Yakobo, bali mikono ni ya Esau.”
Ekegusii: Yakobo akagenda agaika ise ang’e, na ere akamotaba‐taba, akabora: “Eriogi rirorio neria Yakobo, korende amaboko naya Esau.”

English: He didn’t recognize him, because his hands were hairy, like his brother Esau’s hands. So he blessed him.
Kiswahili: Hakumtambua, kwa sababu mikono yake ilikuwa na nywele kama ya ndugu yake Esau, kwa hiyo akambariki.
Ekegusii: Na ise tamomanya, ekiagera amaboko aye nigo areenge namarionya buna aya Esau omwabo. Ase igo, akamosesenia.

English: He said, “Are you really my son Esau?” He said, “I am.”
Kiswahili: Akamuuliza, “Hivi kweli wewe ni mwanangu Esau?” Akajibu, “Mimi ndiye.”
Ekegusii: Akamobooria: “Amaene, naye omwana one Esau?” Yakobo akamoiraneria: “Ee, Tata ninche.”

English: He said, “Bring it near to me, and I will eat of my son’s venison, that my soul may bless you.” He brought it near to him, and he ate. He brought him wine, and he drank.
Kiswahili: Kisha akasema, “Mwanangu, niletee sehemu ya mawindo yako nile, ili nipate kukubariki.” Yakobo akamletea naye akala, akamletea na divai akanywa.
Ekegusii: Naende Isaka akamoteebia: “Ng’ererie endagera eyio gocha ang’e aiga, omwana one, indie enyama y’obotwari bwao, erio ngosesenie.” Ase igo, akamoyeirera endagera eria na ere akaria, akamoa na edivai, akanywa.

English: His father Isaac said to him, “Come near now, and kiss me, my son.”
Kiswahili: Kisha Isaki baba yake akamwambia, “Njoo hapa, mwanangu, unibusu.”
Ekegusii: Isaka ise akamoteebia: “Omwana one, inchwo aiga ang’e ase ’nde, erio onyunyunte.”

English: He came near, and kissed him. He smelled the smell of his clothing, and blessed him, and said, “Behold, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which Yahweh has blessed.
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo akamwendea akambusu. Isaki aliposikia harufu ya nguo zake, akambariki, akasema, “Aha, harufu ya mwanangu ni kama harufu ya shamba ambalo Bwana amelibariki.
Ekegusii: Erio akamoika ang’e, akamonyunyunta. Isaka agatiokerera rimisu rie chianga chiaye, akamosesenia, akabora: “Naama! Rimisu ri’omwana one Esau nigo rigotioka buna rimisu ri’omogondo omuya, osesenirie n’Omonene!

English: God give you of the dew of the sky, of the fatness of the earth, and plenty of grain and new wine.
Kiswahili: Mungu na akupe umande kutoka mbinguni na utajiri wa duniani: wingi wa nafaka na divai mpya.
Ekegusii: Tiga Nyasae agoitororere riime rikorwa igoro na obonoru bwe riroba, ne rigesa riao ribe rinyinge, na edivai boigo.

English: Let peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you. Be lord over your brothers. Let your mother’s sons bow down to you. Cursed be everyone who curses you. Blessed be everyone who blesses you.”
Kiswahili: Mataifa na yakutumikie na mataifa yakusujudie. Uwe bwana juu ya ndugu zako, na wana wa mama yako wakusujudie. Walaaniwe wale wakulaanio, nao wale wakubarikio wabarikiwe.”
Ekegusii: Abanto bagokorere emeremo, na ebisaku bikoe obonene. Obe omonene ase abamino bonsi, abana ba nyoko bagosike; oyorakoragererie, nere naragererigwe, na oyoragosesenie, nere nasesenigwe!”

English: As soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob, and Jacob had just gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, Esau his brother came in from his hunting.
Kiswahili: Baada ya Isaki kumaliza kumbariki na baada tu ya Yakobo kuondoka kwa baba yake, ndugu yake Esau akaingia kutoka mawindoni.
Ekegusii: Ekero Isaka konya aikire gosesenia Yakobo, na Yakobo karure ase obosio bwa Isaka ise, Esau omwabo akairana korwa ase obotwaari bwaye.

English: He also made savory food, and brought it to his father. He said to his father, “Let my father arise, and eat of his son’s venison, that your soul may bless me.”
Kiswahili: Naye pia akaandaa chakula kitamu akamletea baba yake. Kisha akamwambia, “Baba yangu, keti ule sehemu ya mawindo yangu, ili upate kunibariki.”
Ekegusii: Nere boigo akaroisia endagera engiya, akarentera ise, akamoteebia: “Tata, inchwo orie endagera y’obotwari bwane, inche omwana oo, erinde onsesenie.”

English: Isaac his father said to him, “Who are you?” He said, “I am your son, your firstborn, Esau.”
Kiswahili: Isaki baba yake akamuuliza, “Wewe ni nani?” Akajibu, “Mimi ni mwanao, mzaliwa wako wa kwanza, Esau.”
Ekegusii: Isaka ise akamobooria: “Aye naye ng’o?” Ere akamoiraneria: “Ninche Esau omwana oo, okoira kwao ogotang’ani.”

English: Isaac trembled violently, and said, “Who, then, is he who has taken venison, and brought it to me, and I have eaten of all before you came, and have blessed him? Yes, he will be blessed.”
Kiswahili: Isaki akatetemeka kwa nguvu sana, akasema, “Alikuwa nani basi, ambaye aliwinda mawindo akaniletea? Nilikula kabla tu hujaja na nikambariki, naye hakika atabarikiwa!”
Ekegusii: Erio Isaka agakumia mono na koiguswa, akabora: “Kai! Kai! Ning’o oria ocha ondetera endagera engiya, na inche naria yonsi ekero otaracha, namosesenia? Ee! Ee!, Nere bono oikire gosesenigwa!”

English: When Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with an exceedingly great and bitter cry, and said to his father, “Bless me, even me also, my father.”
Kiswahili: Esau aliposikia maneno haya ya baba yake, akalia sauti kubwa na ya uchungu, na kumwambia baba yake, “Nibariki mimi, mimi pia, baba yangu!”
Ekegusii: Ekero Esau achia koigwa amang’ana aya korwa ase ise, agakuura na korera ekerero ekenene mono ki’obororo, akamoteebia: “Nsesenie nainche boigo, Tata!”

English: He said, “Your brother came with deceit, and has taken away your blessing.”
Kiswahili: Lakini akasema, “Ndugu yako amekuja kwa udanganyifu na akachukua baraka yako.”
Ekegusii: Korende Isaka akamoiraneria: “Oyomino nigo achicha nobong’ainereria, na ere bono oirire ogosesenigwa kwao.”

English: He said, “Isn’t he rightly named Jacob? For he has supplanted me these two times. He took away my birthright. See, now he has taken away my blessing.” He said, “Haven’t you reserved a blessing for me?”
Kiswahili: Esau akasema, “Si ndiyo sababu anaitwa Yakobo? Amenidanganya mara hizi mbili: Alichukua haki yangu ya kuzaliwa na sasa amechukua baraka yangu!” Kisha akauliza, “Hukubakiza hata baraka moja kwa ajili yangu?”
Ekegusii: Esau akabora: “Inee! Tari korokwa Yakobo ase oboronge? Naki eye nengaki ya kabere ang’ainereirie. Ritang’ani akaira omwando one bw’okoiborwa kw’obotangi, naende bono oirire ogosesenigwa kwane!” Naende agwo kegima akamobooria ise iga: “Inee, tontigarereti ogosesenigwa?”

English: Isaac answered Esau, “Behold, I have made him your lord, and all his brothers I have given to him for servants. I have sustained him with grain and new wine. What then will I do for you, my son?”
Kiswahili: Isaki akamjibu Esau, “Nimemfanya yeye kuwa bwana juu yako, pia nimewafanya ndugu zako wote kuwa watumishi wake, nimemtegemeza kwa nafaka na divai mpya. Sasa nitaweza kukufanyia nini, mwanangu?”
Ekegusii: Isaka akamoiraneria: “Rora, bono naikire komokora obeire omonene oo, na abamwabo bonsi babe abasomba baye, naende namoeire endagera y’omogondo na edivai. Inki rende bono nkogokorera aye, omwana one?”

English: Esau said to his father, “Do you have just one blessing, my father? Bless me, even me also, my father.” Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.
Kiswahili: Esau akamwambia baba yake, “Je, baba yangu una baraka moja tu? Unibariki mimi pia, baba yangu!” Kisha Esau akalia kwa sauti kubwa.
Ekegusii: Esau akabooria ise: “Ogosesenia nokomo gwoka kwabwate, Tata? Nsesenia nainche boigo, Tata ominto.” Esau agaaka egakuura, na akarera nobororo.

English: Isaac his father answered him, “Behold, your dwelling will be of the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of the sky from above.
Kiswahili: Baba yake Isaki akamjibu, akamwambia, “Makao yako yatakuwa mbali na utajiri wa dunia, mbali na umande wa mbinguni juu.
Ekegusii: Erio Isaka ise akamoiraneria, akamoteebia, “Rora, obomenyo bwao inabobe aare korwa ase obonoru bwe riroba, na aare korwa ase riimi rikorwa igoro.

English: You will live by your sword, and you will serve your brother. It will happen, when you will break loose, that you will shake his yoke from off your neck.”
Kiswahili: Utaishi kwa upanga, nawe utamtumikia ndugu yako, lakini wakati utakapokuwa umejikomboa, utatupa nira yake kutoka shingoni mwako.”
Ekegusii: Omoro oo bw’esegi nogere obe moyo, aye nomokorere oyomino emeremo; korende engaki neche orekong’ie, nobune rikorogoto erio akobekeire ase rigoti riao.”

English: Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing with which his father blessed him. Esau said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand. Then I will kill my brother Jacob.”
Kiswahili: Esau akawa na kinyongo dhidi ya Yakobo kwa ajili ya baraka ambazo baba yake alikuwa amembariki. Akasema moyoni mwake, “Siku za kuomboleza kwa ajili ya baba yangu zimekaribia, ndipo nitamuua ndugu yangu Yakobo.”
Ekegusii: Esau akagecha Yakobo ase engencho y’ogosesenigwa okwo ise amosesenetie, agateeba ase omoyo oye ime: “Amatuko ay’okomoreera Tata ng’ang’e are; erio nario ndaite Yakobo.”

English: The words of Esau, her elder son, were told to Rebekah. She sent and called Jacob, her younger son, and said to him, “Behold, your brother Esau comforts himself about you by planning to kill you.
Kiswahili: Rebeka alipokwisha kuambiwa yale aliyoyasema Esau mwanawe mkubwa, alimwita Yakobo mwanawe mdogo, akamwambia, “Ndugu yako Esau anajifariji kwa wazo la kukuua.
Ekegusii: Korende ekero Rebeka ateebigwa aya Esau, omwana oye omonene, agoteeba, agatoma omonto korangeria Yakobo, omwana oye omoke, akamoteebia: “Rora, momura omino Esau ogotianeire ng’a nkogoitare.

English: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice. Arise, flee to Laban, my brother, in Haran.
Kiswahili: Sasa basi, mwanangu, fanya nisemalo: Kimbilia haraka kwa Labani ndugu yangu kule Harani.
Ekegusii: Na bono, omwana one, igwa amang’ana aane, imoka otame gochia o Labani, momura ominto aaria Harani.

English: Stay with him a few days, until your brother’s fury turns away—
Kiswahili: Ukae naye kwa muda mpaka ghadhabu ya ndugu yako itulie.
Ekegusii: Omenye aroro ase engaki enke, goika ekeririanda kia momura omino gekende.

English: until your brother’s anger turns away from you, and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send, and get you from there. Why should I be bereaved of you both in one day?”
Kiswahili: Wakati ndugu yako atakapokuwa hana hasira nawe tena na amesahau uliyomtendea, nitakupelekea ujumbe urudi. Kwa nini niwapoteze wote wawili kwa siku moja?”
Ekegusii: Ekero endamwamu yaye erakee, na ere ebire aya kwamokorerete, erio nintome abanto bache gokorangeria oirane korwa aroro. Nase ki ndakwerwe nainwe mwensi babere ase rituko erimo.”

English: Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these, of the daughters of the land, what good will my life do me?”
Kiswahili: Kisha Rebeka akamwambia Isaki, “Nimechukia kuishi kwa sababu ya hawa wanawake wa Kihiti. Ikiwa Yakobo ataoa mke miongoni mwa wanawake wa nchi hii, wanawake wa Kihiti kama hawa, sitakuwa na faida kuendelea kuishi.”
Ekegusii: Erio Rebeka agakwana na Isaka, akamoteebia: “Nigo ngechirie mono ase obogima bwane ase engencho y’abaiseke b’Abahiti. Onye Yakobo ogochia konyuoma oyomo bw’abaiseke b’Abahiti, koreng’ana buna aba bamenyete ase ensemo eye, rirorio obogima bwane inki borangwenere?”

English: Isaac called Jacob, blessed him, and commanded him, “You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.
Kiswahili: Basi Isaki akamwita Yakobo, akambariki na akamwamuru, akisema, “Usioe mwanamke wa Kikanaani.
Ekegusii: Erio Isaka akarangeria Yakobo, akamosesenia, akamoteebia: “Tobaisa konyuoma omoiseke bw’Abakaanani.

English: Arise, go to Paddan Aram, to the house of Bethuel your mother’s father. Take a wife from there from the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.
Kiswahili: Nenda mara moja mpaka Padan-Aramu, kwenye nyumba ya Bethueli baba wa mama yako. Uchukue mke kati ya binti za Labani ambaye ni ndugu wa mama yako.
Ekegusii: Imoka, ogende Padan‐Aramu ase omochie o Betueli, sokoro yao, onyuome omokungu oyomo korwa ase abaiseke ba Labani, nyoko-rome.

English: May God Almighty bless you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, that you may be a company of peoples,
Kiswahili: Mungu Mwenyezi na akubariki uwe na uzao uongezeke idadi yako upate kuwa jamii kubwa ya watu.
Ekegusii: Na Nyasae Omobui nagosesenie, agokinie, na oroiboro rwao naromente robe omoganda omonene bw’ebisaku.

English: and give you the blessing of Abraham, to you and to your offspring with you, that you may inherit the land where you travel, which God gave to Abraham.”
Kiswahili: Na akupe wewe na uzao wako baraka aliyopewa Abrahamu, upate kumiliki nchi unayoishi sasa kama mgeni, nchi ambayo Mungu alimpa Abrahamu.”
Ekegusii: Ere nakoe ogosesenigwa kwa Aburaamu, aye amo na ororeeria rwao, erinde onyare koira ense eye ore omomenyi bono, eye Nyasae aete Aburaamu!”

English: Isaac sent Jacob away. He went to Paddan Aram to Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob’s and Esau’s mother.
Kiswahili: Kisha Isaki akamuaga Yakobo, naye akaenda Padan-Aramu, kwa Labani mwana wa Bethueli Mwaramu, ndugu wa Rebeka, aliyekuwa mama wa Yakobo na Esau.
Ekegusii: Naboigo Isaka agateebia Yakobo agende, na ere akagenda Padan‐Aramu ase Labani, mosinto o Betueli Omoaramu, Labani nere momura omwabo Rebeka, ng’ina Yakobo na Esau.

English: Now Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to Paddan Aram, to take him a wife from there, and that as he blessed him he gave him a command, saying, “You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan;”
Kiswahili: Sasa Esau akajua kuwa Isaki amembariki Yakobo na kumtuma kwenda Padan-Aramu ili achukue mke huko na kwamba alipombariki alimwamuru akisema, “Usioe mke katika binti za Wakanaani,”
Ekegusii: Bono Esau akarora buna Isaka asesenirie Yakobo na komotoma agende Padan‐Aramu anyuome omokungu korwa aroro, ekiagera ekero amosesenetie, akamokania tabaisa konyuoma moiseke onde bwensi bw’Abakaanani!

English: and that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother, and was gone to Paddan Aram.
Kiswahili: tena kwamba Yakobo amewatii baba yake na mama yake naye amekwenda Padan-Aramu.
Ekegusii: Naende akarora ng’a Yakobo oigwereire ise na ng’ina ochiire Padan‐Aramu.

English: Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan didn’t please Isaac, his father.
Kiswahili: Esau akatambua jinsi ambavyo baba yake Isaki anavyowachukia binti za Wakanaani.
Ekegusii: Ase igo, ekero Esau arooche ng’a Isaka ise tancheti abaiseke abwo b’Abakaanani,

English: So Esau went to Ishmael, and took, in addition to the wives that he had, Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebaioth, to be his wife.
Kiswahili: Ndipo Esau akaenda kwa Ishmaeli, akamwoa Mahalati, ndugu wa Nebayothi na binti wa Ishmaeli mwana wa Abrahamu, kuongezea wale wake wengine aliokuwa nao.
Ekegusii: nonya obwate abakungu bande, akagenda o Isumaeli, akanyuoma Mahalati, omoiseke o Isumaeli mosinto o Aburaamu, mosubati omwabo Nebayoti, abe omokungu oye amo nabakungu baria bande abwate ritang’ani.

English: Jacob went out from Beersheba, and went toward Haran.
Kiswahili: Yakobo akatoka Beer-Sheba kwenda Harani.
Ekegusii: Yakobo akaimoka korwa Beeri‐Seba kogenda Harani.

English: He came to a certain place, and stayed there all night, because the sun had set. He took one of the stones of the place, and put it under his head, and lay down in that place to sleep.
Kiswahili: Alipofika mahali fulani, akalala hapo kwa sababu jua lilikuwa limetua. Akachukua jiwe moja la mahali pale, akaliweka chini ya kichwa chake akajinyoosha akalala usingizi.
Ekegusii: Agaika aase gete, akaraara agwo botuko, ekiagera erioba konya riagure. Akabogoria rigena erimo ri’aase aria, agatoorera omotwe oye ase rigena riria, karaaire.

English: He dreamed and saw a stairway set upon the earth, and its top reached to heaven. Behold, the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.
Kiswahili: Akaota ndoto ambayo aliona ngazi imesimamishwa juu ya ardhi, ncha yake ikiwa imefika mbinguni na malaika wa Mungu wakawa wakipanda na kushuka juu yake.
Ekegusii: Akaroota, akarora engaasi getenenirie korwa inse y’ense, keigete igoro, na abamalaika ba Nyasae bakoyeriinera na goikera.

English: Behold, Yahweh stood above it, and said, “I am Yahweh, the God of Abraham your father, and the God of Isaac. I will give the land you lie on to you and to your offspring.
Kiswahili: Juu yake alisimama Bwana, akasema, “Mimi ni Bwana, Mungu wa baba yako Abrahamu na Mungu wa Isaki. Nchi ambayo umelala juu yake, nitakupa wewe na uzao wako.
Ekegusii: Akarora Omonene oteneine ase obosio bwaye, okobora: “Inche ninche Omonene, Nyasae o Aburaamu, na Nyasae o Isaka. Ense eye oraire ninkoyee aye amo noroiboro rwao;

English: Your offspring will be as the dust of the earth, and you will spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south. In you and in your offspring, all the families of the earth will be blessed.
Kiswahili: Uzao wako utakuwa kama mavumbi ya nchi, nawe utaenea upande wa magharibi na mashariki, kaskazini na kusini. Kupitia wewe na uzao wako mataifa yote ya duniani yatabarikiwa.
Ekegusii: narororwo inarobe oronge buna orotu rw’ense, naye norande gochia ensemo ya bosongo, na moocha, na sugusu, na Irianyi; na asore aye, na ase ororeeria rwao, chiamate chionsi chi’ense inachisesenigwe.

English: Behold, I am with you, and will keep you, wherever you go, and will bring you again into this land. For I will not leave you until I have done that which I have spoken of to you.”
Kiswahili: Niko pamoja nawe nami nitakulinda kila uendako na nitakurudisha katika nchi hii. Sitakuacha mpaka nitakapofanya hayo niliyokuahidi.”
Ekegusii: Rora, inche nimbe amo naye, ninkorende aande onsi ase orabe gokogenda, naende ninkoiranie gocha ase ense eye; naki tinkogotiga goika nagokoreire ayio nagoteebirie.”

English: Jacob awakened out of his sleep, and he said, “Surely Yahweh is in this place, and I didn’t know it.”
Kiswahili: Yakobo alipoamka kutoka usingizini, akawaza, “Hakika Bwana yuko mahali hapa, wala mimi sikujua.”
Ekegusii: Yakobo akaboka korwa ase chitoro chiaye, akabora: “Amaene, Omonene nao are aase aa, na inche tinamanyete.”

English: He was afraid, and said, “How awesome this place is! This is none other than God’s house, and this is the gate of heaven.”
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo akaogopa, akasema, “Mahali hapa panatisha kama nini! Bila shaka hapa ndipo nyumba ya Mungu ilipo, hili ni lango la mbinguni.”
Ekegusii: Ere akoboa, akabora: “Aa nase okoirokia! Aa takomocha koba enyomba ya Nyasae, aa nao egeita kia igoro.”

English: Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put under his head, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil on its top.
Kiswahili: Asubuhi yake na mapema, Yakobo akalichukua lile jiwe aliloliweka chini ya kichwa chake, akalisimamisha kama nguzo na kumimina mafuta juu yake.
Ekegusii: Yakobo akaboka mambia chuni, akaimokia rigena riria atoorerete omotwe rogoro, akaritenenia buna esiiro koba ekeinyorio, akaumora amaguta igoro yaye.

English: He called the name of that place Bethel, but the name of the city was Luz at the first.
Kiswahili: Mahali pale akapaita Betheli, ingawa mji ule hapo kwanza uliitwa Luzu.
Ekegusii: Aase aria akaaroka Beteli. Korende ritang’ani omochie oria nigo ore korokwa Lusu.

English: Jacob vowed a vow, saying, “If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and clothing to put on,
Kiswahili: Kisha Yakobo akaweka nadhiri, akisema, “Kama Mungu akiwa pamoja nami na kunilinda katika safari niendayo, akinipa chakula nile na nguo nivae
Ekegusii: Erio Yakobo akaria eira, okobora: “Nyasae karabe amo nainche, andende ase orogendo rwane na kong’a endagera nkoria, ne chianga nkobeeka,

English: so that I come again to my father’s house in peace, and Yahweh will be my God,
Kiswahili: na nirudi salama nyumbani kwa baba yangu, hapo ndipo Bwana atakuwa Mungu wangu,
Ekegusii: na inche kondairane ase omochie o Tata nomorembe, eri’Omonene nabe Nyasae one;

English: then this stone, which I have set up for a pillar, will be God’s house. Of all that you will give me I will surely give a tenth to you.”
Kiswahili: nalo jiwe hili nililolisimamisha kama nguzo litakuwa nyumba ya Mungu na katika yote utakayonipa nitakutolea wewe sehemu ya kumi.”
Ekegusii: ne rigena eri natenenia aa buna esiiro nigo rirabe enyomba yao, Nyasae. Na kende gionsi orang’e inche, amaene tinkomocha gokoa ensemo ya ikomi.”

English: Then Jacob went on his journey, and came to the land of the children of the east.
Kiswahili: Kisha Yakobo akaendelea na safari yake na akafika kwenye nchi za mataifa ya mashariki.
Ekegusii: Erio Yakobo akagenderera norogendo rwaye, agaika ense y’abanto ba moocha.

English: He looked, and saw a well in the field, and saw three flocks of sheep lying there by it. For out of that well they watered the flocks. The stone on the well’s mouth was large.
Kiswahili: Huko akaona kisima katika shamba, pamoja na makundi matatu ya kondoo yamelala karibu na kisima hicho kwa sababu walikuwa wanakunywa maji kutoka kwenye kisimani hicho. Jiwe lililokuwa mdomoni mwa kisima lilikuwa kubwa.
Ekegusii: Agwo akarigereria akarora ensoko yaare ase egetii, na amaicho atato e ching’ondi araire ensoko eyio ensemo, ekiagera ase ensoko eyio nao amaicho are konywera amaache. Na ndiareenge aroro rigena rinene igoro y’omonwa bw’ensoko.

English: There all the flocks were gathered. They rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the sheep, and put the stone back on the well’s mouth in its place.
Kiswahili: Wakati kondoo wanapokuwa wamekusanyika hapo, wachungaji huvingirisha jiwe hilo kutoka kwenye mdomo wa kisima na kunywesha kondoo. Kisha hulirudisha jiwe mahali pake juu ya mdomo wa kisima.
Ekegusii: Agwo nao amaicho onsi areenge gosangererekana, na abarisia nigo baare korusia rigena riria korwa ase omonwa bw’ensoko banyoinsia ching’ondi, naende bariirania ase omonwa bw’ensoko.

English: Jacob said to them, “My relatives, where are you from?” They said, “We are from Haran.”
