Ekegusii: Tobaisa gotuumana orobebe orokoro orwo chisokoro chiao chiabeegete.

English: Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will serve kings. He won’t serve obscure men.
Kiswahili: Je, unamwona mtu stadi katika kazi yake? Atahudumu mbele ya wafalme; hatahudumu mbele ya watu duni.
Ekegusii: Oise korora omonto omanyete emeremo yaye buya, oyio natenene ase amasio y’abarwoti, tagokorera abanto bande emeremo.

English: When you sit to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what is before you;
Kiswahili: Uketipo kula chakula na mtawala, angalia vyema kile kilicho mbele yako,
Ekegusii: Ekero ogoikaransa koria endagera amo nomogaambi, orengererie mono ng’a ning’o ore ase obosio bwao.

English: put a knife to your throat if you are a man given to appetite.
Kiswahili: na utie kisu kooni mwako kama ukiwa mlafi.
Ekegusii: Onye kore n’enchara, obeke omoyio ase ring’orong’oche ria’o.

English: Don’t be desirous of his dainties, since they are deceitful food.
Kiswahili: Usitamani vyakula vyake vitamu kwa kuwa chakula hicho ni cha hila.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gosanera chindagera chiaye chinyansu, ekiagera nigo chire echi’obong’ainereria.

English: Don’t weary yourself to be rich. In your wisdom, show restraint.
Kiswahili: Usijitaabishe ili kuupata utajiri, uwe na hekima kuonyesha kujizuia.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gwechaanda mono ng’a obe omonda; tobaisa gosemeria obong’aini bwao omonyene.

English: Why do you set your eyes on that which is not? For it certainly sprouts wings like an eagle and flies in the sky.
Kiswahili: Kufumba na kufumbua utajiri hutoweka, huwa kama umepata mabawa ghafula, ukaruka na kutoweka angani kama tai.
Ekegusii: Tobirigereria ebio, obonda nigo bogochoma chimbaaba, bwairuruka buna ekeongo ekoiruruka yarimera igoro.

English: Don’t eat the food of him who has a stingy eye, and don’t crave his delicacies,
Kiswahili: Usile chakula cha mtu mchoyo, usitamani vyakula vyake vitamu,
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koria endagera y’omonto ogokomogorera, gose tobaisa gosanera chindagera chiaye chinyansu.

English: for as he thinks about the cost, so he is. “Eat and drink!” he says to you, but his heart is not with you.
Kiswahili: kwa maana yeye ni aina ya mtu ambaye kila mara anafikiri juu ya gharama. Anakuambia, “Kula na kunywa,” lakini moyo wake hauko pamoja nawe.
Ekegusii: Buna omonto akorengereria ime ase enkoro yaye, naboigo are. Nigo akogotiotereria, “Karie na kanywe!”, Korende enkoro yaye tegwancheti.

English: You will vomit up the morsel which you have eaten and waste your pleasant words.
Kiswahili: Utatapika kile kidogo ulichokula, nawe utakuwa umepoteza bure maneno yako ya kumsifu.
Ekegusii: Ayio nigo aragere oroke endagera eria kwaria, naende amang’ana ao amaya asire bosa.

English: Don’t speak in the ears of a fool, for he will despise the wisdom of your words.
Kiswahili: Usizungumze na mpumbavu, kwa maana atadhihaki hekima ya maneno yako.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gokwana amang’ana ao ase omonto omoriri aigwete, ekiagera nigo arachaaye obong’aini bw’amang’ana ao.

English: Don’t move the ancient boundary stone. Don’t encroach on the fields of the fatherless,
Kiswahili: Usisogeze jiwe la mpaka wa zamani wala kunyemelea kwenye mashamba ya yatima,
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gotumana orobebe orokoro, gose totumana osoe ase emegondo ye chintakana,

English: for their Defender is strong. He will plead their case against you.
Kiswahili: kwa kuwa Mtetezi wao ni mwenye nguvu, atalichukua shauri lao dhidi yako.
Ekegusii: ekiagera Omobooria obo nigo are ne chinguru, ere nachirwanerere akorwanie aye.

English: Apply your heart to instruction, and your ears to the words of knowledge.
Kiswahili: Elekeza moyo wako kwenye mafundisho na masikio yako kwenye maneno ya maarifa.
Ekegusii: Karue enkoro y’ao oigwe amorokererio, na amato ao aigwe amang’ana ye chiseemi.

English: Don’t withhold correction from a child. If you punish him with the rod, he will not die.
Kiswahili: Usimnyime mtoto adhabu, ukimwadhibu kwa fimbo, hatakufa.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gotiga korongeyia omwana oo; koramoake ekeranya, tagochia gokwa.

English: Punish him with the rod, and save his soul from Sheol.
Kiswahili: Mwadhibu kwa fimbo na kuiokoa nafsi yake kutoka mautini.
Ekegusii: Ee, koramoake ekeranya nigo oratoorie obogima bwaye korwa aase abakuure.

English: My son, if your heart is wise, then my heart will be glad, even mine.
Kiswahili: Mwanangu, kama moyo wako una hekima, basi moyo wangu utafurahi,
Ekegusii: Omwana one, onye enkoro yao ekoba n’obong’aini, rirorio enkoro y’ane nigo eragooke.

English: Yes, my heart will rejoice when your lips speak what is right.
Kiswahili: utu wangu wa ndani utafurahi, wakati midomo yako itakapozungumza lililo sawa.
Ekegusii: Ekero ebikoba biao birakwane amang’ana amaronge, nigo ndabe nomogooko ime y’ane.

English: Don’t let your heart envy sinners, but rather fear Yahweh all day long.
Kiswahili: Usiuruhusu moyo wako kuwaonea wivu wenye dhambi, bali kila mara uwe na bidii katika kumcha Bwana.
Ekegusii: Enkoro y’ao tebaisa gosanera amang’ana yabanyene ebibe, korende aye ogeenderere komoiroka Omonene kera rituko.

English: Indeed surely there is a future hope, and your hope will not be cut off.
Kiswahili: Hakika kuna tumaini la baadaye kwa ajili yako, nalo tarajio lako halitakatiliwa mbali.
Ekegusii: Ekeene, eng’eria nekare bosio, na ogosemeria kwao tikogosira bosa.

English: Listen, my son, and be wise, and keep your heart on the right path!
Kiswahili: Sikiliza, mwanangu na uwe na hekima, weka moyo wako kwenye njia iliyo sawa.
Ekegusii: Aye omwana one, igwa na obe n’obong’aini, naende orende enkoro y’ao ebwatie enchera endonge.

English: Don’t be among ones drinking too much wine, or those who gorge themselves on meat;
Kiswahili: Usiwe miongoni mwa wanywao mvinyo, au wale walao nyama kwa pupa,
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koba ase egati y’abagotinda nedivai, gose ase egati y’abakoria chinyama bobe,

English: for the drunkard and the glutton shall become poor; and drowsiness clothes them in rags.
Kiswahili: kwa maana walevi na walafi huwa maskini, nako kusinzia huwavika matambara.
Ekegusii: ekiagera abagotinda, na abaria bobe, ’mbabe abataka; na obogondereria bwe chitoro nigo boraboyie omonto amachanchabe.

English: Listen to your father who gave you life, and don’t despise your mother when she is old.
Kiswahili: Msikilize baba yako, aliyekuzaa, wala usimdharau mama yako atakapokuwa mzee.
Ekegusii: Igwera iso okoiborete, na tobaisa komochaya nyoko ekero agotire.

English: Buy the truth, and don’t sell it. Get wisdom, discipline, and understanding.
Kiswahili: Nunua kweli wala usiiuze, pata hekima, adabu na ufahamu.
Ekegusii: Gora ekeene, na tobaisa gokeoonia; boigo gora obong’aini, na amorokererio, na obomanyi.

English: The father of the righteous has great joy. Whoever fathers a wise child delights in him.
Kiswahili: Baba wa mwenye haki ana furaha kubwa, naye aliye na mwana mwenye hekima humfurahia.
Ekegusii: Ise bw’omonto ore omonyene oboronge nigo akoba nomogooko omonene. Ere oyoiboire omwana omomura omong’aini nagookigwe nere.

English: Let your father and your mother be glad! Let her who bore you rejoice!
Kiswahili: Baba yako na mama yako na wafurahi, mama aliyekuzaa na ashangilie!
Ekegusii: Bagookie iso na nyoko, tiga oria okoiborete akogookere.

English: My son, give me your heart; and let your eyes keep in my ways.
Kiswahili: Mwanangu, nipe moyo wako, macho yako na yafuate njia zangu,
Ekegusii: Omwana one, ing’a enkoro yao, na amaiso ao tiga agookere chiinchera chiane.

English: For a prostitute is a deep pit; and a wayward wife is a narrow well.
Kiswahili: kwa maana kahaba ni shimo refu na mwanamke mpotovu ni kisima chembamba.
Ekegusii: Omokungu omotayayi nigo anga engoro entambe gochia inse, na omokungu bw’omonto onde nigo anga egesiima ekegote.

English: Yes, she lies in wait like a robber, and increases the unfaithful among men.
Kiswahili: Kama mnyangʼanyi, hungojea akivizia, naye huzidisha wasio waaminifu miongoni mwa wanaume.
Ekegusii: Ee, omokungu oyio nigo akoboera buna omouri, nigo akomentekania abasaria ase egati ya Mwanyabaanto.

English: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has strife? Who has complaints? Who has needless bruises? Who has bloodshot eyes?
Kiswahili: Ni nani mwenye ole? Ni nani mwenye huzuni? Ni nani mwenye ugomvi? Ni nani mwenye malalamiko? Ni nani aliye na majeraha yasiyo na sababu? Ni nani mwenye macho mekundu?
Ekegusii: Ning’o oyio ore nobobe? Ning’o oyio oichanete? Ning’o oyio okorwana na kwereera? Ning’o oyio oakirwe chingoma chitagwenerete aakwe? Ning’o oyio obariiretie amaiso?

English: Those who stay long at the wine; those who go to seek out mixed wine.
Kiswahili: Ni hao wakaao sana kwenye mvinyo, hao waendao kuonja mabakuli ya mvinyo uliochanganywa.
Ekegusii: Nabaanto abwo bakona-konywa edivai ase chingaki chintambe, na abwo bakona‐korigia konywa edivai yochoganirie n’eyende.

English: Don’t look at the wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup, when it goes down smoothly.
Kiswahili: Usiukodolee macho mvinyo wakati ukiwa mwekundu, wakati unapometameta kwenye bilauri, wakati ushukapo taratibu!
Ekegusii: Tobaisa korigereria edivai koyabariirire, ekero ekobera ase egekombe na koirana inse ng’ora ng’ora.

English: In the end, it bites like a snake, and poisons like a viper.
Kiswahili: Mwishowe huuma kama nyoka na kutia sumu yake kama nyoka mwenye sumu.
Ekegusii: Omoerio nigo ekoroma buna eng’iti na korasa buna enchoka.

English: Your eyes will see strange things, and your mind will imagine confusing things.
Kiswahili: Macho yako yataona mambo mageni na moyo wako kuwazia mambo yaliyopotoka.
Ekegusii: Amaiso ao nigo ararore amang’ana amageni, na ebirengererio biao ’mbibe ebikorekanu.

English: Yes, you will be as he who lies down in the middle of the sea, or as he who lies on top of the rigging:
Kiswahili: Utakuwa kama alalaye katikati ya bahari, alalaye juu ya kamba ya merikebu.
Ekegusii: Nigo or’abe buna omonto oraire ase egati‐gati y’enyancha, gose buna omonto ore ase omote omotambe igoro okoirwa esiororia.

English: “They hit me, and I was not hurt! They beat me, and I don’t feel it! When will I wake up? I can do it again. I will look for more.”
Kiswahili: Utasema, “Wamenipiga lakini sikuumia! Wamenichapa, lakini sisikii! Nitaamka lini ili nikanywe tena?”
Ekegusii: Aye nigo orateebe, “Nigo bang’agete bororo, korende tinyigweti bobe; nigo bang’wanetie bokong’u, korende tinyigweti kende. Indi ’ngocha koboka ingeende korigia eyende?.”

English: Don’t be envious of evil men, neither desire to be with them;
Kiswahili: Usiwaonee wivu watu waovu, usitamani ushirika nao;
Ekegusii: Aye tobaisa gosanera amang’ana yabakori amabe, gose togania koba amo nabarabwo,

English: for their hearts plot violence and their lips talk about mischief.
Kiswahili: kwa maana mioyo yao hupanga mambo ya jeuri, nayo midomo yao husema juu ya kuleta madhara.
Ekegusii: ekiagera ebirengererio biabo nigo bikoroberia ay’ogosiria, na ebikoba biabo nigo bigokwama ayakorenta emechando.

English: Through wisdom a house is built; by understanding it is established;
Kiswahili: Kwa hekima nyumba hujengwa, nayo kwa njia ya ufahamu huimarishwa
Ekegusii: Enyomba nigo ekoagachwa nobong’aini na yakong’igwa goetera ase okomanya.

English: by knowledge the rooms are filled with all rare and beautiful treasure.
Kiswahili: kwa njia ya maarifa vyumba vyake hujazwa vitu vya thamani na vya kupendeza.
Ekegusii: Ase chiseemi chire, chiero chi’enyomba eyio nigo chigoichorigwa n’ebinto ao ao bi’engeencho enene, na ebi’okogokia.

English: A wise man has great power. A knowledgeable man increases strength,
Kiswahili: Mtu mwenye hekima ana uwezo mkubwa, naye mtu mwenye maarifa huongeza nguvu,
Ekegusii: Omonto omong’aini nigo are ne chinguru, na oyore n’okomanya nigo akoorokia okobua okonene.

English: for by wise guidance you wage your war, and victory is in many advisors.
Kiswahili: kwa kufanya vita unahitaji uongozi na kwa ushindi washauri wengi.
Ekegusii: Ase ogoseemia kw’obong’aini kore, nonyaare korwana esegi, na ase abasemia abange abaya bare, obobui nigo bokonyorekanao.

English: Wisdom is too high for a fool. He doesn’t open his mouth in the gate.
Kiswahili: Hekima i juu mno kwa mpumbavu, katika kusanyiko langoni hana lolote la kusema.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini nigo bore egento kere aare korwa ase omonto omoriri; ere tari komaanora omonwa oye agwo ase egeita.

English: One who plots to do evil will be called a schemer.
Kiswahili: Yeye apangaye mabaya atajulikana kama mtu wa hila.
Ekegusii: Ere oyokoroberia gokora amabe narokwe omonto okorenta emechando.

English: The schemes of folly are sin. The mocker is detested by men.
Kiswahili: Mipango ya upumbavu ni dhambi, watu huchukizwa na mwenye dhihaka.
Ekegusii: Ebirengererio bi’oboriri n’ebibe, na omonyacheche nigo are okogechia ase abanto.

English: If you falter in the time of trouble, your strength is small.
Kiswahili: Ukikata tamaa wakati wa taabu, jinsi gani nguvu zako ni kidogo!
Ekegusii: Korarose na gotang’ang’a ase engaki y’obokong’u rirorio aye nigo ore omoreu otari na nguru.

English: Rescue those who are being led away to death! Indeed, hold back those who are staggering to the slaughter!
Kiswahili: Okoa wale wanaoongozwa kwenye kifo; wazuie wote wanaojikokota kuelekea machinjoni.
Ekegusii: Tooria abwo bakoirwa gochia gokwa; irania abwo bakoirwa gochia goitwa.

English: If you say, “Behold, we didn’t know this,” doesn’t he who weighs the hearts consider it? He who keeps your soul, doesn’t he know it? Shall he not give to every man according to his work?
Kiswahili: Kama mkisema, “Lakini hatukujua lolote kuhusu hili,” je, yule apimaye mioyo halitambui hili? Je, yule awalindaye maisha yenu halijui hili? Je, hatamlipa kila mtu kulingana na aliyotenda?
Ekegusii: Oise goteeba, “Intwe titwamanyete amang’ana aya”, Inee, oyio okorenga chinkoro tamanyeti ayio? Oyio origereretie omoyo oo nigo amanyete ayio, na nigo araakane kera omonto buna ogokora kwaye kore.

English: My son, eat honey, for it is good, the droppings of the honeycomb, which are sweet to your taste;
Kiswahili: Ule asali mwanangu, kwa kuwa ni nzuri; asali kutoka kwenye sega ni tamu kwa kuonja.
Ekegusii: Aye omwana one, karie obooke, ekiagera nobuya; obooke bogotonya korwa ase eriana nigo bore obwansu ase ore.

English: so you shall know wisdom to be to your soul. If you have found it, then there will be a reward: Your hope will not be cut off.
Kiswahili: Ujue pia kwamba hekima ni tamu kwa nafsi yako, kama ukiipata, kuna matumaini kwako ya siku zijazo, nalo tumaini lako halitakatiliwa mbali.
Ekegusii: Manya ng’a obong’aini buna obwo ’mboganeirie ase omoyo oo, korabonyore, rirorio ’nonyore amaya ase amatuko agochi‐goocha, na ogosemeria kwao tikogosira bosa.

English: Don’t lay in wait, wicked man, against the habitation of the righteous. Don’t destroy his resting place;
Kiswahili: Usivizie kama haramia afanyavyo ili kuyashambulia makao ya mwenye haki, wala usiyavamie makazi yake,
Ekegusii: Aye omokori amabe, tobaisa koboera omonyene oboronge ase amenyete, tosaria aase aye agotimokera.

English: for a righteous man falls seven times and rises up again, but the wicked are overthrown by calamity.
Kiswahili: Kwa maana ingawa mtu mwenye haki huanguka mara saba, huinuka tena, lakini waovu huangushwa chini na maafa.
Ekegusii: Omonyene oboronge nigo akogwa ara gatano na kabere, naende oboka, korende abakori amabe nigo bagosira ekero banyorire emechando.

English: Don’t rejoice when your enemy falls. Don’t let your heart be glad when he is overthrown,
Kiswahili: Usitazame kwa kufurahia adui yako aangukapo; wakati ajikwaapo, usiruhusu moyo wako ushangilie.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kogooka ekero omobisa oo agure, na enkoro yao tebaisa gosasoka ekero agochirwe.

English: lest Yahweh see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.
Kiswahili: Bwana asije akaona na kuchukia akaiondoa ghadhabu yake mbali naye.
Ekegusii: Omonene nigo ararore okogooka okwo agechigwe, erio aonchore endamwamu yaye erue ase omobisa oo.

English: Don’t fret yourself because of evildoers, neither be envious of the wicked;
Kiswahili: Usikasirike kwa sababu ya watu wabaya wala usiwaonee wivu waovu,
Ekegusii: Aye togechigwa ase engencho y’abagokora amabe, gose tobaisa gosanera amang’ana y’abakori amabe.

English: for there will be no reward to the evil man. The lamp of the wicked will be snuffed out.
Kiswahili: kwa maana mtu mbaya hana tumaini la siku zijazo, nayo taa ya waovu itazimwa.
Ekegusii: Abagokora amabe tibakonyora amaya ase amatuko agochi‐gocha; etaya y’abakori amabe nerimigwe.

English: My son, fear Yahweh and the king. Don’t join those who are rebellious,
Kiswahili: Mwanangu, mche Bwana na mfalme, wala usijiunge na waasi,
Ekegusii: Aye omwana one, omoiroke Omonene, oiroke na omorwoti, tobaisa gosang’anana nabasaria.

English: for their calamity will rise suddenly. Who knows what destruction may come from them both?
Kiswahili: kwa maana hao wawili watatuma maangamizi ya ghafula juu yao, naye ni nani ajuaye maafa wawezayo kuleta?
Ekegusii: Abwo nigo baranyore emechando ya mobosokano, na ning’o oranyaare komanya ogosirigwa kwabo?

English: These also are sayings of the wise: To show partiality in judgment is not good.
Kiswahili: Hii pia ni misemo ya wenye hekima: Kuonyesha upendeleo katika hukumu si vyema:
Ekegusii: Amang’ana aya boigo nay’abang’aini. Tari buya gwanchereria abanto ekero ebiina bikonachwa.

English: He who says to the wicked, “You are righteous,” peoples will curse him, and nations will abhor him—
Kiswahili: Yeyote amwambiaye mwenye hatia, “Wewe huna hatia,” Kabila zitamlaani na mataifa yatamkana.
Ekegusii: Oyo ogoteebia omonto omomochi ng’a: “Aye tori omonyaboronge”, oyio abanto ’mbamoragererie, na abanto b’ebisaku nigo baramogeche.

English: but it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and a rich blessing will come on them.
Kiswahili: Bali itakuwa vyema kwa wale watakaowatia hatiani wenye hatia, nazo baraka tele zitawajilia juu yao.
Ekegusii: Korende abwo bakoa omomochi egesusuro ’mbanyore amaya amo nogosesenigwa okuya.

English: An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips.
Kiswahili: Jawabu la uaminifu ni kama busu la midomoni.
Ekegusii: Omonto okoiraneria amairanerio amaronge nigo anga okonyunyuntwa kw’ebikoba.

English: Prepare your work outside, and get your fields ready. Afterwards, build your house.
Kiswahili: Maliza kazi zako za nje, nawe uweke mashamba yako tayari, baada ya hayo, jenga nyumba yako.
Ekegusii: Roisia emeremo yao isiko onsi, naende kora emeremo y’ao ya mogondo eere, na magega y’ayio oagache enyomba y’ao.

English: Don’t be a witness against your neighbor without cause. Don’t deceive with your lips.
Kiswahili: Usishuhudie dhidi ya jirani yako bila sababu, au kutumia midomo yako kudanganya.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koba kirori bosa igo mamincha y’omonto onde, na tobaisa kong’ainereria nebikoba biao.

English: Don’t say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will repay the man according to his work.”
Kiswahili: Usiseme, “Nitamtenda kama alivyonitenda mimi; nitamlipiza mtu yule kwa kile alichonitendea.”
Ekegusii: Tobaisa goteeba, “Goika nainche imokorere buna ankorera; goika imoakane buna ogokora kwaye kore.”

English: I went by the field of the sluggard, by the vineyard of the man void of understanding.
Kiswahili: Nilipita karibu na shamba la mvivu, karibu na shamba la mizabibu la mtu asiye na akili,
Ekegusii: Ngaeta ase omogondo bw’omonto omworo, na ase omogondo bw’emesabibu bw’omonto otari nobong’aini.

English: Behold, it was all grown over with thorns. Its surface was covered with nettles, and its stone wall was broken down.
Kiswahili: miiba ilikuwa imeota kila mahali, ardhi ilikuwa imefunikwa na magugu, na ukuta wa mawe ulikuwa umebomoka.
Ekegusii: Nkarora omogondo oyio omerire amagwa, na amasa ayotubire, na amagena aagacheire chindwaki chiaye konya atagokire.

English: Then I saw, and considered well. I saw, and received instruction:
Kiswahili: Nikatafakari moyoni mwangu lile nililoliona, nami nikajifunza somo kutokana na niliyoyaona:
Ekegusii: Nkayorigereria na korengereria mono igoro y’omogondo oyio, nkanyora amorokererio aya:

English: a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep,
Kiswahili: Bado kulala kidogo, kusinzia kidogo, bado kukunja mikono kidogo upate kupumzika:
Ekegusii: Okorara ake, na ogosundoka ake, na okoringania amaboko ake,

English: so your poverty will come as a robber and your want as an armed man.
Kiswahili: hivyo umaskini utakuja juu yako kama mnyangʼanyi, na kupungukiwa kutakujia kama mtu mwenye silaha.
Ekegusii: goika obotaka bogochere buna omouri, na oboremerwa kogochere buna omorwani esegi.

English: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
Kiswahili: Hizi ni mithali zaidi za Solomoni, zilizonakiliwa na watu wa Hezekia mfalme wa Yuda:
Ekegusii: Eye nero emebayeno ya Sulemani, eyio abanto ba Hezekia omorwoti bw’Abayuda, basangereretie.

English: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing, but the glory of kings is to search out a matter.
Kiswahili: Ni Utukufu wa Mungu kuficha jambo, bali ni utukufu wa wafalme kuchunguza jambo.
Ekegusii: Nigo bore obonene bwa Nyasae kobisa amang’ana; korende na obonene bw’abarwoti gokora obotuki ase amang’ana ayio.

English: As the heavens for height, and the earth for depth, so the hearts of kings are unsearchable.
Kiswahili: Kama mbingu zilivyo juu na nchi ilivyo chini, ndivyo ambavyo mioyo ya wafalme haichunguziki.
Ekegusii: Buna koreng’ana igoro ere aare mono etatukwe emanywe, na ayare ase ense inse boigo, ne chinkoro chi’abarwoti tichigotukwa chimanywe.

English: Take away the dross from the silver, and material comes out for the refiner.
Kiswahili: Ondoa takataka kwenye madini ya fedha, nako ndani yake kutatokea chombo cha mfua fedha.
Ekegusii: Rusia amabiria korwa ase efeta, na omoturi ’nanyore efeta akoroiseria egekorero ekiya.

English: Take away the wicked from the king’s presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
Kiswahili: Ondoa waovu mbele ya mfalme, nacho kiti chake cha enzi kitaimarishwa kwa njia ya haki.
Ekegusii: Rusia abakori amabe korwa ase obosio bw’omorwoti, erio ekerogo kiaye ki’obonene nigo kerageenderere gokong’igwa n’oboronge.

English: Don’t exalt yourself in the presence of the king, or claim a place among great men;
Kiswahili: Usijikweze mwenyewe mbele ya mfalme, wala usidai nafasi miongoni mwa watu wakuu;
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gwetang’anania ase obosio bw’omorwoti, gose tobaisa kwebeeka aase abanene bare.

English: for it is better that it be said to you, “Come up here,” than that you should be put lower in the presence of the prince, whom your eyes have seen.
Kiswahili: ni afadhali yeye akuambie, “Njoo huku juu,” kuliko yeye kukuaibisha mbele ya mkuu. Kile ulichokiona kwa macho yako
Ekegusii: Nigo er’abe buya mono ekero orateebigwe, “Inchuo gocha aa”, kobua goseerigwa gochia goikaransa magega korwa ase ribaga ri’abaanto abasike.

English: Don’t be hasty in bringing charges to court. What will you do in the end when your neighbor shames you?
Kiswahili: usiharakishe kukipeleka mahakamani, maana utafanya nini mwishoni kama jirani yako atakuaibisha?
Ekegusii: Toba omwango kogeenda ase ekegambero. Inee! Inki orakore ase omoerio, ekero omonto oyio gwasoerete arakobue n’obe n’obosooku?

English: Debate your case with your neighbor, and don’t betray the confidence of another,
Kiswahili: Kama ukifanya shauri na jirani yako, usisaliti siri ya mtu mwingine,
Ekegusii: Onye aye omonyene kobwate amang’ana n’omonto onde, kwana nere, korende tobaisa koorokia obobisi bw’omonto omoao.

English: lest one who hears it put you to shame, and your bad reputation never depart.
Kiswahili: ama yeye aisikiaye aweza kukuaibisha na kamwe sifa yako mbaya haitaondoka.
Ekegusii: Oise koboorokia, na omonto onde aise koigwa ayio, nigo aragosookie, na erieta ria’o risareke kogeenderera botambe.

English: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
Kiswahili: Neno lisemwalo kwa wakati ufaao ni kama matunda ya mtofaa ya dhahabu yaliyowekwa kwenye vijalizo vya fedha.
Ekegusii: Ring’ana rigokwanwa ase enchera egwenerete nigo ringa buna amatunda amororo amaya mono abekire ase egekabu keroisirie korwa ase efeta.

English: As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover to an obedient ear.
Kiswahili: Kama vile kipuli cha dhahabu au pambo la dhahabu safi, ndivyo lilivyo karipio la mtu mwenye hekima kwa sikio lisikilizalo.
Ekegusii: Omonto omong’aini ogokuurera oyokoigwera nigo are buna ebonyi ne chisonoi biroseirie chitaabu.

English: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to those who send him; for he refreshes the soul of his masters.
Kiswahili: Kama vile ubaridi wa theluji wakati wa mavuno ndivyo alivyo mjumbe mwaminifu kwa wale wamtumao, huburudisha roho za bwana zake.
Ekegusii: Omotomwa ore omwegenwa nigo are ase abwo bakomotoma buna amaache amakendu ase engaki ye rigesa, ekiagera nigo akogera emioyo yabo yaba emeyia.

English: As clouds and wind without rain, so is he who boasts of gifts deceptively.
Kiswahili: Kama vile mawingu na upepo pasipo mvua ndivyo alivyo mtu ajisifuye kwa zawadi ambazo hatoi.
Ekegusii: Omonto ogwetogia ng’a nare nomoyo omorabu, ko tari korua ebiegwa, nigo anga amare na omwaga bitari korenta embura.

English: By patience a ruler is persuaded. A soft tongue breaks the bone.
Kiswahili: Kwa njia ya uvumilivu mtawala aweza kushawishiwa, nao ulimi laini waweza kuvunja mfupa.
Ekegusii: Oboremereria nigo bokwororobia omogambi, na oromeme rw’obwororo nigo rokobuna riuga.

English: Have you found honey? Eat as much as is sufficient for you, lest you eat too much, and vomit it.
Kiswahili: Ukipata asali, kula kiasi tu cha kukutosha, ukila zaidi, utatapika.
Ekegusii: Onye kwanyorire obooke, karie ekerengo kegoisaine; oise kogeetania nigo oraboroke.

English: Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor’s house, lest he be weary of you, and hate you.
Kiswahili: Ingiza mguu wako nyumbani kwa jirani yako mara chache, ukizidisha, atakukinai na atakuchukia.
Ekegusii: Amagoro ao tanara kona‐kogeenda ase enyomba y’omosani oo, nigo arabaise korosa naye, erinde akogeche.

English: A man who gives false testimony against his neighbor is like a club, a sword, or a sharp arrow.
Kiswahili: Kama vile rungu au upanga au mshale mkali ndivyo alivyo mtu atoaye ushuhuda wa uongo dhidi ya jirani yake.
Ekegusii: Omonto okoba kirori bw’oborimo ase omonto onde nigo anga buna enungu y’eseegi, gose omoro, gose ensara enyonge.

English: Confidence in someone unfaithful in time of trouble is like a bad tooth or a lame foot.
Kiswahili: Kama vile jino bovu au mguu uliolemaa, ndivyo ilivyo kumtegemea mtu asiye mwaminifu wakati wa shida.
Ekegusii: Ogosemeria omonto otari omwegenwa ase engaki y’emechando, nigo enga buna erino ribunegete gose okogoro goteng’eretie.

English: As one who takes away a garment in cold weather, or vinegar on soda, so is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
Kiswahili: Kama vile avuaye mavazi siku ya baridi, au kama siki iliyomwagwa juu ya magadi, ndivyo alivyo yeye amuimbiaye nyimbo mtu mwenye moyo mzito.
Ekegusii: Omonto ogoteera amatera y’omogooko ase omonto obwate enkoro ere nobororo nigo anga buna okorusia eanga ase engaki y’obokendu gose kobeeka egento ekeroro ase riote.

English: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink;
Kiswahili: Kama adui yako ana njaa, mpe chakula ale; kama ana kiu, mpe maji anywe.
Ekegusii: Onye omobisa oo ore nenchara, moe endagera arie; onye ore nerang’o, moe amaache anywe.

English: for you will heap coals of fire on his head, and Yahweh will reward you.
Kiswahili: Kwa kufanya hivyo, unaweka makaa ya moto yanayowaka kichwani pake, naye Bwana atakupa thawabu.
Ekegusii: Igo nobeke omorero bw’amakara ase omotwe oye, n’Omonene nakoe eng’eria yao.

English: The north wind produces rain; so a backbiting tongue brings an angry face.
Kiswahili: Kama vile upepo wa kaskazini uletavyo mvua, ndivyo ulimi usingiziao uletavyo uso wa hasira.
Ekegusii: Omwaga okogusa korwa sugusu nigo okorenta embura, naboigo nomonto omogenki akorenta okobeeana.

English: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop than to share a house with a contentious woman.
Kiswahili: Ni afadhali kuishi pembeni mwa paa la nyumba, kuliko kuishi nyumba moja na mke mgomvi.
Ekegusii: Mbuya komenya ase ekenunchi kia irongo igoro, kobua komenya ase enyomba amo n’omokungu omonyariomana.

English: Like cold water to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.
Kiswahili: Kama vile maji baridi kwa nafsi iliyochoka ndivyo zilivyo habari njema kutoka nchi ya mbali.
Ekegusii: Amang’ana amaya akorentwa korwa ase ense y’aare nigo anga buna amaache amakendu ase omonto ore n’erang’o.

English: Like a muddied spring and a polluted well, so is a righteous man who gives way before the wicked.
Kiswahili: Kama vile chemchemi iliyotibuliwa matope au kisima kilichotiwa taka ndivyo alivyo mtu mwenye haki akishiriki na waovu.
Ekegusii: Omonyene oboronge okorua ribaga ase omokori amabe nigo anga buna orooche rore netintira na buna ensoko yasarekire.

English: It is not good to eat much honey, nor is it honorable to seek one’s own honor.
Kiswahili: Si vyema kula asali nyingi sana, wala si heshima kujitafutia heshima yako mwenyewe.
Ekegusii: Tari buya koria obooke obonge, na abwo bakwerigeria obonene, obonene bwabo nigo borabe bosa.

English: Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.
Kiswahili: Kama vile mji ambao kuta zake zimebomoka ndivyo alivyo mtu ambaye hawezi kujitawala mwenyewe.
Ekegusii: Omonto otamanyeti kwegambera omonyene nigo anga buna omochie chindwaki chiaye chiatagoirwe.

English: Like snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool.
Kiswahili: Kama theluji wakati wa kiangazi au mvua wakati wa mavuno, ndivyo asivyostahili heshima mpumbavu.
Ekegusii: Buna koreng’ana obokendu bogocha ase engaki y’egurugura, gose embura egotwa ase engaki ye rigesa, naboigo ere bobe omonto omoriri konyora amasikani.

English: Like a fluttering sparrow, like a darting swallow, so the undeserved curse doesn’t come to rest.
Kiswahili: Kama shomoro apigapigavyo mabawa yake au mbayuwayu katika kuruka kwake kasi, ndivyo ilivyo laana isiyo na sababu haimpati mtu.
Ekegusii: Buna enchiro ekona‐koong’anya, na buna egesingororo gekoiruruka, naboigo na okoragereria gotari nengeencho gotaikere oria oragererigwe.

English: A whip is for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the back of fools!
Kiswahili: Mjeledi kwa farasi, lijamu kwa punda, nayo fimbo kwa migongo ya wapumbavu!
Ekegusii: Ekeranya nigo kere ase ogoaka ebarasi, na ekeokio ase okoraa etigere, naboigo n’enyimbo ere ase ogoaka omogongo bw’omonto omoriri.

English: Don’t answer a fool according to his folly, lest you also be like him.
Kiswahili: Usimjibu mpumbavu sawasawa na upumbavu wake, ama wewe mwenyewe utakuwa kama yeye.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koiraneria omonto omoriri buna oboriri bwaye bore, nigo orabaise koba omoriri buna are.

English: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own eyes.
Kiswahili: Mjibu mpumbavu sawasawa na upumbavu wake, ama atakuwa mwenye hekima machoni pake mwenyewe.
Ekegusii: Moiranerie omonto omoriri buna oboriri bwaye bore, tabaisa gwekaga ng’a nomong’aini are.

English: One who sends a message by the hand of a fool is cutting off feet and drinking violence.
Kiswahili: Kama vile ilivyo kujikata miguu au kunywa hasara, ndivyo ilivyo kutuma ujumbe kwa mkono wa mpumbavu.
Ekegusii: Omonto ogotoma amang’ana ase okoboko kw’omonto omoriri, oyio nigo akobutora amaboko aye omonyene bwerentera emechando.

English: Like the legs of the lame that hang loose, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
Kiswahili: Kama miguu ya kiwete inavyoningʼinia ndivyo ilivyo mithali katika kinywa cha mpumbavu.
Ekegusii: Omoreng’anio ogokwanwa n’omonwa bw’omoriri nigo onga buna omonto egesegora, okogoro kwaye gotari gokora emeremo.

English: As one who binds a stone in a sling, so is he who gives honor to a fool.
Kiswahili: Kama kufunga jiwe kwenye kombeo, ndivyo ilivyo kumpa mpumbavu heshima.
Ekegusii: Omonto okoa omoriri amasikani, nigo anga buna oyokoruta omobuko ore n’ebinto bi’erigori rinene ase etui y’amagena.

English: Like a thorn bush that goes into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
Kiswahili: Kama mwiba kwenye mkono wa mlevi ndivyo ilivyo mithali kinywani mwa mpumbavu.
Ekegusii: Omoreng’anio okorwa ase omonwa bw’omonto omoriri nigo onga buna rigwa rikobeta okoboko kw’omonto otindire amarwa.

English: As an archer who wounds all, so is he who hires a fool or he who hires those who pass by.
Kiswahili: Kama mpiga upinde ambaye hujeruhi ovyo, ndivyo alivyo yeye aajiriye mpumbavu au yeyote apitaye njiani.
Ekegusii: Omonto omanyete emeremo nigo agwekorera emeremo emiya, korende oyore omoriri nigo akoriika onde bwensi ogoeta, na emeremo yasareka.

English: As a dog that returns to his vomit, so is a fool who repeats his folly.
Kiswahili: Kama mbwa ayarudiavyo matapiko yake, ndivyo mpumbavu arudiavyo upumbavu wake.
Ekegusii: Omonto omoriri okoiranerera gokora oboriri bwaye nigo anga esese ekoiranera amaroki aye enyene.

English: Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
Kiswahili: Je, unamwona mtu ajionaye mwenye hekima machoni pake mwenyewe? Liko tumaini zaidi kwa mpumbavu kuliko kwake.
Ekegusii: Oise korora omonto ogwekora omong’aini, ogosemeria ’nkore ase omonto omoriri kobua ase oyio.

English: The sluggard says, “There is a lion in the road! A fierce lion roams the streets!”
Kiswahili: Mvivu husema, “Yuko simba barabarani, simba mkali anazunguka mitaa!”
Ekegusii: Omonto omworo nigo agoteeba, “Endo nere isiko, ee, endo nere ase chiinchera chi’omochie.”

English: As the door turns on its hinges, so does the sluggard on his bed.
Kiswahili: Kama vile mlango ugeukavyo kwenye bawaba zake, ndivyo mvivu ajigeuzavyo kitandani mwake.
Ekegusii: Omonto omworo nigo akonakweoncha‐onchora buna egesieri gekona‐koonchorwa ase chimbata gesibeire.

English: The sluggard buries his hand in the dish. He is too lazy to bring it back to his mouth.
Kiswahili: Mtu mvivu hutumbukiza mkono wake kwenye sahani, naye huchoka kuupeleka kwenye kinywa chake.
Ekegusii: Omonto omworo nigo akobeeka okoboko kwaye ase esani y’endagera, orosa gokobogoria gocha ase omonwa oye.

English: The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer with discretion.
Kiswahili: Mtu mvivu ni mwenye hekima machoni pake mwenyewe, kuliko watu saba wawezao kujibu kwa busara.
Ekegusii: Omonto omworo nigo akwerora ng’a n’omong’aini are abuete abanto batano na babere barakwane amang’ana are n’engeencho.

English: Like one who grabs a dog’s ears is one who passes by and meddles in a quarrel not his own.
Kiswahili: Kama yeye amkamataye mbwa kwa masikio, ndivyo alivyo mtu apitaye njiani na kujiingiza kwenye ugomvi usiomhusu.
Ekegusii: Omonto orenge goeta na gwesoyia ase eriomana ritarenge eriaye nigo anga buna oyo okobwata amato y’esese.

English: Like a madman who shoots torches, arrows, and death,
Kiswahili: Kama mtu mwendawazimu atupaye vijinga vya moto au mishale ya kufisha,
Ekegusii: Omonto okong’aina omonto onde, na magega yaye omoteebia, “Negosori yoka nare kogokorera,” oyio nigo anga buna ebarimo ekoruta ebigenga bi’omorero, ne chinsara, chia amakweri.

English: is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, “Am I not joking?”
Kiswahili: ndivyo alivyo mtu amdanganyaye jirani yake na kusema, “Nilikuwa nikifanya mzaha tu!”
Ekegusii: Ase chinko chitari, omorero nigo okorima, naboigo nase omogenki atari, eriomana nigo rigosira.

English: For lack of wood a fire goes out. Without gossip, a quarrel dies down.
Kiswahili: Bila kuni moto huzimika; pasipo uchongezi ugomvi humalizika.
Ekegusii: Omonyariomana ogoseegeta amariomana nigo anga buna amakara akogeenderera koyia, gose chinko chikogera omorero ogeenderera gwoka.

English: As coals are to hot embers, and wood to fire, so is a contentious man to kindling strife.
Kiswahili: Kama makaa juu ya makaa yanayowaka, na kama kuni kwenye moto, ndivyo alivyo mtu mgomvi kwa kuchochea ugomvi.
Ekegusii: Amang’ana omonto omoitania nigo are buna endagera enyansu egotirimboka gochia ase enda inse.

English: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, they go down into the innermost parts.
Kiswahili: Maneno ya mchongezi ni kama chakula kitamu; huingia sehemu za ndani sana za mtu.
Ekegusii: Omonto obwate amang’ana amansu ase ebikoba biaye, korende ore nobobe ase enkoro yaye, nigo anga buna egekorero ki’amaroba giatekire keoomire nefeta.

English: Like silver dross on an earthen vessel are the lips of a fervent one with an evil heart.
Kiswahili: Kama rangi ingʼaayo iliyopakwa kwenye vyombo vya udongo ndivyo ilivyo midomo laini pamoja na moyo mbaya.
Ekegusii: Omonto omogechi nigo akobisa ase ebikoba biaye, obong’ainereria bore ase enkoro yaye.

English: A malicious man disguises himself with his lips, but he harbors evil in his heart.
Kiswahili: Mtu mwenye nia ya kudhuru wengine hujificha kwa maneno ya midomo yake, lakini moyoni mwake huficha udanganyifu.
Ekegusii: Ekero agokwana amang’ana are amansu, tobaisa komwegena, ekiagera nabwate ay’okogechia atano na abere, ase enkoro yaye ime.

English: When his speech is charming, don’t believe him, for there are seven abominations in his heart.
Kiswahili: Ingawa maneno yake huvutia, usimwamini, kwa maana machukizo saba hujaza moyo wake.
Ekegusii: Naisa gotuba okogecha kwaye nobong’ainereria, obokayayu bwaye goika bomanyekane n’omosangererekano bwonsi.

English: His malice may be concealed by deception, but his wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.
Kiswahili: Nia yake ya kudhuru wengine inaweza kufichwa na udanganyifu, lakini uovu wake utafichuliwa kwenye kusanyiko.
Ekegusii: Omonto okorema eirima, nere omonyene oragwe imeo; na omonto ogoturunkania rigena, nere omonyene rirairanere rimogwere.

English: Whoever digs a pit shall fall into it. Whoever rolls a stone, it will come back on him.
Kiswahili: Kama mtu akichimba shimo, atatumbukia ndani yake, kama mtu akivingirisha jiwe, litamrudia.
Ekegusii: Omonto ore noromeme rogokwana oborimo, nigo akogecha abanto abwo amang’ana aye achaandire bobe, na omonwa ogokwana amang’ana ay’okweansia nigo okorenta ogosirigwa.

English: Don’t boast about tomorrow; for you don’t know what a day may bring.
Kiswahili: Usijisifu kwa ajili ya kesho, kwa kuwa hujui ni nini kitakachozaliwa kwa siku moja.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gwetogeria rituko ri’ankio, ekiagera tomanyeti aya rituko erio rikorenta.

English: Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips.
Kiswahili: Mwache mwingine akusifu, wala si kinywa chako mwenyewe; mtu mwingine afanye hivyo na si midomo yako mwenyewe.
Ekegusii: Aye omonyene tobaisa gwetogia, korende tiga omonto onde agotogie; tiga omonto omoao agotogie, korende tari ebikoba biao omonyene.

English: A stone is heavy, and sand is a burden; but a fool’s provocation is heavier than both.
Kiswahili: Jiwe ni zito na mchanga ni mzigo, lakini kukasirishwa na mpumbavu ni kuzito kuliko vyote viwili.
Ekegusii: Rigena neririto na omokenye nomorito, korende okogechigwa kw’omonto omoriri nigo kore okorito kobua ebinto ebio bibere.

English: Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; but who is able to stand before jealousy?
Kiswahili: Hasira ni ukatili na ghadhabu kali ni gharika, lakini ni nani awezaye kusimama mbele ya wivu?
Ekegusii: Endamwamu nentindi, na ekeririanda nigo kegosiria, korende ning’o oranyaare koremereria ribero?

English: Better is open rebuke than hidden love.
Kiswahili: Afadhali karipio la wazi kuliko upendo uliofichika.
Ekegusii: Ogotogonyera kwa maiso marore nigo kore okuya kobua obwanchani bobisegete.

English: The wounds of a friend are faithful, although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
Kiswahili: Majeraha kutoka kwa rafiki yaonyesha uaminifu, bali kubusu kwa adui ni kwingi sana.
Ekegusii: Ogoakwa gokorwa ase omosani nigo kore okw’obwegenwa, korende okonyunyunta kw’omobisa nigo kore okw’obong’ainereria.

English: A full soul loathes a honeycomb; but to a hungry soul, every bitter thing is sweet.
Kiswahili: Yeye aliyeshiba huchukia kabisa asali, bali kwa mwenye njaa hata kile kilicho kichungu kwake ni kitamu.
Ekegusii: Omonto oigotete nigo agochaaya nonya nobooke, korende oyore n’enchara nonya n’endagera ere endoro nigo ekomwansera.

English: As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man who wanders from his home.
Kiswahili: Kama ndege atangatangavyo mbali na kiota chake, ndivyo alivyo mtu atangatangaye mbali na nyumbani mwake.
Ekegusii: Omonto ogotama korwa bwoye nigo anga buna enyoni ekong’anya korwa ase egeswa kiaye.

English: Perfume and incense bring joy to the heart; so does earnest counsel from a man’s friend.
Kiswahili: Manukato na uvumba huleta furaha moyoni, nao uzuri wa rafiki huchipuka kutoka kwenye ushauri wake wa uaminifu.
Ekegusii: Amaguta akweakwa na amanukato nigo bikogokia enkoro, naboigo bore obwororo bw’omosani oyo okorua ogoseemia okuya.

English: Don’t forsake your friend and your father’s friend. Don’t go to your brother’s house in the day of your disaster. A neighbor who is near is better than a distant brother.
Kiswahili: Usimwache rafiki yako wala rafiki wa baba yako, tena usiende nyumbani mwa ndugu yako wakati umepatwa na maafa. Bora jirani wa karibu kuliko ndugu aliye mbali.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kweba omosani oo, na omosani o iso; rituko kwanyorire emechando togeenda ase enka y’oyomino. Mbuya kogeenda bw’omogisangio ase engaki eyio, kobua korigia oyomino omenyete aare.

English: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, then I can answer my tormentor.
Kiswahili: Mwanangu, uwe na hekima, nawe ulete furaha moyoni mwangu, ndipo nitakapoweza kumjibu yeyote anitendaye kwa dharau.
Ekegusii: Omwana one, kabe n’obong’aini na ogokie enkoro y’ane, erio nario ’ndanyore ring’ana ’nkoiraneria omonto ogonchaaya.

English: A prudent man sees danger and takes refuge; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
Kiswahili: Mtu mwenye busara huona hatari na kujificha, bali mjinga huendelea mbele nayo ikamtesa.
Ekegusii: Omonto omong’aini nigo akororera emechando aare bwebisa, korende oyotamanyeti amaange nigo akogeenderera gochia bosio oumerana nero, erio ochaandeka.

English: Take his garment when he puts up collateral for a stranger. Hold it for a wayward woman!
Kiswahili: Chukua vazi la yule awekaye dhamana kwa ajili ya mgeni; lishikilie iwe dhamana kama anafanya hivyo kwa ajili ya mwanamke mpotovu.
Ekegusii: Ira eanga y’omonto oyo bwerure koba intenenera ase omonto omoao, ira ebi abwate, ekiagera bwerure ase engencho y’omonto otamanyekaneti.

English: He who blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be taken as a curse by him.
Kiswahili: Kama mtu akimbariki jirani yake kwa sauti kuu asubuhi na mapema, itahesabiwa kama ni laana.
Ekegusii: Omonto okobooka mambia chuni oaka eriogi gosesenia omogisangio oye, oyio nabarerwe okoragererigwa.

English: A continual dropping on a rainy day and a contentious wife are alike:
Kiswahili: Mke mgomvi ni kama matone yasiyokoma ya siku ya mvua.
Ekegusii: Omokungu omonyariomana nigo anga buna amatoima y’embura akona‐gotoonya.

English: restraining her is like restraining the wind, or like grasping oil in his right hand.
Kiswahili: Kumzuia yeye ni kama kuuzuia upepo au kukamata mafuta kwa kiganja cha mkono.
Ekegusii: Omonto ogotanga omokungu buna oyio, okwo nigo konga ogotangwa kw’omwaga gose okobwata amaguta n’okoboko gw’okorio.

English: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
Kiswahili: Kama vile chuma kinoavyo chuma, ndivyo mtu amnoavyo mwenzake.
Ekegusii: Ekioma nigo kegotieria ekioma kende, naboigo n’omonto otieria omonto onde.

English: Whoever tends the fig tree shall eat its fruit. He who looks after his master shall be honored.
Kiswahili: Yeye autunzaye mtini atakula tunda lake, naye amtunzaye bwana wake ataheshimiwa.
Ekegusii: Omonto okorenda omoko narie okwama kw’omoko oyio, na oyio okorenda omonene oye, oyio nanyore ogosikwa.

English: Like water reflects a face, so a man’s heart reflects the man.
Kiswahili: Kama uso uonekanavyo kwenye maji, ndivyo hivyo moyo wa mtu humwonyesha alivyo.
Ekegusii: Ekero okorigereria ase amaache ime nigo okorora obosio bwao, naboigo nebirengererio bi’enkoro y’omonto bikororekana ase omonto onde.

English: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; and a man’s eyes are never satisfied.
Kiswahili: Kuzimu na Uharibifu havishibi kadhalika macho ya mwanadamu.
Ekegusii: Buna aase abakuure na embeera bitari goisaneka, naboigo n’amaiso a Mwanyabaanto atari goisaneka.

English: The crucible is for silver, and the furnace for gold; but man is refined by his praise.
Kiswahili: Kalibu ni kwa ajili ya fedha na tanuru kwa ajili ya dhahabu, bali mtu hupimwa kwa sifa azipokeazo.
Ekegusii: Buna koreng’ana efeta egoteemerwa ase egetaabo gekonyititora, na etaabu ase omorero ekebemberi, naboigo omonto agoteemwa na komanyekana ase ogosikwa kwaye.

English: Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with grain, yet his foolishness will not be removed from him.
Kiswahili: Hata ukimtwanga mpumbavu kwenye kinu, ukimtwanga kama nafaka kwa mchi, hutauondoa upumbavu wake.
Ekegusii: Omonto omoriri n’omobekerania ase ekonu ime, omoswageranie amo nobori, oboriri bwaye tibogosira.

English: Know well the state of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds,
Kiswahili: Hakikisha kuwa unajua hali ya makundi yako ya kondoo na mbuzi, angalia kwa bidii ngʼombe zako.
Ekegusii: Manya buya chingencho chi’eching’ondi ne chimbori chiao, na orende riicho ria’o buya.

English: for riches are not forever, nor does the crown endure to all generations.
Kiswahili: Kwa kuwa utajiri haudumu milele, nayo taji haidumu vizazi vyote.
Ekegusii: Obonda tibori kogeenderera kobao botambe, na eguutwa y’obogambi teri kogeenderera kobao ekiaare ase ekiaare.

English: The hay is removed, and the new growth appears, the grasses of the hills are gathered in.
Kiswahili: Wakati majani makavu yameondolewa na mapya yamechipua, nayo majani toka milimani yamekusanywa,
Ekegusii: Ekero obonyansi obokoro bwasirire, na oboyia nigo bokomera, na ebimeri bi’ebitunwa biasangererigwa,

English: The lambs are for your clothing, and the goats are the price of a field.
Kiswahili: wana-kondoo watakupatia mavazi na mbuzi thamani ya shamba.
Ekegusii: ching’ondi nigo chikonachwa amarionya akoroisigwa chianga, ne chimbori chiaoonigwa ase okogora omogondo.

English: There will be plenty of goats’ milk for your food, for your family’s food, and for the nourishment of your servant girls.
Kiswahili: Utakuwa na maziwa mengi ya mbuzi kukulisha wewe na jamaa yako, na kuwalisha watumishi wako wa kike.
Ekegusii: Erio nonyore amabeere ye chimbori agoisaine aye na abanto b’enka yao, boigo nase abasomba bao abaiseke.

English: The wicked flee when no one pursues; but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
Kiswahili: Mtu mwovu hukimbia ingawa hakuna yeyote anayemfukuza, bali wenye haki ni wajasiri kama simba.
Ekegusii: Abakori amabe nigo bagotama nonya onde tari kobabwatia, korende abanyaboronge nigo bare abaremu buna chindo chinsae.

English: In rebellion, a land has many rulers, but order is maintained by a man of understanding and knowledge.
Kiswahili: Wakati nchi inapokuwa na uasi, inakuwa na viongozi wengi, bali mwenye ufahamu na maarifa hudumisha utaratibu.
Ekegusii: Ekero ense yasaririe nigo ekoba n’abagaambi abange, korende eye ebwate abanto bare nobong’aini na okomanya, obogambi nigo bokogeenderera gotenena bokong’u.

English: A needy man who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain which leaves no crops.
Kiswahili: Mtu maskini amwoneaye yeye aliye maskini zaidi ni kama mvua ya dhoruba isiyosaza mazao.
Ekegusii: Omonto omotaka ore n’okobua ogokorera abataka bande bobe ase okobaurereria, nigo anga buna embura enyinge egosaria chindagera.

English: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked; but those who keep the law contend with them.
Kiswahili: Wale waiachao sheria huwasifu waovu, bali wale waishikao sheria huwapinga.
Ekegusii: Abanto batigire amachiiko nigo bagotogia abakori amabe, korende abarendete amachiiko nigo bakoamererania nabwo.

English: Evil men don’t understand justice; but those who seek Yahweh understand it fully.
Kiswahili: Watu wabaya hawaelewi haki, bali wale wamtafutao Bwana wanaielewa kikamilifu.
Ekegusii: Abakori amabe tibamanyeti ayare amaronge, korende abwo bakomorigia Omonene nigo bayamanyete onsi.

English: Better is the poor who walks in his integrity than he who is perverse in his ways, and he is rich.
Kiswahili: Afadhali maskini ambaye mwenendo wake hauna lawama kuliko tajiri ambaye njia zake ni potovu.
Ekegusii: Omonto omotaka okobwatia oboronge nigo are omuya kobua omonda ore omokorekanu.

English: Whoever keeps the law is a wise son; but he who is a companion of gluttons shames his father.
Kiswahili: Yeye ashikaye sheria ni mwana mwenye ufahamu, bali rafiki wa walafi humwaibisha baba yake.
Ekegusii: Omwana orendete amachiiko nigo are omong’aini, korende oyore omogisangio bwa baria bobe nigo akorenta obosooku ase ise.

English: He who increases his wealth by excessive interest gathers it for one who has pity on the poor.
Kiswahili: Yeye aongezaye utajiri wake kwa riba kubwa mno hukusanya kwa ajili ya mwingine, ambaye atawahurumia maskini.
Ekegusii: Omonto okomenta chinibo chiaye ase enchera etari ey’ekeene ase okogania ebitoki, oyio nigo agochisangereria chibe echi’omonto okororera abataka amaabera.

English: He who turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer is an abomination.
Kiswahili: Kama mtu yeyote akikataa kusikia sheria, hata maombi yake ni chukizo.
Ekegusii: Omonto okoonchora ogoto kwaye taigwera amachiiko, nonya n’ogosaba kwaye nigo kore okogechia.

English: Whoever causes the upright to go astray in an evil way, he will fall into his own trap; but the blameless will inherit good.
Kiswahili: Yeye ambaye humwongoza mwenye haki kwenye mapito mabaya, ataanguka kwenye mtego wake mwenyewe, bali wasio na lawama watapokea urithi mwema.
Ekegusii: Omonto ogosiria abare ne chinkoro chindonge, na kobaraa ase enchera ende, oyio nagwe ase eirima eria aremire ere omonyene, korende abwo batari na komocha ’mbanyore omwando omuya.

English: The rich man is wise in his own eyes; but the poor who has understanding sees through him.
Kiswahili: Mtu tajiri anaweza kuwa na hekima machoni pake mwenyewe, bali mtu maskini mwenye ufahamu atamfichua.
Ekegusii: Omonto omonda nigo akwerengereria ng’a nomong’aini are, korende omonto omotaka ore n’okomanya nigo aramotuke amomanye.

English: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory; but when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.
Kiswahili: Mwenye haki ashindapo, kuna furaha kubwa, bali waovu watawalapo, watu hujificha.
Ekegusii: Ekero abanyene oboronge babuire, okoiririata okonge nigo gokobao, korende ekero abakori amabe bakobua, abanto nigo bakwebisa.

English: He who conceals his sins doesn’t prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them finds mercy.
Kiswahili: Yeye afichaye dhambi zake hatafanikiwa, bali yeyote aziungamaye na kuziacha hupata rehema.
Ekegusii: Omonto okobisa ebibe biaye tagosesenigwa, korende oyo okobiorokia na kobitiga narorerwe amaabera.

English: Blessed is the man who always fears; but one who hardens his heart falls into trouble.
Kiswahili: Amebarikiwa mtu ambaye siku zote humcha Bwana, bali yeye afanyaye moyo wake kuwa mgumu huangukia kwenye taabu.
Ekegusii: Nasesenirie omonto omoirogete Omonene botambe, korende oyo okong’etie enkoro yaye nanyore emechando eramosirie.

English: As a roaring lion or a charging bear, so is a wicked ruler over helpless people.
Kiswahili: Kama simba angurumaye au dubu ashambuliaye, ndivyo alivyo mtu mwovu atawalaye wanyonge.
Ekegusii: Omogambi omokaayayu okogambera abanto abataka nigo anga buna endo ekoruma, gose edubu yagechiigwe.

English: A tyrannical ruler lacks judgment. One who hates ill-gotten gain will have long days.
Kiswahili: Mtawala dhalimu hana akili, bali yeye achukiaye mapato ya udhalimu atafurahia maisha marefu.
Ekegusii: Omogambi otari n’obong’aini nigo are omochaandi omotindi, korende oria ogechete okonyora ebitooki bitari bi’oboronge, nigo akogeenderera kogamba ase amatuko amaange.

English: A man who is tormented by blood guilt will be a fugitive until death. No one will support him.
Kiswahili: Mtu mwenye kusumbuliwa na hatia ya kuua atakuwa mtoro mpaka kufa; mtu yeyote na asimsaidie.
Ekegusii: Onye omonto oritoereirwe n’okomocha kw’ogoitera amanyinga y’omonto onde, tiga abe okona‐gotama goika akwe, na onde tagokoonya omonto oyio.

English: Whoever walks blamelessly is kept safe; but one with perverse ways will fall suddenly.
Kiswahili: Yeye ambaye mwenendo wake hauna lawama hulindwa salama, bali yeye ambaye njia zake ni potovu ataanguka ghafula.
Ekegusii: Omonto otari na komocha ase chiinchera chiaye natoorigwe; korende oyore omokorekanu ase chiinchera chiaye nasire ase eyemo y’echio.

English: One who works his land will have an abundance of food; but one who chases fantasies will have his fill of poverty.
Kiswahili: Yeye alimaye shamba lake atakuwa na chakula tele, bali yule afuataye mambo ya upuzi atakuwa na umaskini wa kumtosha.
Ekegusii: Omonto ogokora emeremo ase omogondo oye ’nanyore endagera enyinge, korende oyokobwatia emeroberio etagwenereti nigo arabe omotaka omoraboku.

English: A faithful man is rich with blessings; but one who is eager to be rich will not go unpunished.
Kiswahili: Mtu mwaminifu atabarikiwa sana, bali yeye atamaniye kupata utajiri kwa haraka hataacha kuadhibiwa.
Ekegusii: Omonto ore n’enkoro endonge ’nanyore ogosesenigwa okonge, korende oyo okoayerera ase okoba omonda takomocha konyora egesusuro.

English: To show partiality is not good, yet a man will do wrong for a piece of bread.
Kiswahili: Kuonyesha upendeleo si vizuri, hata hivyo mtu atafanya kosa kwa kipande cha mkate.
Ekegusii: Ase engencho y’agasamunye k’omogati omonto nigo agwesaria ase ogwanchereria. Korende, tari buya gokora ogwanchereria nonya ’ng’ake.

English: A stingy man hurries after riches, and doesn’t know that poverty waits for him.
Kiswahili: Mtu mchoyo ana tamaa ya kupata utajiri, naye hana habari kuwa umaskini unamngojea.
Ekegusii: Omonto omwegimeria nigo akoayerera koba omonda, gose tari korengereria ng’a obotaka ’mbomonyooore.

English: One who rebukes a man will afterward find more favor than one who flatters with the tongue.
Kiswahili: Yeye amkemeaye mtu mwishoni hupata kibali zaidi, kuliko mwenye maneno ya kusifu isivyostahili.
Ekegusii: Omonto ogotogonyera oyo oiranire magega ase okomoorongeyia ’nanyoore ogwancherwa kobua oria okomong’aina namang’ana amansu.

English: Whoever robs his father or his mother and says, “It’s not wrong,” is a partner with a destroyer.
Kiswahili: Yeye amwibiaye babaye au mamaye na kusema, “Si kosa,” yeye ni mwenzi wa yule aharibuye.
Ekegusii: Omonto okoura ise gose ng’ina enibo yabo, erio oteeba, “Ebi tibiri ebibe,” oyio nigo are omogisangio bw’oyogosiria.

English: One who is greedy stirs up strife; but one who trusts in Yahweh will prosper.
Kiswahili: Mtu mwenye tamaa huchochea fitina, bali yule amtegemeaye Bwana atafanikiwa.
Ekegusii: Omonto ore n’endamwamu nigo agoseegeta eriomana, korende oyosemeretie Omonene ’natenenkigwe.

English: One who trusts in himself is a fool; but one who walks in wisdom is kept safe.
Kiswahili: Yeye ajitumainiaye mwenyewe ni mpumbavu, bali yeye atembeaye katika hekima hulindwa salama.
Ekegusii: Oyobwesemeretie ere omonyene, oyio nomoriri, korende oyo okobwatia obong’aini natoorigwe.

English: One who gives to the poor has no lack; but one who closes his eyes will have many curses.
Kiswahili: Yeye ampaye maskini hatapungukiwa na kitu chochote, bali yeye awafumbiaye maskini macho hupata laana nyingi.
Ekegusii: Omonto ogokoonya abataka takoremerwa, korende oyo ogotuba amaiso aye ng’a tarora abataka ’nanyore okoragererigwa okonge.

English: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves; but when they perish, the righteous thrive.
Kiswahili: Wakati waovu watawalapo, watu huenda mafichoni, bali waovu wanapoangamia, wenye haki hufanikiwa.
Ekegusii: Ekero abakori amabe bakogamba, abanto nigo bakwebisa, korende ekero basiriigwe, abanyaboronge nigo bakomentekana.

English: He who is often rebuked and stiffens his neck will be destroyed suddenly, with no remedy.
Kiswahili: Mtu anayeendelea kuwa na shingo ngumu baada ya maonyo mengi, ataangamia ghafula, wala hapati dawa.
Ekegusii: Omonto okona gokurerwa botambe ase okorongeigwa, korende okong’ia ebigoti, oyio nasirigwe mobosokano, tagokonywa.

English: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; but when the wicked rule, the people groan.
Kiswahili: Wenye haki wanapostawi, watu hufurahi; waovu watawalapo, watu hulia kwa huzuni.
Ekegusii: Ekero abanyene oboronge bakogaamba, abanto nigo bakoba n’omogooko, korende ekero abakori amabe bakogaamba, abanto nigo bagochaandeka na kweumia.

English: Whoever loves wisdom brings joy to his father; but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.
Kiswahili: Mtu apendaye hekima huleta furaha kwa baba yake, bali aambatanaye na makahaba hutapanya mali yake.
Ekegusii: Oyo bwanchete obong’aini nigo akomogokia ise, korende oyogotaara amo nabakungu abatayayi nigo agosiria chinibo chiaye.

English: The king by justice makes the land stable, but he who takes bribes tears it down.
Kiswahili: Kwa haki mfalme huipa nchi uthabiti, bali mfalme aliye na tamaa ya rushwa huiangamiza.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti ogokora ay’oboronge nigo akogera ense yaye yageenderera gotenena bokong’u, korende oyo okorigia amaaki nigo akoyeiyeria.

English: A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet.
Kiswahili: Yeyote amsifuye jirani yake isivyostahili, anautandaza wavu kuitega miguu yake.
Ekegusii: Omonto okong’aina omonto onde namang’ana amansu, oyio nigo agwetegera omotego ase amagoro aye.

English: An evil man is snared by his sin, but the righteous can sing and be glad.
Kiswahili: Mtu mbaya hutegwa na dhambi yake mwenyewe bali mwenye haki huweza kuimba na kufurahi.
Ekegusii: Omonto omonyabibe nigo agotegwa nobosareku bwaye, korende omonyene oboronge nigo agoteera n’omogooko na gochenga.

English: The righteous care about justice for the poor. The wicked aren’t concerned about knowledge.
Kiswahili: Mwenye haki hujali haki kwa ajili ya maskini, bali mwovu hajishughulishi na hilo.
Ekegusii: Omonyene oboronge nigo agwechaandera oboronge bw’abataka, korende omokori amabe tamanyeti kende.

English: Mockers stir up a city, but wise men turn away anger.
Kiswahili: Wenye mzaha huuchochea mji, bali watu wenye hekima hugeuzia mbali hasira.
Ekegusii: Abanyacheche nigo bakoburukania omochie, korende abanto abang’aini nigo bagokendia ekeririanda.

English: If a wise man goes to court with a foolish man, the fool rages or scoffs, and there is no peace.
Kiswahili: Kama mwenye hekima akienda mahakamani na mpumbavu, mpumbavu hukasirika na kudhihaki, wala hakuna amani.
Ekegusii: Ekero omonto omong’aini akoamererania nomoriri, oria omoriri nigo akogechigwa na goseka, tari gokira-kiri.

English: The bloodthirsty hate a man of integrity; and they seek the life of the upright.
Kiswahili: Watu wamwagao damu humchukia mtu mwadilifu na hutafuta kumuua mtu mnyofu.
Ekegusii: Abanto bare nerang’o y’ogoitera amanyinga nigo bakogecha oyo otari na komocha, korende abare ne chinkoro chindonge nigo bakomorenda.

English: A fool vents all of his anger, but a wise man brings himself under control.
Kiswahili: Mpumbavu huonyesha hasira yake yote, bali mwenye hekima hujizuia.
Ekegusii: Omonto omoriri nigo agosokia endamwamu yaye yonsi, korende oyore omong’aini nigo akoyetanga otoerera.

English: If a ruler listens to lies, all of his officials are wicked.
Kiswahili: Kama mtawala akisikiliza uongo, maafisa wake wote huwa waovu.
Ekegusii: Omogambi aise gwancha amang’ana y’oborimo, abasomba baye bonsi nigo barabe abakori amabe.

English: The poor man and the oppressor have this in common: Yahweh gives sight to the eyes of both.
Kiswahili: Mtu maskini na mtu anayeonea wanafanana kwa jambo hili: Bwana hutia nuru macho yao wote wawili.
Ekegusii: Omotaka na omochaandi nigo bamenyete amo; Omonene nere okobaa bonsi babere oborabu bw’amaiso.

English: The king who fairly judges the poor, his throne shall be established forever.
Kiswahili: Kama mfalme akiwaamua maskini kwa haki, kiti chake cha enzi kitakuwa thabiti siku zote.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti okogambera abataka ase oboronge, obogambi bwaye ’mbogeenderere gotenena bokong’u.

English: The rod of correction gives wisdom, but a child left to himself causes shame to his mother.
Kiswahili: Fimbo ya maonyo hutia hekima, bali mtoto aliyeachiwa bila maonyo humwaibisha mama yake.
Ekegusii: Ekeranya na ogotogonyera ase okorongeyia nigo bikorenta obong’aini, korende omwana ogotigwa okora buna anchete, nigo akorentera ng’ina obosooku.

English: When the wicked increase, sin increases; but the righteous will see their downfall.
Kiswahili: Wakati waovu wanapostawi, pia dhambi vivyo hivyo, lakini wenye haki wataliona anguko lao.
Ekegusii: Ekero abakori amabe bakomentekana, ogosaria nigo gokomentekana, korende abanyene oboronge ’mbarore okogwa kw’abwo.

English: Correct your son, and he will give you peace; yes, he will bring delight to your soul.
Kiswahili: Mrudi mwanao, naye atakupa amani, atakufurahisha nafsi yako.
Ekegusii: Rongeyia omwana oo omomura, ere nakorentere ogotimoka, nigo araarente omosasoko omonge ase enkoro yao.

English: Where there is no revelation, the people cast off restraint; but one who keeps the law is blessed.
Kiswahili: Mahali pasipo na ufunuo, watu kujizuia, bali ana heri mtu yule aishikaye sheria.
Ekegusii: Ase okomaanorerwa kw’amang’ana gotari, abanto tibari gwetanga gokora amabe, korende nasesenirie oyo obwatete amachiiko.

English: A servant can’t be corrected by words. Though he understands, yet he will not respond.
Kiswahili: Mtumishi hawezi kuonywa kwa maneno matupu, ajapoelewa, hataitikia.
Ekegusii: Amang’ana oka amasa takorongeyia omosomba, ekiagera n’aba oyamanyete, takoyaigwera.

English: Do you see a man who is hasty in his words? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
Kiswahili: Je, unamwona mtu azungumzaye kwa haraka? Kuna matumaini zaidi kwa mpumbavu kuliko yeye.
Ekegusii: Oise korora omonto ore omwango ase ogokwana, ogosemeria ’nkore ase omonto omoriri kobua ase oyio.

English: He who pampers his servant from youth will have him become a son in the end.
Kiswahili: Kama mtu akimdekeza mtumishi wake tangu ujanani, atamletea sikitiko mwishoni.
Ekegusii: Omonto ogotuga omosomba oye na omoa ebinto bionsi aganetie korwa obwana bwaye, omosomba oyio nabo araire omwando oye.

English: An angry man stirs up strife, and a wrathful man abounds in sin.
Kiswahili: Mtu mwenye hasira huchochea ugomvi, naye mtu mwenye hasira ya haraka hutenda dhambi nyingi.
Ekegusii: Omonto obwate endamwamu nigo agoseegeta eriomana, na oyo okogechigwa nigo akorenta ogosaria okonge.

English: A man’s pride brings him low, but one of lowly spirit gains honor.
Kiswahili: Kiburi cha mtu humshusha, bali mtu mwenye roho ya unyenyekevu hupata heshima.
Ekegusii: Oboenenu bw’omonto nigo bokomokeeyia, korende oyore n’Omoika bw’oboitongo nigo akonyoora ogosikwa okonene.

English: Whoever is an accomplice of a thief is an enemy of his own soul. He takes an oath, but dares not testify.
Kiswahili: Anayekubaliana na mwizi ni adui wa nafsi yake mwenyewe; huapishwa lakini hathubutu kushuhudia.
Ekegusii: Omonto ore omogisangio bw’omoibi nigo ageechete obogima bwaye obonyene; nigo akoigwa ogotianerwa gw’okoragereria, korende okira takoorokia gento.

English: The fear of man proves to be a snare, but whoever puts his trust in Yahweh is kept safe.
Kiswahili: Kuwaogopa watu huwa ni mtego, bali yeyote amtumainiaye Bwana atakuwa salama.
Ekegusii: Okobairoka Mwanyabaanto nigo gokoba omotego, korende omonto omosemeretie Omonene nigo arendire buya.

English: Many seek the ruler’s favor, but a man’s justice comes from Yahweh.
Kiswahili: Wengi hutafuta kusikilizwa na mtawala, bali mtu hupata haki kutoka kwa Bwana.
Ekegusii: Abanto abange nigo bakorigia ogwancherwa gokorwa ase omogambi, korende kera omonto nigo akonyora oboronge korwa ase Omonene.

English: A dishonest man detests the righteous, and the upright in their ways detest the wicked.
Kiswahili: Mwenye haki huwachukia sana wasio waaminifu; waovu huwachukia sana wenye haki.
Ekegusii: Omonto otari omooronge nigo are okogechia ase oyore omooronge, na oyore n’enkoro endonge nigo are okogechia ase omokori amabe.

English: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, the revelation: the man says to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:
Kiswahili: Misemo ya Aguri mwana wa Yake, usia: Huyu mtu alimwambia Ithieli, naam, kwa Ithieli na kwa Ukali:
Ekegusii: Aya naro amang’ana y’Aguri, mosinto o Yake o Masa. Omonto oyio agateebia Itieli na Ukali:

English: “Surely I am the most ignorant man, and don’t have a man’s understanding.
Kiswahili: “Mimi ni mjinga kuliko wanadamu wote; sina ufahamu wa kibinadamu.
Ekegusii: Ekeene, inche nigo inde omoriri otagwenereti korokwa omonto, gose timbwati obomanyi bwa Mwanyabaanto.

English: I have not learned wisdom, neither do I have the knowledge of the Holy One.
Kiswahili: Sijajifunza hekima, wala sina maarifa ya kumjua yeye Aliye Mtakatifu.
Ekegusii: Inche tineorokereretie obong’aini, erinde imomanye oyore Omochenu.

English: Who has ascended up into heaven, and descended? Who has gathered the wind in his fists? Who has bound the waters in his garment? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his son’s name, if you know?
Kiswahili: Ni nani ameshapanda mbinguni na kushuka? Ni nani ameshakusanya upepo kwenye vitanga vya mikono yake? Ni nani ameshafungia maji kwenye nguo yake? Ni nani ameimarisha miisho yote ya dunia? Jina lake ni nani, na mwanawe anaitwa nani? Niambie kama unajua!
Ekegusii: Ning’o oriinete gochia igoro na goika gocha aa inse? Ning’o osangereirie omwaga ase enkundi yaye? Ning’o obwatire amaache na koyaboa ase eanga yaye? Ning’o okong’etie chinsinyo chionsi chi’ense? Inaki oyio akorokwa, na omwana oye naki akorokwa? Nteebia onye koyamanyete!

English: “Every word of God is flawless. He is a shield to those who take refuge in him.
Kiswahili: “Kila neno la Mungu ni kamilifu; yeye ni ngao kwa wale wanaomkimbilia.
Ekegusii: Kera ring’ana ria Nyasae nigo rienekirie ng’a neri’ekeene. Ere nenguba ase abwo bakomotamera, barendwe.

English: Don’t you add to his words, lest he reprove you, and you be found a liar.
Kiswahili: Usiongeze kwenye maneno yake, ama atakukemea na kukuthibitisha kuwa mwongo.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa komenta kende ase amang’ana aye, nigo arabaise kogotogonyera, naye obe omonyaborimo.

English: “Two things I have asked of you. Don’t deny me before I die.
Kiswahili: “Ninakuomba vitu viwili, Ee Bwana; usininyime kabla sijafa:
Ekegusii: Amang’ana abere naro nagosabire, toyandina ntarakwa.

English: Remove far from me falsehood and lies. Give me neither poverty nor riches. Feed me with the food that is needful for me,
Kiswahili: Uutenge mbali nami udanganyifu na uongo; usinipe umaskini wala utajiri, bali unipe chakula cha kunitosha kila siku.
Ekegusii: Orusie korwa ase ’nde ayare abosa na oborimo. Tobaisa kong’a obotaka gose obotenenku, korende ong’e endagera engwenerete.

English: lest I be full, deny you, and say, ‘Who is Yahweh?’ or lest I be poor, and steal, and so dishonor the name of my God.
Kiswahili: Nisije nikawa na vingi vya kuzidi nikakukana na kusema, ‘Bwana ni nani?’ Au nisije nikawa maskini nikaiba, nami nikaliaibisha jina la Mungu wangu.
Ekegusii: Oise konyigotia mono, nigo ’ndakwange ’nteebe, “Omonene nere ng’o?” Gose inse koba omotaka nigo ’ndabaisa koiba na ’ndetere erieta ria Nyasae one obosooku.

English: “Don’t slander a servant to his master, lest he curse you, and you be held guilty.
Kiswahili: “Usimchongee mtumishi kwa bwana wake, asije akakulaani, ukapatilizwa kwalo.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kogenka omosomba ase omonene oye, nigo arakoragererie, erinde obe nokomocha.

English: There is a generation that curses their father, and doesn’t bless their mother.
Kiswahili: “Wako watu wale ambao huwalaani baba zao na wala hawawabariki mama zao;
Ekegusii: Ekegori ’nkere gekoragereria abaise na tikeri gosesenia abaang’ina.

English: There is a generation that is pure in their own eyes, yet are not washed from their filthiness.
Kiswahili: wale ambao ni safi machoni pao wenyewe kumbe hawakuoshwa uchafu wao;
Ekegusii: Abanto ’mbare bakwerora ng’a nabaikeranu bare, korende tibachenegeti korwa ase obobe bwabo.

English: There is a generation, oh how lofty are their eyes! Their eyelids are lifted up.
Kiswahili: wale ambao daima macho yao ni ya kiburi, ambao kutazama kwao ni kwa dharau;
Ekegusii: Abanto ’mbare bagwekaga ng’a nabaya bare na korigereria namaiso aichire nobomwenu.

English: There is a generation whose teeth are like swords, and their jaws like knives, to devour the poor from the earth, and the needy from among men.
Kiswahili: wale ambao meno yao ni panga na ambao mataya yao yamewekwa visu kuwaangamiza maskini katika nchi, na wahitaji kutoka miongoni mwa wanadamu.
Ekegusii: Abanto ’mbare babwate amaino anga emioro, ne chintakunero chi’amaino abo nigo chinga emeyio; barabwo nigo bakoria na gosiria abataka bare ase ense; nigo bakoura abaremeire bare ase abanto.

English: “The leech has two daughters: ‘Give, give.’ “There are three things that are never satisfied; four that don’t say, ‘Enough!’:
Kiswahili: “Mruba anao binti wawili waliao, ‘Nipe! Nipe!’ “Kuna vitu vitatu visivyotosheka kamwe, naam, viko vinne visivyosema, ‘Yatosha!’:
Ekegusii: Rikorominyo ’ndibwate abaiseke babere; barabwo nigo bakorangeria, “Toe, toe!” Mbire ebinto bitato bitari goisaneka; ee, mbire bine bitari goteeba ng’a biaisanekire, nabio ebi;

English: Sheol, the barren womb, the earth that is not satisfied with water, and the fire that doesn’t say, ‘Enough!’
Kiswahili: Ni kaburi, tumbo lisilozaa, nchi isiyoshiba maji kamwe, na moto, usiosema kamwe, ‘Yatosha!’
Ekegusii: aase abakuure, na enda engomba, ne riroba rirang’ete amaache, na omorero. Ebio tibiana goteeba, “Twaisanekire.”

English: “The eye that mocks at his father, and scorns obedience to his mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, the young eagles shall eat it.
Kiswahili: “Jicho lile limdhihakilo baba, lile linalodharau kumtii mama, litangʼolewa na kunguru wa bondeni, litaliwa na tai.
Ekegusii: Eriso ri’omonto ogochecheria ise na gochaaya ng’ina ndirusigwe nebigonkoru bie rigoko na ririegwe namage ye chinsoti.

English: “There are three things which are too amazing for me, four which I don’t understand:
Kiswahili: “Kuna vitu vitatu vinavyonishangaza sana, naam, vinne nisivyovielewa:
Ekegusii: Ebinto mbire bitato bire bi’ogokumia ase ’nde; ee, mbire bine ebio ’ntamanyeti, nabio ebi:

English: The way of an eagle in the air, the way of a serpent on a rock, the way of a ship in the middle of the sea, and the way of a man with a maiden.
Kiswahili: Ni mwendo wa tai katika anga, mwendo wa nyoka juu ya mwamba, mwendo wa meli katika maji makuu ya bahari, nao mwendo wa mtu pamoja na msichana.
Ekegusii: enchera y’ekeongo igoro, na ey’eng’iti igoro ase egetare, na ey’emeeri igoro ase amaache y’enyancha, na enchera omosacha akobua omoiseke.

English: “So is the way of an adulterous woman: She eats and wipes her mouth, and says, ‘I have done nothing wrong.’
Kiswahili: “Huu ndio mwendo wa mwanamke mzinzi, hula akapangusa kinywa chake na kusema, ‘Sikufanya chochote kibaya.’
Ekegusii: Eyio nenchera y’omokuungu omotomani: Nigo akoria na otinyia omonwa oye, erio oteeba, “Inche tindakora bonyaka bonde.”

English: “For three things the earth trembles, and under four, it can’t bear up:
Kiswahili: “Kwa mambo matatu nchi hutetemeka, naam, kwa mambo manne haiwezi kuvumilia:
Ekegusii: Nare amang’ana atato akonyegeria ense, ee, nare ane etanyaare koyaremereria, naro aya:

English: For a servant when he is king, a fool when he is filled with food,
Kiswahili: Mtumwa awapo mfalme, mpumbavu ashibapo chakula,
Ekegusii: Ekero omosomba akoba omorwoti, na omonto omoriri akoigota endagera,

English: for an unloved woman when she is married, and a servant who is heir to her mistress.
Kiswahili: mwanamke asiyependwa aolewapo, naye mtumishi wa kike achukuapo nafasi ya bibi yake.
Ekegusii: na ekero omoiseke otanchiri akonyuomwa, na omoiseke omosomba akoira ribaga ri’omokuungu oria agokorera emeremo.

English: “There are four things which are little on the earth, but they are exceedingly wise:
Kiswahili: “Vitu vinne duniani vilivyo vidogo, lakini vina akili nyingi sana:
Ekegusii: Mbire ebinto bine ebisinini mono ase ense, korende bire n’obong’aini obonge, nabio ebi:

English: The ants are not a strong people, yet they provide their food in the summer.
Kiswahili: Mchwa ni viumbe wenye nguvu ndogo, hata hivyo hujiwekea akiba ya chakula chao wakati wa kiangazi.
Ekegusii: Amage nigo are ebitongwa bitari ne chinguru, korende nigo akogaacha endagera yabo agocha koria engaki y’egurugura.

English: The hyraxes are but a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks.
Kiswahili: Pelele ni viumbe vyenye uwezo mdogo hata hivyo hujitengenezea nyumba zao kwenye miamba.
Ekegusii: Ebisengi tibibwati chinguru, korende nigo bikoroisia ase bikomenya ase ebitare ime.

English: The locusts have no king, yet they advance in ranks.
Kiswahili: Nzige hawana mfalme, hata hivyo huenda pamoja vikosi vikosi.
Ekegusii: Chingige tichibwati omorwoti, korende nigo chikogeendera amo emegaanda ase emegaanda.

English: You can catch a lizard with your hands, yet it is in kings’ palaces.
Kiswahili: Mjusi anaweza kushikwa kwa mkono, hata hivyo huonekana katika majumba ya kifalme.
Ekegusii: Ensagara nabo erabogorigwe nokoboko kw’omonto, korende nabo ekomenya ase chinyomba chi’abarwoti.

English: “There are three things which are stately in their march, four which are stately in going:
Kiswahili: “Viko vitu vitatu ambavyo vinapendeza katika mwendo wao, naam, vinne ambavyo hutembea kwa mwendo wa madaha:
Ekegusii: Mbire ebinto bitato bikogokia ase ogotaara kwabo, ee, mbire bine bire nogotaara okuya, nabio ebi.

English: The lion, which is mightiest among animals, and doesn’t turn away for any;
Kiswahili: simba, mwenye nguvu miongoni mwa wanyama, asiyerudi nyuma kwa chochote;
Ekegusii: Endo ere ne chinguru chinyinge kobua ching’iti chinde, na teri kwoboigwa na ng’iti ende,

English: the greyhound; the male goat; and the king against whom there is no rising up.
Kiswahili: jogoo atembeaye kwa maringo, pia beberu, naye mfalme pamoja na jeshi lake lililomzunguka.
Ekegusii: na etuoni egwesigoria, na egoree, na omorwoti okoraa abarwani baye b’esegi.

English: “If you have done foolishly in lifting up yourself, or if you have thought evil, put your hand over your mouth.
Kiswahili: “Ikiwa umefanya upumbavu na ukajitukuza mwenyewe, au kama umepanga mabaya, basi funika mdomo wako na mkono wako.
Ekegusii: Onye kwabeire omoriri na kweimokereirie igoro, gose onye kwabeire gokorengereria amabe, beeka okoboko kwao ase omonwa oo, oyotube.

English: For as the churning of milk produces butter, and the wringing of the nose produces blood, so the forcing of wrath produces strife.”
Kiswahili: Kwa maana kama vile kusukasuka maziwa hutoa siagi, na pia kule kufinya pua hutoa damu, kadhalika kuchochea hasira hutokeza ugomvi.”
Ekegusii: Amabeere agotundwa nigo akorua amaguta, na okomintontoria emioro, amanyinga nigo akoruerao. Naboigo ogoseegeta na koba nendamwamu, ayio nigo akorenta okorwana.

English: The words of King Lemuel—the revelation which his mother taught him:
Kiswahili: Misemo ya Mfalme Lemueli, usia wa mama yake aliyomfundisha:
Ekegusii: Amang’ana aya naro Lemweli omorwoti orokereretigwe na ng’ina.

English: “Oh, my son! Oh, son of my womb! Oh, son of my vows!
Kiswahili: “Ee mwanangu, ee mwana wa tumbo langu, ee mwana wa nadhiri zangu,
Ekegusii: Inaki aye omwana o’ne? Inaki aye omwana bw’enda y’ane? Ninki ndagoteebie, aye omwana bw’eira y’ane nariete?

English: Don’t give your strength to women, nor your ways to that which destroys kings.
Kiswahili: Usitumie nguvu zako kwa wanawake, uhodari wako kwa wale wanaowaharibu wafalme.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gochwara chinguru chiao ase abakungu, gose chiinchera chiao ase bare, ekiagera nigo bagosiria abarwoti.

English: It is not for kings, Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine, nor for princes to say, ‘Where is strong drink?’
Kiswahili: “Ee Lemueli, haifai wafalme, haifai wafalme kunywa mvinyo, haifai watawala kutamani sana kileo,
Ekegusii: Aye Lemweli, okonywa edivai tikogwenereti abarwoti, gose abagaambi tibaabaisa kogania ebinyugwa bigotindia.

English: lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the justice due to anyone who is afflicted.
Kiswahili: wasije wakanywa na kusahau vile sheria inavyoamuru na kuwanyima haki zao wote walioonewa.
Ekegusii: Baise konywa, nigo barebe amachiiko, na baonchorane oboronge bwa abachaandegete bonsi.

English: Give strong drink to him who is ready to perish, and wine to the bitter in soul.
Kiswahili: Wape kileo wale wanaoangamia, mvinyo wale walio na uchungu,
Ekegusii: Moe ekenyugwa kegotindia oyo ogochia gosira, na edivai ase oyio oichanete ase omoyo oye.

English: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.
Kiswahili: Wanywe na kusahau umaskini wao na wasikumbuke taabu yao tena.
Ekegusii: Tiga banywe, erinde beebe tibaabaisa kona‐koinyora emechando yabo n’obotaka bwabo.

English: Open your mouth for the mute, in the cause of all who are left desolate.
Kiswahili: “Sema kwa ajili ya wale wasioweza kujisemea, kwa ajili ya haki za wote walioachwa ukiwa.
Ekegusii: Maanora omonwa oo, okwanere rimama, orwanerere oboronge bw’abwo batigirwe bachaandegete.

English: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and serve justice to the poor and needy.”
Kiswahili: Sema na uamue kwa haki, tetea haki za maskini na wahitaji.”
Ekegusii: Maanora omonwa oo, ogambe ebiina bi’ekeene, orwanerere oboronge bw’abataka na obaremeire.

English: Who can find a worthy woman? For her value is far above rubies.
Kiswahili: Mke mwenye sifa nzuri, ni nani awezaye kumpata? Yeye ni wa thamani sana kuliko marijani.
Ekegusii: Ning’o oranyaare konyora omokungu omuya? Omokungu omuya nigo are n’engeencho enene kobua amagena ye rigori rinene.

English: The heart of her husband trusts in her. He shall have no lack of gain.
Kiswahili: Mume wake anamwamini kikamilifu wala hakosi kitu chochote cha thamani.
Ekegusii: Enkoro y’omosaacha oye nigo emwegenete, gose omosacha oyio takoremerwa konyora ebitoki.

English: She does him good, and not harm, all the days of her life.
Kiswahili: Humtendea mumewe mema, wala si mabaya, siku zote za maisha yake.
Ekegusii: Ase obogima bwaye bwonsi omokungu oyio nigo agokorera omosacha oye amaya, gose tari korenta amabe ase are.

English: She seeks wool and flax, and works eagerly with her hands.
Kiswahili: Huchagua sufu na kitani naye hufanya kazi kwa mikono yenye bidii.
Ekegusii: Omokungu oyio nigo akorigia amarionya e ching’ondi ne chiusi chi’egatani, okora emeremo namaboko aye ore n’omoyo omuya.

English: She is like the merchant ships. She brings her bread from afar.
Kiswahili: Yeye ni kama meli za biashara akileta chakula chake kutoka mbali.
Ekegusii: Nigo anga chimeeri chi’abaonchoreria; nigo akorenta endagera korwa ase ense y’aare.

English: She rises also while it is yet night, gives food to her household, and portions for her servant girls.
Kiswahili: Yeye huamka kungali bado giza huwapa jamaa yake chakula na mafungu kwa watumishi wake wa kike.
Ekegusii: Nigo akoboka kobore botuko, oroiseria abanto b’enyomba yaye endagera, na oa abasomba baye abaiseke eyebatungetie.

English: She considers a field, and buys it. With the fruit of her hands, she plants a vineyard.
