Kiswahili: Huangalia shamba na kulinunua, kutokana na mapato yake hupanda shamba la mizabibu.
Ekegusii: Nigo akorigia omogondo oyogora, na korwa ase ebitoki bi’emeremo y’amaboko aye nigo agosimeka emesabibu.

English: She arms her waist with strength, and makes her arms strong.
Kiswahili: Hufanya kazi zake kwa nguvu, mikono yake ina nguvu kwa ajili ya kazi zake.
Ekegusii: Nigo akweboyia chinguru buna orokini, okora emeremo emekong’u n’amaboko aye.

English: She perceives that her merchandise is profitable. Her lamp doesn’t go out by night.
Kiswahili: Huona kwamba biashara yake ina faida, wala taa yake haizimiki usiku.
Ekegusii: Nigo akorora ng’a emeremo yaye nigo ekorenta ebitoki, na etaaya yaye teri korima nyomba mwaye botuko.

English: She lays her hands to the distaff, and her hands hold the spindle.
Kiswahili: Huweka mikono yake kwenye pia, navyo vidole vyake hushikilia kijiti chenye uzi.
Ekegusii: Nigo abwate egekorero akoroiseria chiusi namaboko aye na egete agochiranderera nebiara biaye.

English: She opens her arms to the poor; yes, she extends her hands to the needy.
Kiswahili: Huwanyooshea maskini mikono yake na kuwakunjulia wahitaji vitanga vyake.
Ekegusii: Nigo akorambora okoboko kwaye okonya abataka, ee, nabaremeire nigo akobaramborera amaboko aye.

English: She is not afraid of the snow for her household, for all her household are clothed with scarlet.
Kiswahili: Theluji ishukapo, hana hofu kwa ajili ya watu wa nyumbani mwake, kwa maana wote wamevikwa nguo za kutia joto.
Ekegusii: Ere tari kwoboa chingaki chi’obokendu, ekiagera abanto bonsi b’enyomba yaye nigo babwate chianga chie riberera chiroisirie korwa ase chiusi chimonyinga.

English: She makes for herself carpets of tapestry. Her clothing is fine linen and purple.
Kiswahili: Hutengeneza mazulia ya urembo ya kufunika kitanda chake, yeye huvaa kitani safi na urujuani.
Ekegusii: Omokungu oyio nigo akweroiseria ebirarero; chianga chiaye nigo chiroisirie korwa ase egatani engiya ne chiusi chimbariri.

English: Her husband is respected in the gates, when he sits among the elders of the land.
Kiswahili: Mume wake anaheshimiwa kwenye lango la mji, aketipo miongoni mwa wazee wa nchi.
Ekegusii: Omosacha bw’omokuungu oyio nigo amanyekanete ase ebiita bi’omochie, agwo ase agoikaransa ogaamba ebiina amo nabagaaka b’ense eyio.

English: She makes linen garments and sells them, and delivers sashes to the merchant.
Kiswahili: Hutengeneza mavazi ya kitani na kuyauza, naye huwauzia wafanyabiashara mishipi.
Ekegusii: Omokungu oyio nigo akoroisia chianga chi’egatani engiya, ochioonia; naende nigo akoroisia chinkini, ochiooneria abaonchoreria bande.

English: Strength and dignity are her clothing. She laughs at the time to come.
Kiswahili: Amevikwa nguvu na heshima, anaweza kucheka bila kuwa na hofu kwa siku zijazo.
Ekegusii: Nigo akweboyia chinguru na amasikani, na igo nabe nomogooko ase chingaki chigochi‐gocha.

English: She opens her mouth with wisdom. Kind instruction is on her tongue.
Kiswahili: Huzungumza kwa hekima na mafundisho ya kuaminika yapo ulimini mwake.
Ekegusii: Amorokererio akorua ase omonwa oye nigo are ay’obong’aini n’obuya, amo n’obwororo nigo bore ase oromeme rw’aye.

English: She looks well to the ways of her household, and doesn’t eat the bread of idleness.
Kiswahili: Huangalia mambo ya nyumbani mwake wala hali chakula cha uvivu.
Ekegusii: Nigo akoroberia buya amang’ana y’enyomba yaye, gose tari koria endagera atari gokorera emeremo.

English: Her children rise up and call her blessed. Her husband also praises her:
Kiswahili: Watoto wake huamka na kumwita aliyebarikiwa, mumewe pia humsifu, akisema:
Ekegusii: Abana baye nigo bakoboka bamoroka “Oyosesenirie”, naboigo n’omosaacha oye nigo akomotogia, oteeba.

English: “Many women do noble things, but you excel them all.”
Kiswahili: “Wanawake wengi hufanya vitu vyenye sifa nzuri, lakini wewe umewapita wote.”
Ekegusii: “Abakungu abange bakorire ayare amaya mono, korende aye kwababuire bonsi.”

English: Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain; but a woman who fears Yahweh, she shall be praised.
Kiswahili: Kujipamba ili kuvutia ni udanganyifu na uzuri unapita upesi, bali mwanamke anayemcha Bwana atasifiwa.
Ekegusii: Obonyakieni nigo bokong’ainereria, na ekieni ekiya nigo kere bosa, korende omokungu omoirogete Omonene, oyio nere oranyaare gotogigwa.

English: Give her of the fruit of her hands! Let her works praise her in the gates!
Kiswahili: Mpe thawabu anayostahili, nazo kazi zake na zimletee sifa kwenye lango la mji.
Ekegusii: Kae omokungu oyio okwama kw’emeremo y’amaboko aye, na tiga atogigwe agwo ase ebiita ase ogokora kwaye gwonsi.

English: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:
Kiswahili: Maneno ya Mhubiri, mwana wa Daudi, mfalme huko Yerusalemu:
Ekegusii: Aya naro amang’ana ’omorandia mosinto o Daudi, omorwoti o Yerusalemu.

English: “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher; “Vanity of vanities, all is vanity.”
Kiswahili: “Ubatili mtupu! Ubatili mtupu!” Mhubiri anasema. “Ubatili mtupu! Kila kitu ni ubatili.”
Ekegusii: Omorandia nigo agoteeba: Mbosa na bosa kegima, mbosa, bosa. Amang’ana onsi mbosa.

English: What does man gain from all his labor in which he labors under the sun?
Kiswahili: Mwanadamu anafaidi nini kutokana na kazi yake yote anayotaabikia chini ya jua?
Ekegusii: Mbitoki ki Mwanyabaanto akonyora ase okwerosia gokora emeremo emekong’u aiga inse y’erioba?

English: One generation goes, and another generation comes; but the earth remains forever.
Kiswahili: Vizazi huja na vizazi hupita, lakini dunia inadumu milele.
Ekegusii: Ekegori ekemo nigo kegoeta, na ekende giacha, korende ense nigo egendererete kobao goika kare na kare.

English: The sun also rises, and the sun goes down, and hurries to its place where it rises.
Kiswahili: Jua huchomoza na jua huzama, nalo huharakisha kurudi mawioni.
Ekegusii: Erioba nigo rigosoka naende riarimera, erio riaayerera gochia aase rigosoka korwa.

English: The wind goes toward the south, and turns around to the north. It turns around continually as it goes, and the wind returns again to its courses.
Kiswahili: Upepo huvuma kuelekea kusini na kugeukia kaskazini, hurudia mzunguko huo huo, daima ukirudia njia yake.
Ekegusii: Embeo nigo ekogusa gochia Irianyi, naende yaonchoka yagusa gochia sugusu; nigo ekona‐goetanana yagenderera kogusa, naende yagenderera goetanana naende yairana.

English: All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full. To the place where the rivers flow, there they flow again.
Kiswahili: Mito yote hutiririka baharini, hata hivyo bahari kamwe haijai. Mahali mito inapotoka, huko hurudi tena.
Ekegusii: Chindooche chionsi nigo chikogenda ase enyancha, korende tiyana goichora. Amache ayio nigo akoirana gochia ase chindooche echio chiachakerete, naende agenderera kogenda.

English: All things are full of weariness beyond uttering. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
Kiswahili: Vitu vyote vinachosha, zaidi kuliko mtu anavyoweza kusema. Jicho kamwe halitosheki kutazama, wala sikio halishibi kusikia.
Ekegusii: Amang’ana onsi agokorwa nigo akorenta omooroso otanyare gokwaneka. Amaiso tari goisaneka naya akorora, na amato tari goisaneka naya akoigwa.

English: That which has been is that which shall be, and that which has been done is that which shall be done; and there is no new thing under the sun.
Kiswahili: Kile kilichokuwepo kitakuwepo tena, kile kilichofanyika kitafanyika tena, hakuna kilicho kipya chini ya jua.
Ekegusii: Aya arengeo kare, naro agochia kobao naende. Aya akoregete kare, naro agochia gokoreka naende. Ande tari are amayia inse y’erioba.

English: Is there a thing of which it may be said, “Behold, this is new”? It has been long ago, in the ages which were before us.
Kiswahili: Kuna kitu chochote ambacho mtu anaweza kusema, “Tazama! Kitu hiki ni kipya”? Kilikuwepo tangu zamani za kale, kilikuwepo kabla ya wakati wetu.
Ekegusii: Inee! Ing’ana rinde ndireo rigokwanwa ng’a neriyia? Yaya. Kera ring’ana nao riarenge korwa kare, intwe konya totarabao.

English: There is no memory of the former; neither shall there be any memory of the latter that are to come, among those that shall come after.
Kiswahili: Hakuna kumbukumbu ya watu wa zamani, hata na wale ambao hawajaja bado hawatakumbukwa na wale watakaofuata baadaye.
Ekegusii: Amang’ana aetire takoinyorwa, gose ayagochi‐gocha takoinyorwa nabwo bakorwa magega.

English: I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
Kiswahili: Mimi, Mhubiri, nilikuwa mfalme wa Israeli katika Yerusalemu.
Ekegusii: Inche omorandia nigo narenge omorwoti igoro ase Abaisraeli, agwo Yerusalemu.

English: I applied my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under the sky. It is a heavy burden that God has given to the sons of men to be afflicted with.
Kiswahili: Nilitumia muda wangu wote kujifunza na kuvumbua kwa hekima yote yanayofanyika chini ya mbingu. Jinsi gani Mungu ameweka mzigo mzito juu ya wanadamu!
Ekegusii: Nkerua nenkoro yane korigia na komanya ase obong’aini amang’ana onsi agokoreka inse y’erioba. Nigo ere emeremo etari y’omogooko Nyasae aeire Mwanyabaanto bechande ase okoyekora.

English: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and behold, all is vanity and a chasing after wind.
Kiswahili: Nimeshaona mambo yote yanayotendeka chini ya jua, hayo yote ni ubatili, hii ni kukimbiza upepo.
Ekegusii: Narigereirie kera egento kegokorwa inse y’erioba, narorire ng’a bionsi nigo bire bosa; nigo enga buna okominyokia embeo.

English: That which is crooked can’t be made straight; and that which is lacking can’t be counted.
Kiswahili: Kilichopindika hakiwezi kunyooshwa, kile ambacho hakipo haiwezekani kukihesabu.
Ekegusii: Egento giachiire bogeka tigekorongeigwa, na ekiaremire tigekobareka.

English: I said to myself, “Behold, I have obtained for myself great wisdom above all who were before me in Jerusalem. Yes, my heart has had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.”
Kiswahili: Niliwaza mwenyewe, “Tazama, nimekua na kuongezeka katika hekima kuliko yeyote aliyewahi kutawala Yerusalemu kabla yangu. Nimekuwa na uzoefu mkubwa wa hekima na maarifa.”
Ekegusii: Nkerengereria inche omonyene erio ngateeba, “Nenyoreire obong’aini obonge kobua abwo bonsi bantang’anerete kogamba agwo Yerusalemu. Enkoro yane yanyorire obong’aini obonge na okomanya okonge.”

English: I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also was a chasing after wind.
Kiswahili: Ndipo nilipojitahidi kufahamu kutofautisha hekima, wazimu na upumbavu, lakini nikatambua hata hili nalo ni kukimbiza upepo.
Ekegusii: Naende nkerua nenkoro yane komanya goatanana gati y’echisemi, n’oboriri, obong’aini na obobarimo, korende nigo nanyorete ng’a ayio onsi akominyokerwa konyorwa nigo are buna embeo bosa.

English: For in much wisdom is much grief; and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.
Kiswahili: Kwa kuwa hekima nyingi huleta huzuni kubwa; maarifa yanapoongezeka, masikitiko yanaongezeka.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera ase obong’aini obonge bore, nao omoichano omonge ore, na omonto okomenta chisemi, nigo akomenta obororo.

English: I said in my heart, “Come now, I will test you with mirth; therefore enjoy pleasure;” and behold, this also was vanity.
Kiswahili: Nikafikiri moyoni mwangu, “Haya basi, nitakujaribu kwa anasa nione ni lipi lililo jema.” Lakini hilo nalo likaonekana ni ubatili.
Ekegusii: Ngakwana nenkoro yane, ngateba, “Bono ninteeme ndore naki omogooko ore, imbe nkwegokia omonyene.” Korende nonya nayio onsi nigo arenge bosa.

English: I said of laughter, “It is foolishness;” and of mirth, “What does it accomplish?”
Kiswahili: Nikasema, “Kicheko nacho ni upumbavu. Nayo matokeo ya anasa ni nini?”
Ekegusii: Nkanyora ng’a amaseko nigo are obobarimo, na omogooko tori gokora gento kende ekiya.

English: I searched in my heart how to cheer my flesh with wine, my heart yet guiding me with wisdom, and how to lay hold of folly, until I might see what it was good for the sons of men that they should do under heaven all the days of their lives.
Kiswahili: Nikajaribu kujifurahisha kwa mvinyo na kukumbatia upumbavu, huku bado akili yangu inaniongoza kwa hekima. Nilitaka kuona ni lipi bora watu wafanye kwa siku chache wanazoishi chini ya mbingu.
Ekegusii: Ekero ebirengererio biane biarenge koraagwa nobong’aini, nkagania kogokia omobere one nekenyugwa ki’edivai, nkarigia kobwatia oboriri obwo, erinde ndore ayare amaya agwenerete Mwanyabaanto bakore inse y’erioba, ase amatuko ayio amake bagendererete koba moyo.

English: I made myself great works. I built myself houses. I planted myself vineyards.
Kiswahili: Nikafanya miradi mikubwa: Nikajijengea majumba na kulima mashamba ya mizabibu.
Ekegusii: Ngakora emeremo emenene; nkeagachera chinyomba na gwesimekera emesabibu ase emegondo.

English: I made myself gardens and parks, and I planted trees in them of all kinds of fruit.
Kiswahili: Nikatengeneza bustani na viwanja vya starehe nikaotesha huko kila aina ya miti ya matunda.
Ekegusii: Nkeroiseria emegondo na emegondo ende y’amatunda, erio ngasimeka emete y’amatunda ao ao.

English: I made myself pools of water, to water the forest where trees were grown.
Kiswahili: Nikajenga mabwawa ya kukusanya maji ya kunyweshea hii miti iliyokuwa inastawi vizuri.
Ekegusii: Nkeroiseria amatibo ase nare korusia amaache nasiarera emete egokina ase rinani.

English: I bought male servants and female servants, and had servants born in my house. I also had great possessions of herds and flocks, above all who were before me in Jerusalem.
Kiswahili: Nikanunua watumwa wa kiume na wa kike na watumwa wengine walizaliwa nyumbani mwangu. Pia nilikuwa na makundi ya ngʼombe, kondoo na mbuzi kuliko mtu yeyote aliyewahi kuishi Yerusalemu kabla yangu.
Ekegusii: Nkagora abasomba, abasacha na abakungu; abwo bakanyiborera abasomba bande ase enka yane; nigo nabwate amaicho amange e chiombe, ne chimbori, ne ching’ondi, nkabua abwo bonsi bantang’anerete kogamba agwo Yerusalemu.

English: I also gathered silver and gold for myself, and the treasure of kings and of the provinces. I got myself male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of men: musical instruments of all sorts.
Kiswahili: Nikajikusanyia fedha na dhahabu, hazina za wafalme na za majimbo. Nikajipatia waimbaji wanaume na wanawake, nazo nyumba za masuria: vitu ambavyo moyo wa mwanadamu hufurahia.
Ekegusii: Boigo ngasangereria chifeta ne chitaabu, amo ne chimonga chi’abarwoti na echie chingongo chi’oborwoti bwane; ngatwara abateeri, abasacha na abakungu, naende ngatwara abakungu abange Mwanyabaanto bagosanera.

English: So I was great, and increased more than all who were before me in Jerusalem. My wisdom also remained with me.
Kiswahili: Nikawa maarufu sana kuliko mtu mwingine yeyote aliyepata kuishi Yerusalemu kabla yangu. Katika haya yote bado nikawa nina hekima.
Ekegusii: Ase ayio nkaba omonto bw’amasikani amanene, nkabua abwo bantang’anerete kogamba agwo Yerusalemu; boigo obong’aini bwane bogantigarera.

English: Whatever my eyes desired, I didn’t keep from them. I didn’t withhold my heart from any joy, for my heart rejoiced because of all my labor, and this was my portion from all my labor.
Kiswahili: Sikujinyima kitu chochote ambacho macho yangu yalikitamani, hakuna anasa ambayo niliunyima moyo wangu. Moyo wangu ulifurahia kazi zangu zote, hii ilikuwa thawabu ya kazi zangu zote.
Ekegusii: Egento kende gionsi narenge korora na gokegania tinare gwetanga gokenyora, gose tinarinete enkoro yane omogooko onde bwensi, ekiagera enkoro yane nigo yagokerete aya onsi nechanderete, na omogooko oyio noro orenge eng’eria yane y’emeremo yonsi nechanderete.

English: Then I looked at all the works that my hands had worked, and at the labor that I had labored to do; and behold, all was vanity and a chasing after wind, and there was no profit under the sun.
Kiswahili: Hata hivyo nilipokuja kuangalia yote ambayo mikono yangu ilikuwa imefanya na yale niliyotaabika kukamilisha, kila kitu kilikuwa ni ubatili, ni kukimbiza upepo; hapakuwa na faida yoyote chini ya jua.
Ekegusii: Magega y’ayio nkarengereria igoro y’emeremo eyio nakorete namaboko aane, na buna nayiechanderete. Naama! Ayio onsi nigo arenge bosa, na aya naminyokerete konyora nigo are buna embeo bosa, gose bitoki binde tibiri konyorekana inse y’erioba.

English: I turned myself to consider wisdom, madness, and folly; for what can the king’s successor do? Just that which has been done long ago.
Kiswahili: Kisha nikageuza mawazo yangu kufikiria hekima, wazimu na upumbavu. Ni nini zaidi mtu anayetawala baada ya mfalme anachoweza kufanya ambacho hakijafanywa?
Ekegusii: Nkaonchora ebirengererio biane korigereria obong’aini na obobarimo, na oboriri. Omonto oyio okobekwa oborwoti ribaga ri’oyio orengeo, ninki arakore? Tagokora kende otatiga keria oyio omotang’ani akorete.

English: Then I saw that wisdom excels folly, as far as light excels darkness.
Kiswahili: Nikaona kuwa hekima ni bora kuliko upumbavu, kama vile nuru ilivyo bora kuliko giza.
Ekegusii: Erio nkamanya ng’a obong’aini nigo bobuete oboriri, buna oborabu bobuete omosunte.

English: The wise man’s eyes are in his head, and the fool walks in darkness—and yet I perceived that one event happens to them all.
Kiswahili: Mtu mwenye hekima ana macho katika kichwa chake, lakini mpumbavu anatembea gizani; lakini nikaja kuona kwamba wote wawili hatima yao inafanana.
Ekegusii: Omonto omong’aini nigo abwate amaiso ase omotwe oye, korende omonto omoriri nigo agotaara ase omosunte; nonya naboigo, nkarora ng’a bonsi nigo bakonyorwa negento ekemo.

English: Then I said in my heart, “As it happens to the fool, so will it happen even to me; and why was I then more wise?” Then I said in my heart that this also is vanity.
Kiswahili: Kisha nikafikiri moyoni mwangu, “Hatima ya mpumbavu itanipata mimi pia. Nitafaidi nini basi kwa kuwa na hekima?” Nikasema moyoni mwangu, “Hili nalo ni ubatili.”
Ekegusii: Erio nkebooria, “Ande, amang’ana akomonyoora omoriri naro aranyore nainche, nase ki rende inche nabeire nobong’aini obonge?” Ase ayio ngeteebia ng’a aya boigo mbosa.

English: For of the wise man, even as of the fool, there is no memory forever, since in the days to come all will have been long forgotten. Indeed, the wise man must die just like the fool!
Kiswahili: Kwa maana kwa mtu mwenye hekima, kama ilivyo kwa mpumbavu, hatakumbukwa kwa muda mrefu, katika siku zijazo wote watasahaulika. Kama vile ilivyo kwa mpumbavu, mtu mwenye hekima pia lazima atakufa!
Ekegusii: Buna ere ase omonto omong’aini, naboigo ere nase omoriri, onde takogenderera koinyorwa; bonsi nigo barabe bebirwe kegima ase amatuko agochi‐gocha. Inee! Omonto omong’aini tagokwa buna oria omoriri agokwa?

English: So I hated life, because the work that is worked under the sun was grievous to me; for all is vanity and a chasing after wind.
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo nikachukia maisha, kwa sababu kazi inayofanyika chini ya jua ilikuwa masikitiko kwangu. Yote hayo ni ubatili, ni kukimbiza upepo.
Ekegusii: Ase ayio nkagecha obogima, ekiagera emeremo egokorwa inse y’erioba, nigo ekorenta obororo ase ’nde. Ayio onsi mbosa, na aya akominyokerwa konyorwa nigo are buna embeo bosa.

English: I hated all my labor in which I labored under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who comes after me.
Kiswahili: Nikachukia kila kitu nilichokuwa nimetaabikia chini ya jua, kwa sababu ni lazima nimwachie yule ajaye baada yangu.
Ekegusii: Nkagecha emeremo yonsi, eyio nabeete ngwechandera inse y’erioba, ekiagera goika ntigere omonto orambwatie ebinto ebio nakorire.

English: Who knows whether he will be a wise man or a fool? Yet he will have rule over all of my labor in which I have labored, and in which I have shown myself wise under the sun. This also is vanity.
Kiswahili: Nani ajuaye kama atakuwa ni mtu mwenye hekima au mpumbavu? Lakini hata hivyo yeye ndiye atakayetawala kazi zote ambazo nimemiminia juhudi na ustadi chini ya jua. Hili nalo ni ubatili.
Ekegusii: Ning’o omanyete gose omonto oyio nigo arabe omong’aini, gose nigo arabe omoriri? Korende oyio goika aire ebinto ebio bionsi nechandeire inde nobong’aini kobinyora inse y’erioba. Ayio boigo mbosa.

English: Therefore I began to cause my heart to despair concerning all the labor in which I had labored under the sun.
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo moyo wangu ukaanza kukata tamaa juu ya kazi yangu yote niliyoifanya kwa taabu chini ya jua.
Ekegusii: Ase ayio ngachaka goichana na gokwa omoyo ase engencho y’emeremo yonsi nechanderete inse y’erioba.

English: For there is a man whose labor is with wisdom, with knowledge, and with skillfulness; yet he shall leave it for his portion to a man who has not labored for it. This also is vanity and a great evil.
Kiswahili: Kwa kuwa mtu anaweza kufanya kazi yake kwa hekima, maarifa na ustadi, kisha analazimika kuacha vyote alivyo navyo kwa mtu mwingine ambaye hajavifanyia kazi. Hili nalo pia ni ubatili tena ni balaa kubwa.
Ekegusii: Omonto nigo agokora emeremo emekong’u nobong’aini bwaye, ne chisemi, na okomanya kwaye, konyora ebinto, korende magega yaye atigera omonto omoao otabiechanderete okwegokia nabirobio. Ayio boigo mbosa, naende mbobe mono.

English: For what does a man have of all his labor and of the striving of his heart, in which he labors under the sun?
Kiswahili: Mtu atapata nini kwa taabu yote na kuhangaika kwa bidii katika kazi anayotaabikia chini ya jua?
Ekegusii: Ngento ki omonto aranyore ekero akorire emeremo emekong’u na kwerosia mono inse y’erioba?

English: For all his days are sorrows, and his travail is grief; yes, even in the night his heart takes no rest. This also is vanity.
Kiswahili: Siku zake zote kazi yake ni maumivu na masikitiko, hata usiku akili yake haipati mapumziko. Hili nalo pia ni ubatili.
Ekegusii: Nigo akoba nobokong’u ase amatuko aye onsi are moyo, na emeremo yaye emekong’u nigo ere ey’omoichano; nonya nase obotuko obogima ebirengererio biaye tibiri gotimoka. Ayio boigo mbosa.

English: There is nothing better for a man than that he should eat and drink, and make his soul enjoy good in his labor. This also I saw, that it is from the hand of God.
Kiswahili: Hakuna kitu bora anachoweza kufanya mtu zaidi ya kula na kunywa na kuridhika katika kazi yake. Hili nalo pia, ninaona, latokana na mkono wa Mungu,
Ekegusii: Egento ekiya omonto aranyare gokora nokoria na konywa, na kogokera ebinto ebio echandeire kobinyora. Nkamanya ng’a nonya nayio nigo akorwa ase okoboko kwa Nyasae.

English: For who can eat, or who can have enjoyment, more than I?
Kiswahili: kwa sababu pasipo yeye, ni nani awezaye kula na kufurahi?
Ekegusii: Ning’o oranyare koria, gose konyora omogooko, onye tari amo n’Omonene?

English: For to the man who pleases him, God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy; but to the sinner he gives travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him who pleases God. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
Kiswahili: Kwa yule mtu anayempendeza Mungu, Mungu humpa hekima, maarifa na furaha, bali kwa mwenye dhambi Mungu humpa kazi ya kukusanya na kuhifadhi utajiri ili Mungu ampe yule anayempenda. Hili nalo pia ni ubatili, ni kukimbiza upepo.
Ekegusii: Nyasae nigo akoa omonto oyo okomogokia obong’aini, naende omoa okomanya, na omogooko, korende nigo akoa omonyabibe emeremo y’ogosangereria ebinto na kobigacha, korende omonto oria abie oria ogogetie Nyasae. Ayio boigo mbosa, na aya akominyokerwa konyorwa nigo are buna embeo bosa.

English: For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:
Kiswahili: Kuna wakati kwa ajili ya kila jambo, nayo majira kwa kila tendo chini ya mbingu:
Ekegusii: Kera egento nkere nekero kiaye, na aiga inse y’erioba kera ekegokorekana nkere nengaki yaye.

English: a time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;
Kiswahili: wakati wa kuzaliwa na wakati wa kufa, wakati wa kupanda na wakati wa kungʼoa yaliyopandwa,
Ekegusii: Nere engaki y’okoiborwa, na ey’ogokwa; engaki y’ogosimeka, na ey’ogosimora ekio giasimegetwe;

English: a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;
Kiswahili: wakati wa kuua na wakati wa kuponya, wakati wa kubomoa, na wakati wa kujenga,
Ekegusii: engaki y’ogoita, na ey’okogwenia; engaki y’ogotagora, na ey’okoagacha;

English: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
Kiswahili: wakati wa kulia na wakati wa kucheka, wakati wa kuomboleza na wakati wa kucheza,
Ekegusii: engaki y’okorera, na ey’ogoseka; engaki y’okobokia amagombo, na ey’ogotenga;

English: a time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
Kiswahili: wakati wa kutawanya mawe na wakati wa kukusanya mawe, wakati wa kukumbatia na wakati wa kutokumbatia,
Ekegusii: engaki y’ogosiarera amagena, na ey’okoyasangereria; engaki y’okoboania, na ey’ogotaboania;

English: a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;
Kiswahili: wakati wa kutafuta na wakati wa kupoteza, wakati wa kuweka na wakati wa kutupa,
Ekegusii: engaki y’okorigia, na ey’ogosiria; engaki y’okogaacha, na ey’ogotuguta;

English: a time to tear, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
Kiswahili: wakati wa kurarua na wakati wa kushona, wakati wa kunyamaza na wakati wa kuzungumza,
Ekegusii: engaki y’ogotandora, na ey’okobareera; engaki y’ogokira, na ey’ogokwana;

English: a time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.
Kiswahili: wakati wa kupenda na wakati wa kuchukia, wakati wa vita na wakati wa amani.
Ekegusii: engaki y’ogwanchana, na ey’okogechana; engaki y’esegi, na ey’omorembe.

English: What profit has he who works in that in which he labors?
Kiswahili: Mfanyakazi anapata faida gani kutokana na taabu yake?
Ekegusii: Inee! Mbitoki ki omonto akonyora ase emeremo yonsi agwechandera?

English: I have seen the burden which God has given to the sons of men to be afflicted with.
Kiswahili: Nimeona mzigo Mungu alioweka juu ya wanadamu.
Ekegusii: Narorire obokong’u obwo Nyasae aeire Mwanyabaanto bechande naborobwo.

English: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts, yet so that man can’t find out the work that God has done from the beginning even to the end.
Kiswahili: Amefanya kila kitu kiwe kizuri kwa wakati wake. Pia ameiweka hiyo milele katika mioyo ya wanadamu, wala hawawezi kutambua kwa kina yale ambayo Mungu amefanya tangu mwanzo hadi mwisho.
Ekegusii: Okorire kera egento kiabeire egeseera ase engaki yaye, naende obekire ime ase chinkoro chia Mwanyabaanto engaki etabe nomoerio. Korende nonya naboigo tibakonyara komanya aya Nyasae akorete korwa omochakano goika omoerio.

English: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice, and to do good as long as they live.
Kiswahili: Ninajua kwamba hakuna kitu bora kwa wanadamu kuliko kuwa na furaha na kutenda mema wakati wanapoishi.
Ekegusii: Namanyire ng’a gento kende tikeri kere ekiya kerabagwenere otatiga babe nomogooko, naende bakore ayare amaya ekero bare moyo.

English: Also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy good in all his labor, is the gift of God.
Kiswahili: Tena ni karama ya Mungu kila mtu apate kula na kunywa na kujiburudisha kwa mema katika kazi yake yote.
Ekegusii: Omonto kararie na konywa, naende egokie ase ebio echandeire, ekio nekeegwa kia Nyasae.

English: I know that whatever God does, it shall be forever. Nothing can be added to it, nor anything taken from it; and God has done it, that men should fear before him.
Kiswahili: Ninajua kwamba kila kitu anachokifanya Mungu kitadumu milele, hakuna kinachoweza kuongezwa au kupunguzwa. Mungu hufanya hivyo ili watu wamche yeye.
Ekegusii: Namanyire ng’a gento kende gionsi Nyasae agokora nigo gekogenderera kobao kare na kare; gento kende tigekomentwa ase ekio, gose kende tigekorusigwa korwa ase ekio. Nyasae nere okorire igo, erinde Mwanyabaanto bamoiroke.

English: That which is has been long ago, and that which is to be has been long ago. God seeks again that which is passed away.
Kiswahili: Chochote kilichopo kilishakuwepo, na kitakachokuwepo kimekwishakuwepo kabla; naye Mungu huyaita yale yaliyopita yarudi tena.
Ekegusii: Amang’ana areo bono, nao arenge korwa kare; na ayio agochia koba, boigo nao arenge korwa kare. Nyasae nigo agokora egento keria keria kiaba naende.

English: Moreover I saw under the sun, in the place of justice, that wickedness was there; and in the place of righteousness, that wickedness was there.
Kiswahili: Pia nikaona kitu kingine tena chini ya jua: Mahali pa kutolea hukumu, uovu ulikuwepo, mahali pa kupatia haki, uovu ulikuwepo.
Ekegusii: Naende nkarora aiga inse y’erioba ng’a aase ekeene na oboronge bigwenerete koba, nao obobe bore.

English: I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked; for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.”
Kiswahili: Nikafikiri moyoni mwangu, “Mungu atawaleta hukumuni wote wawili wenye haki na waovu, kwa maana kutakuwako na wakati kwa ajili ya kila jambo, wakati kwa ajili ya kila tendo.”
Ekegusii: Erio ngateeba ase enkoro yane ime ng’a Nyasae nanachere abanyaboronge ekiina, na abanyabibe boigo, ekiagera obeekire engaki ase kera ring’ana, na ase kera emeremo.

English: I said in my heart, “As for the sons of men, God tests them, so that they may see that they themselves are like animals.
Kiswahili: Pia nikafikiri, “Kuhusu wanadamu, Mungu huwajaribu ili wajione kwamba wao ni kama wanyama.
Ekegusii: Naende ngateeba ase enkoro yane ime ng’a Nyasae nigo agoteema Mwanyabaanto kobaenekia ng’a barabwo nigo banga buna ching’iti.

English: For that which happens to the sons of men happens to animals. Even one thing happens to them. As the one dies, so the other dies. Yes, they have all one breath; and man has no advantage over the animals, for all is vanity.
Kiswahili: Hatima ya mwanadamu ni kama ile ya wanyama; wote wana mwisho unaofanana: Jinsi anavyokufa mnyama, ndivyo anavyokufa mwanadamu. Wote wana pumzi inayofanana; mwanadamu hana cha zaidi kuliko mnyama. Kila kitu ni ubatili.
Ekegusii: Amang’ana akonyora ching’iti naro ayio akobanyora Mwanyabaanto; buna ching’iti chigokwa, naboigo na Mwanyabaanto bagokwa. Omoika noyomo ore ase ching’iti na ase Mwanyabaanto; Mwanyabaanto tabueti ching’iti kende. Amang’ana onsi mbosa.

English: All go to one place. All are from the dust, and all turn to dust again.
Kiswahili: Wote huenda mahali panapofanana; wote hutoka mavumbini, mavumbini wote hurudi.
Ekegusii: Mwanyabaanto nigo bakogenda aase ching’iti chikogenda; Mwanyabaanto nigo baruete ase amaroba, ne ching’iti naboigo; nigo bakoirana ase amaroba, naboigo na chirochio.

English: Who knows the spirit of man, whether it goes upward, and the spirit of the animal, whether it goes downward to the earth?”
Kiswahili: Ni nani ajuaye kama roho ya mtu huenda juu na roho ya mnyama hushuka chini ardhini?”
Ekegusii: Ning’o omanyete gose omoika o Mwanyabaanto niigoro ogochia, na oyo bwe ching’iti ogenda inse y’ense?

English: Therefore I saw that there is nothing better than that a man should rejoice in his works, for that is his portion; for who can bring him to see what will be after him?
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo nikaona kwamba hakuna kitu kilicho bora zaidi kwa mwanadamu kuliko kuifurahia kazi yake, kwa sababu hilo ndilo fungu lake. Kwa maana ni nani awezaye kumrudisha ili aje kuona kile kitakachotendeka baada yake?
Ekegusii: Ase ayio nkarora ng’a gento kende tikeri kere ekiya, otatiga omonto agokere emeremo yaye; ekio nakio egetari kiaye. Ning’o orachie komoirania ache korora na komanya ayakoregete magega yaye?

English: Then I returned and saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold, the tears of those who were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter.
Kiswahili: Nikatazama tena nikaona uonevu wote uliokuwa unafanyika chini ya jua: Nikaona machozi ya walioonewa, wala hawana wa kuwafariji; uwezo ulikuwa upande wa wale wanaowaonea, wala hawana wa kuwafariji.
Ekegusii: Naende nkarigereria nkarora ogokora okobe kware gokorwa inse y’erioba. Nkarora abwo bagokorerwa bobe bakorera, na monto onde tarengeo okobaremia, ekiagera abwo barenge kobakorera bobe nigo barenge nokobua, na onde tarengeo okobaremia.

English: Therefore I praised the dead who have been long dead more than the living who are yet alive.
Kiswahili: Nami nikasema kwamba wafu, waliokwisha kufa, wana furaha kuliko watu walio hai, ambao bado wanaishi.
Ekegusii: Nkarora ng’a nigo ere buya ase abakuure kobua ase abare moyo.

English: Yes, better than them both is him who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
Kiswahili: Lakini aliye bora kuliko hao wawili ni yule ambaye hajazaliwa bado, ambaye hajaona ule uovu unaofanyika chini ya jua.
Ekegusii: Korende ase oyo otaraiborwa, oyio otararora ogokora okobe kore aiga inse y’erioba, nigo ere buya asare kobua ase abwo bonsi bare moyo na abakuure.

English: Then I saw all the labor and achievement that is the envy of a man’s neighbor. This also is vanity and a striving after wind.
Kiswahili: Tena nikaona kuwa kazi zote na mafanikio yote huchipuka kutokana na wivu wa mtu kwa jirani yake. Hili nalo ni ubatili, ni kukimbiza upepo.
Ekegusii: Erio nkarora emeremo eye emekong’u egokorwa, na omokia bwonsi bw’ogwechanda ase ogokora emeremo, ayio nigo agokorwa, ekiagera omonto akoba ne ribero ng’a abue oyonde. Ayio boigo mbosa, nigo are buna okominyokia embeo.

English: The fool folds his hands together and ruins himself.
Kiswahili: Mpumbavu hukunja mikono yake na kujiangamiza mwenyewe.
Ekegusii: Omoriri nigo agwetumata, na bweria omobere oye orea.

English: Better is a handful, with quietness, than two handfuls with labor and chasing after wind.
Kiswahili: Afadhali konzi moja pamoja na utulivu kuliko konzi mbili pamoja na taabu na kukimbiza upepo.
Ekegusii: Mbuya koba negento geichire oroe oromo na koba nomorembe, kobua koba n’ebinto biichire chindoe ibere na koba nogwechanda na kominyokera konyora ebire buna embeo bosa.

English: Then I returned and saw vanity under the sun.
Kiswahili: Tena nikaona kitu kingine kilicho ubatili chini ya jua:
Ekegusii: Naende nkarora obosa kegima bore inse y’erioba:

English: There is one who is alone, and he has neither son nor brother. There is no end to all of his labor, neither are his eyes satisfied with wealth. “For whom then do I labor and deprive my soul of enjoyment?” This also is vanity. Yes, it is a miserable business.
Kiswahili: Kulikuwepo mwanadamu aliye peke yake, hakuwa na mwana wala ndugu. Hapakuwa na mwisho wa kazi yake, hata hivyo macho yake hayakutosheka na utajiri wake. Aliuliza, “Ninajitaabisha hivi kwa ajili ya nani, nami kwa nini ninajinyima kufurahia?” Hili pia ni ubatili, ni shughuli yenye taabu!
Ekegusii: Nare omonto otabwate omwana gose omwabo; ere nigo agendererete gwechanda gokora emeremo emekong’u, na amaiso aye tari goisaneka ne chinibo; omonto oyio tana kweboria, “Ning’o ngochandekera gokorera na kwerina omogooko bwonsi?” Aya naro mbosa, na ogwechanda gotari nomogooko.

English: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.
Kiswahili: Wawili ni afadhali kuliko mmoja, kwa sababu wana malipo mazuri kwa kazi yao:
Ekegusii: Nigo ere buya koba babere kobua oyomo, ekiagera mbanyore eng’eria engiya ase emeremo yabo bagokora.

English: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up.
Kiswahili: Kama mmoja akianguka, mwenzake atamwinua. Lakini ni jambo la kuhuzunisha kwa mtu yule aangukaye naye hana wa kumwinua!
Ekegusii: Oyomo karagwe, oyonde namogororokie; korende obobe nobwaye oria ore bweka ekero aragwe, na onde tari oramogororokie.

English: Again, if two lie together, then they have warmth; but how can one keep warm alone?
Kiswahili: Pia, kama wawili wakilala pamoja watapashana joto. Lakini ni vipi mtu aweza kujipasha joto mwenyewe?
Ekegusii: Abanto babere kobararaare amo mbaigwe riberera korende naki oyomo arakore aigwe riberera kare bweka?

English: If a man prevails against one who is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
Kiswahili: Ingawa mtu mmoja aweza kushindwa, watu wawili wanaweza kumkabili adui na kumshinda. Kamba ya nyuzi tatu haikatiki kwa urahisi.
Ekegusii: Omonto aise korwania oyomo ore bweka, namobue, korende onye bare babere, takobabua. Engori esisire nemegoye etato teri kobutoka bwango.

English: Better is a poor and wise youth than an old and foolish king who doesn’t know how to receive admonition any more.
Kiswahili: Afadhali kijana maskini mwenye hekima kuliko mfalme mzee mpumbavu ambaye hajui tena kupokea maonyo.
Ekegusii: Omwana omosae omotaka ore nobong’aini niigo’are omuya kobua omorwoti omogotu ore omoriri, otari gwancha gosemigwa;

English: For out of prison he came out to be king; yes, even in his kingdom he was born poor.
Kiswahili: Kijana huyo angeweza kutokea gerezani akapata ufalme, au angeweza kuwa amezaliwa katika umaskini kwenye huo ufalme.
Ekegusii: neba ng’a omosae oria nigo aruete echela akabeekwa oborwoti, gose nigo aiboretwe ore omotaka ase obogambi bw’omorwoti oria.

English: I saw all the living who walk under the sun, that they were with the youth, the other, who succeeded him.
Kiswahili: Nikaona kwamba wote walioishi na kutembea chini ya jua walimfuata kijana, aliyepokea ufalme.
Ekegusii: Nkarora abanto bonsi abamenyete inse y’erioba bakobwatia omosae oria ogochia kobeekwa oborwoti ribaga ri’oria orengeo.

English: There was no end of all the people, even of all them over whom he was—yet those who come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
Kiswahili: Hapakuwa na kikomo cha watu wote aliowatawala. Lakini wale waliokuja baadaye hawakufurahia kazi ya yule aliyepokea ufalme. Hili nalo pia ni ubatili, ni kukimbiza upepo.
Ekegusii: Abanto abwo arenge koraa tibare kobareka. Nonya naboigo abwo barachiche magega y’abwo tibakomogokera. Ekeene, aya naro mbosa, na aya akominyokerwa konyorwa nigo are buna embeo bosa.

English: Guard your steps when you go to God’s house; for to draw near to listen is better than to give the sacrifice of fools, for they don’t know that they do evil.
Kiswahili: Linda hatua zako uendapo katika nyumba ya Mungu. Karibia usikilize kuliko kutoa dhabihu ya wapumbavu, ambao hawajui kuwa wanafanya kosa.
Ekegusii: Orende amagoro ao ekero ogosoa ase enyomba ya Nyasae; mbuya kogenda aroro ase ogotegerera kobua korua ebing’wanso ebio abariri bakorua, ekiagera abwo tibamanyeti ng’a nigo bagokora ebibe.

English: Don’t be rash with your mouth, and don’t let your heart be hasty to utter anything before God; for God is in heaven, and you on earth. Therefore let your words be few.
Kiswahili: Usiwe mwepesi kuzungumza, usiwe na haraka katika moyo wako kuzungumza lolote mbele za Mungu. Mungu yuko mbinguni nawe uko duniani, kwa hiyo maneno yako na yawe machache.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koba omwango ase ogokwana amang’ana, gose enkoro yao teba enyango gokwana ase obosio bwa Nyasae, ekiagera ere nigo are igoro, naye nigo ore inse aa ase ense; ase ayio tiga amang’ana ogokwana abe amake.

English: For as a dream comes with a multitude of cares, so a fool’s speech with a multitude of words.
Kiswahili: Kama vile ndoto huja wakati kuna shughuli nyingi, ndivyo yalivyo mazungumzo ya mpumbavu wakati kuna maneno mengi.
Ekegusii: Chindoto nigo chigocha korwa ase ogwechanda okonge, ne chinkwana chinyinge nigo chikorenta amang’ana ’oboriri.

English: When you vow a vow to God, don’t defer to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools. Pay that which you vow.
Kiswahili: Wakati unapomwekea Mungu nadhiri, usikawie kuitimiza. Yeye hafurahii wapumbavu; timiza nadhiri yako.
Ekegusii: Ekero kwarire eira ase Nyasae, tobaisa goteebana koyeikerania, ekiagera ere tari kogokigwa nabaanto abariri. Ikerania eira kwariete.

English: It is better that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not pay.
Kiswahili: Ni afadhali usiweke nadhiri kuliko kuiweka na usiitimize.
Ekegusii: Mbuya toria eira kobua koria eira na toyeikerania.

English: Don’t allow your mouth to lead you into sin. Don’t protest before the messenger that this was a mistake. Why should God be angry at your voice, and destroy the work of your hands?
Kiswahili: Usiruhusu kinywa chako kukuingiza dhambini. Tena usijitetee mbele ya huyo mjumbe wa hekaluni, ukisema, “Niliweka nadhiri kwa makosa.” Kwa nini Mungu akasirike kwa ajili ya yale unayosema na kuiharibu kazi ya mikono yako?
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gotiga amang’ana ’omonwa oo agere okore ebibe, gose tobaisa goteebia omosomba o Nyasae ng’a oko nokomocha gwakora. Nase ki oragere Nyasae agechigwe nogokwana kwao, na asarie emeremo y’amaboko ao?

English: For in the multitude of dreams there are vanities, as well as in many words; but you must fear God.
Kiswahili: Kuota ndoto kwingi na maneno mengi ni ubatili. Kwa hiyo simama katika kicho cha Mungu.
Ekegusii: Ekero amang’ana atari nengencho amentekanire, ne chindoto chiamentekanire, obobe nigo bokoba obonge; korende aye omoiroke Nyasae.

English: If you see the oppression of the poor, and the violent taking away of justice and righteousness in a district, don’t marvel at the matter, for one official is eyed by a higher one, and there are officials over them.
Kiswahili: Kama ukiona maskini wanaonewa katika nchi, hukumu na haki vikipotoshwa, usishangazwe na mambo hayo, kwa maana afisa mmoja anaangaliwa na aliye juu yake zaidi na juu ya hao wawili kuna wengine walio juu zaidi yao.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa goichana ekero orarore agwo ase obogambi abataka bagokorerwa bobe, na ekeene na oboronge biarusigweo ase enchera y’obotindi, omonene oyio okogamba nigo arigereirie noria ore omonene komobua, naende mbare abwo bare abanene kobua abwo bare nokobua.

English: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all. The king profits from the field.
Kiswahili: Mafanikio ya nchi ni kwa ajili ya wote, hata mfalme mwenyewe hufaidi kutoka mashambani.
Ekegusii: Mbuya ase ense ere nomorwoti okogamba buya na korigereria ng’a abanto nkorema bare emegondo yabo.

English: He who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver, nor he who loves abundance, with increase. This also is vanity.
Kiswahili: Yeyote apendaye fedha kamwe hatosheki na fedha; yeyote apendaye utajiri kamwe hatosheki na kipato chake. Hili nalo pia ni ubatili.
Ekegusii: Omonto bwanchete chitaabu, tagoisaneka nachirochio; gose oyobwanchete obotenenku, tagoisaneka nebitoki biaye. Ayio boigo mbosa.

English: When goods increase, those who eat them are increased; and what advantage is there to its owner, except to feast on them with his eyes?
Kiswahili: Mali ikiongezeka, ndivyo walaji wanavyoongezeka. Hii nayo inamfaidia nini mwenye mali isipokuwa ni kushibisha macho yake?
Ekegusii: Ekero obotenenku bokomentekana, boigo nabwo bakoboria nigo bakomentekana; bono mbuya ki oria omonyene akonyora, otatiga akoborora namaiso rioka?

English: The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the abundance of the rich will not allow him to sleep.
Kiswahili: Usingizi wa kibarua ni mtamu, awe amekula kidogo au kingi, lakini wingi wa mali humnyima tajiri usingizi.
Ekegusii: Chitoro chi’omokori emeremo nigo chire chingiya mono, neba ng’a nigo abwate egento egeke akoria, gose ebinge; korende obotenenku bw’omonto omonda tibokomotiga araare chitoro.

English: There is a grievous evil which I have seen under the sun: wealth kept by its owner to his harm.
Kiswahili: Nimeshaona uovu mzito chini ya jua: Utajiri uliolimbikizwa kwa kujinyima na kuleta madhara kwa mwenye mali,
Ekegusii: Obobe mono narorire inse y’erioba nabwo obo: chinibo chinyinge chikogachwa nigo chiranyare gosiria omonto ochigachete.

English: Those riches perish by misfortune, and if he has fathered a son, there is nothing in his hand.
Kiswahili: au utajiri uliopotea kwa bahati mbaya, hivyo kwamba wakati akiwa na mwana hakuna chochote kilichobaki kwa ajili yake.
Ekegusii: Chinibo echio nigo chigosira ase egesio ekebe, na ekero omonto oyio aiboire omwana omomura nigo akonyorekana ore bosa, tabwati kende akomoa.

English: As he came out of his mother’s womb, naked shall he go again as he came, and shall take nothing for his labor, which he may carry away in his hand.
Kiswahili: Mtu hutoka tumboni mwa mama yake uchi, naye jinsi alivyokuja vivyo hivyo huondoka. Hachukui chochote kutokana na kazi yake ambacho anaweza kukibeba mkononi mwake.
Ekegusii: Buna aiboretwe ore getirianda korwa ase enda ya ng’ina, naboigo aragende ore getirianda buna achete, gose takoira kende ase ebio echandeire mono kobinyora.

English: This also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he came, so shall he go. And what profit does he have who labors for the wind?
Kiswahili: Hili nalo ni baya la kusikitisha: Kama vile mtu ajavyo, vivyo hivyo huondoka, naye anapata faida gani, maadamu hutaabika kwa ajili ya upepo?
Ekegusii: Obo boigo nobobe bw’obororo; onye okorua ase ense ogenda buna achete, mbitoki ki abwate ase ogwechanda gokora emeremo emekong’u y’okominyokia aya are buna embeo bosa?

English: All his days he also eats in darkness, he is frustrated, and has sickness and wrath.
Kiswahili: Siku zake zote hula gizani, pamoja na fadhaa kubwa, mateso na hasira.
Ekegusii: Ase obogima bwaye bwonsi nigo abeire okoria endagera ore ase omosunte, obeire ogwechanda ore nobororo na okogechigwa.

English: Behold, that which I have seen to be good and proper is for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy good in all his labor, in which he labors under the sun, all the days of his life which God has given him; for this is his portion.
Kiswahili: Ndipo nikatambua kwamba ni vyema na sahihi kwa mtu kula na kunywa na kutosheka katika kazi yake ngumu chini ya jua katika siku chache za maisha yake Mungu alizompa, kwa maana hili ndilo fungu lake.
Ekegusii: Naama! Aya narorire are amaya na agwenerete nokoria na konywa na koba nomogooko ase ebinto ebio bionsi omonto echandeire aiga inse y’erioba, ase engaki y’amatuko amake Nyasae amoeire; ekio nakio egetari kiaye.

English: Every man also to whom God has given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat of it, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor—this is the gift of God.
Kiswahili: Zaidi ya yote, Mungu anapompa mtu yeyote utajiri na milki, humwezesha kuvifurahia, kukubali fungu lake na kuwa na furaha katika kazi yake, hii ni karama ya Mungu.
Ekegusii: Onye Nyasae oeire omonto obotenenku ne chinibo, naende omoeire okobua gw’okwegokia ase ebinto ebio na kobikorera ase obuya bwaye, boigo koba nomogooko ase emeremo yaye, ayio onsi nigo are ebiegwa bia Nyasae.

English: For he shall not often reflect on the days of his life, because God occupies him with the joy of his heart.
Kiswahili: Mara chache mtu huzifikiri siku za maisha yake, kwa sababu Mungu humfanya ashikwe na furaha ya moyoni.
Ekegusii: Omonto oyio takogenderera koinyora amatuko aetire ay’obogima bwaye, ekiagera Nyasae nigo akomoa omogooko ase enkoro yaye.

English: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is heavy on men:
Kiswahili: Nimeona ubaya mwingine chini ya jua, nao unalemea sana wanadamu:
Ekegusii: Mbore obobe narorie aiga inse y’erioba boritoerete Mwanyabaanto:

English: a man to whom God gives riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing for his soul of all that he desires, yet God gives him no power to eat of it, but an alien eats it. This is vanity, and it is an evil disease.
Kiswahili: Mungu humpa mwanadamu utajiri, mali na heshima, hivyo hakukosa chochote moyo wake unachokitamani. Lakini Mungu hamwezeshi kuvifurahia, badala yake mgeni ndiye anayevifurahia. Hili ni ubatili, ni ubaya unaosikitisha.
Ekegusii: Nyasae oeire omonto obotenenku, ne chinibo, na ogosikwa, na omonto oyio taremeiri gento kende ase ebio bionsi aganetie, korende Nyasae tamoeti okobua gw’okwegokia ase ebinto ebio; omonto omoao nigo akobiira bwegokia nabirobio. Ayio naro mbosa, naende nogwechanda okobe.

English: If a man fathers a hundred children, and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul is not filled with good, and moreover he has no burial, I say that a stillborn child is better than he;
Kiswahili: Mtu anaweza kuwa na watoto mia moja naye akaishi miaka mingi, lakini haidhuru kuwa ataishi muda mrefu kiasi gani, kama hawezi kufurahia mafanikio yake na kwamba hapati mazishi ya heshima, ninasema afadhali mtoto aliyezaliwa akiwa amekufa kuliko yeye.
Ekegusii: Onye omonto oiboire abana rigana erimo, na abe moyo ase engaki y’emiaka emenge, ee, nonya amatuko ’obogima bwaye abeire amange, korende tegogetie ase ebinto ebiya bi’obogima obwo, na tatindekwa ase amasikani, nigo ngoteeba ng’a omwana okwerete enda ya ng’ina nigo are buya kobua omonto oyio.

English: for it comes in vanity, and departs in darkness, and its name is covered with darkness.
Kiswahili: Kuzaliwa kwake hakuna maana, huondokea gizani na gizani jina lake hufunikwa.
Ekegusii: Omwana oyio okwete nigo achete egento bosa, naende nigo akogenda gochia ase omosunte, na omosunte oyio otuba erieta riaye.

English: Moreover it has not seen the sun nor known it. This has rest rather than the other.
Kiswahili: Ingawa hakuwahi kuliona jua wala kujua kitu chochote, yeye ana pumziko zaidi kuliko mtu huyo,
Ekegusii: Omwana oria taroche erioba, gose tamanyete gento kende, korende nonya naboigo nigo akonyora omotimoko kobua omonto oria,

English: Yes, though he live a thousand years twice told, and yet fails to enjoy good, don’t all go to one place?
Kiswahili: Hata kama huyo mtu ataishi miaka elfu mara mbili na zaidi, lakini akashindwa kufurahia mafanikio yake, je, wote hawaendi sehemu moja?
Ekegusii: nonya omonto oria ogochia komenya emiaka chilifu ibere, korende tanyora omogooko ase obogima bwaye. Inee! Abwo bonsi babere tibakogenda aase amo?

English: All the labor of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
Kiswahili: Juhudi zote za binadamu ni kwa ajili ya kinywa chake, hata hivyo hamu yake kamwe haitoshelezwi.
Ekegusii: Emeremo yonsi omonto akwerosia gokora nokonyora egento akoria, korende nonya naboigo tari koigota.

English: For what advantage has the wise more than the fool? What has the poor man, that knows how to walk before the living?
Kiswahili: Mtu mwenye hekima ana faida gani zaidi ya mpumbavu? Mtu maskini anapata faida gani kwa kujua jinsi ya kujistahi mbele ya watu wengine?
Ekegusii: Mbuya ki omonto omong’aini abwate kobua oyore omoriri? Gose ninki omonto omotaka akonyora, oria omanyete buna akwerenda ase abare moyo?

English: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
Kiswahili: Ni bora kile ambacho jicho linakiona kuliko hamu isiyotoshelezwa. Hili nalo ni ubatili, ni kukimbiza upepo.
Ekegusii: Eki amaiso aroche nigo kere buya kobua eki okogania ng’a okenyore. Ayio boigo mbosa, na okominyokia aya are buna embeo bosa.

English: Whatever has been, its name was given long ago; and it is known what man is; neither can he contend with him who is mightier than he.
Kiswahili: Lolote lililopo limekwisha kupewa jina, naye mwanadamu alivyo ameshajulikana; hakuna mtu awezaye kushindana na mwenye nguvu kuliko yeye.
Ekegusii: Gento kende gionsi kereo nigo kiarogetwe erieta korwa kare, naende nigo yamanyekanete eki omonto are gocha koba. Mwanyabaanto takonyara koamererania noria ore ne chinguru komobua.

English: For there are many words that create vanity. What does that profit man?
Kiswahili: Maneno yanavyokuwa mengi, ndivyo yanavyokosa maana, Je, hilo linamfaidia vipi yeyote?
Ekegusii: Ogokwana okonge nigo gokorenta amang’ana amange are bosa. Inee! Ayio mbuya ki akorenta ase Mwanyabaanto?

English: For who knows what is good for man in life, all the days of his vain life which he spends like a shadow? For who can tell a man what will be after him under the sun?
Kiswahili: Kwa maana ni nani anayejua lililo jema kwa ajili ya maisha ya mwanadamu, katika siku chache na za ubatili anazopita kama kivuli? Ni nani awezaye kumwambia yatakayotokea chini ya jua baada ya yeye kuondoka?
Ekegusii: Ning’o omanyete egento kere ekiya ase omonto, ekero amenyete amatuko amake ase obogima bore bosa, agoeta buna omorengari? Ning’o oranyare goteebia omonto amang’ana arabe korwa magega yaye aiga inse y’erioba?

English: A good name is better than fine perfume; and the day of death better than the day of one’s birth.
Kiswahili: Afadhali sifa nzuri kuliko manukato safi, nayo siku ya kufa kuliko ya kuzaliwa.
Ekegusii: Erieta rigiya nigo ribuete amaguta amaya akweakwa, ne rituko ri’ogokwa nigo rire rigiya kobua eri’okoiborwa.

English: It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting; for that is the end of all men, and the living should take this to heart.
Kiswahili: Afadhali kwenda kwenye nyumba ya msiba kuliko kwenda kwenye nyumba ya karamu, kwa kuwa kifo ni hatima ya kila mwanadamu, imewapasa walio hai kuliweka hili mioyoni mwao.
Ekegusii: Mbuya kogenda ase enyomba y’ebirero kobua kogenda ase enyomba y’omoyega bw’okwegokia, ekiagera oyio noro omoerio o kera omonto, na abare moyo mbabeeke amang’ana aya ase chinkoro chiabo.

English: Sorrow is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the face the heart is made good.
Kiswahili: Huzuni ni afadhali kuliko kicheko, kwa sababu uso wenye huzuni wafaa kwa moyo.
Ekegusii: Omoichano nigo ore omuya kobua amaseko, ekiagera omoichano okororekana ase obosio nigo ogokora enkoro yaba nomogooko.

English: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
Kiswahili: Moyo wa wenye hekima uko katika nyumba ya msiba, lakini moyo wa wapumbavu uko katika nyumba ya anasa.
Ekegusii: Chinkoro chi’abaanto abang’aini nigo chikoba ase enyomba y’ebirero, korende chinkoro chi’abariri nigo chire ase enyomba y’okwegokia.

English: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise than for a man to hear the song of fools.
Kiswahili: Afadhali kusikia karipio la mtu mwenye hekima, kuliko kusikiliza wimbo wa wapumbavu.
Ekegusii: Mbuya omonto gotegerera ogotogonyerwa kw’omonto omong’aini kobua gotegerera ogoteera kw’abariri.

English: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This also is vanity.
Kiswahili: Kama ilivyo kuvunjika kwa miiba chini ya sufuria, ndivyo kilivyo kicheko cha wapumbavu. Hili nalo pia ni ubatili.
Ekegusii: Ogoseka kw’abariri nigo konga amagwa akoyia atoreka inse y’enyongo ere riko. Ayio boigo mbosa.

English: Surely extortion makes the wise man foolish; and a bribe destroys the understanding.
Kiswahili: Dhuluma humfanya mtu mwenye hekima kuwa mpumbavu, nayo rushwa huuharibu moyo.
Ekegusii: Ekeene, emoko nigo ekoonchora omonto omong’aini oba omoriri, ne riaaki nigo rigosaria ebirengererio.

English: Better is the end of a thing than its beginning. The patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
Kiswahili: Mwisho wa jambo ni bora kuliko mwanzo wake, uvumilivu ni bora kuliko kiburi.
Ekegusii: Omoerio bw’egento nigo ore omuya kobua omochakano oye; na omonto omoremereria nigo are omuya kobua omonto omoenenu.

English: Don’t be hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools.
Kiswahili: Usiwe mwepesi kukasirika rohoni mwako, kwa kuwa hasira hukaa kifuani mwa wapumbavu.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koba omwango ase okogechigwa, ekiagera okogechigwa nigo komenyete ase chinkoro chi’abariri.

English: Don’t say, “Why were the former days better than these?” For you do not ask wisely about this.
Kiswahili: Usiseme, “Kwa nini siku za kale zilikuwa bora kuliko siku hizi?” Kwa maana si hekima kuuliza maswali kama hayo.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa goteeba, “Nase ki amatuko a kare arenge amaya kobua aya bono?” Okoboria okwo tikori okw’obong’aini.

English: Wisdom is as good as an inheritance. Yes, it is more excellent for those who see the sun.
Kiswahili: Hekima, kama ulivyo urithi, ni kitu chema na huwafaidia wale walionalo jua.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini nigo bore obuya buna omwando, na nigo bogokonya abwo baroche erioba.

English: For wisdom is a defense, even as money is a defense; but the excellency of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of him who has it.
Kiswahili: Hekima ni ulinzi kama fedha ilivyo ulinzi, lakini faida ya maarifa ni hii: kwamba hekima huhifadhi maisha ya aliye nayo.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini nigo bogotokonya buna chitaabu chigotokonya, korende obuya bw’omonyasemi mboria ng’a obong’aini nigo bokorenda obogima bw’oyio ong’ainiire.

English: Consider the work of God, for who can make that straight which he has made crooked?
Kiswahili: Tafakari kile Mungu alichokitenda: Nani awezaye kunyoosha kile ambacho yeye amekipinda?
Ekegusii: Rengereria emeremo ya Nyasae! Ning’o oranyare korongeyia egento Omonene akorire borogochi?

English: In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider; yes, God has made the one side by side with the other, to the end that man should not find out anything after him.
Kiswahili: Nyakati zikiwa nzuri, ufurahi, lakini nyakati zikiwa mbaya, tafakari: Mungu amefanya hiyo moja, naam, sanjari na hiyo nyingine. Kwa hiyo, mwanadamu hawezi kugundua kitu chochote kuhusu maisha yake ya baadaye.
Ekegusii: Ekero amatuko ao are amaya kabe nomogooko, na ekero are amabe rengereria ng’a Nyasae nere okorire ayio onsi abere, erinde omonto tabaisa komanya erirache komobwatia korwa magega yaye.

English: All this I have seen in my days of vanity: there is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man who lives long in his evildoing.
Kiswahili: Katika maisha haya yangu ya ubatili nimeshaona haya mawili: mtu mwadilifu akiangamia katika uadilifu wake, naye mtu mwovu akiishi maisha marefu katika uovu wake.
Ekegusii: Ase obogima obo bwane obore bosa narorire kera egento; narorire omonto omonyaboronge ogosira ore ase oboronge bwaye, na omonyabibe okogenderera koba moyo amatuko amange ore ase ebibe biaye.

English: Don’t be overly righteous, neither make yourself overly wise. Why should you destroy yourself?
Kiswahili: Usiwe mwenye haki kupita kiasi, wala usiwe na hekima kupita kiasi: kwa nini kujiangamiza mwenyewe?
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koba omooronge goetania, gose koba omong’aini goetania. Nase ki ogwesiria aye omonyene?

English: Don’t be too wicked, neither be foolish. Why should you die before your time?
Kiswahili: Usiwe mwovu kupita kiasi, wala usiwe mpumbavu: kwa nini kufa kabla ya wakati wako?
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koba omobe goetania, gose tobaisa koba omoriri. Nase ki oganetie gokwa engaki yao etaraika?

English: It is good that you should take hold of this. Yes, also don’t withdraw your hand from that; for he who fears God will come out of them all.
Kiswahili: Ni vyema kushika hilo moja na wala usiache hilo jingine likupite. Mtu amchaye Mungu ataepuka huko kupita kiasi.
Ekegusii: Nigo ere buya ng’a obwate ring’ana eri erimo, na totiga neria kabere, ekiagera omonto omoirogete Nyasae namanye eki agokora ase kera ring’ana.

English: Wisdom is a strength to the wise man more than ten rulers who are in a city.
Kiswahili: Hekima humfanya yeye aliye nayo kuwa na uwezo zaidi kuliko watawala kumi katika mji.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini nigo bogokora abare abang’aini koba ne chinguru chibuete echi’abagaambi ikomi bare ase omochie oyomo.

English: Surely there is not a righteous man on earth who does good and doesn’t sin.
Kiswahili: Hakuna mtu mwenye haki duniani ambaye hufanya mambo ya haki na kamwe asitende dhambi.
Ekegusii: Ekeene, omonto tari aiga ase ense ore omooronge ogokora amaya otari gokora ebibe.

English: Also don’t take heed to all words that are spoken, lest you hear your servant curse you;
Kiswahili: Usitie maanani kila neno linalosemwa na watu, la sivyo, waweza kumsikia mtumishi wako akikulaani:
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gotegerera amang’ana onsi abanto bagokwana, nigo orabaise koigwa omosomba oo ogokoragereria.

English: for often your own heart knows that you yourself have likewise cursed others.
Kiswahili: kwa kuwa unafahamu moyoni mwako kwamba wewe mwenyewe mara nyingi umewalaani wengine.
Ekegusii: Aye omonyene nomanyete ase enkoro yao ng’a ase chingaki chinyinge kwabeire gokoragereria abanto bande.

English: All this I have proved in wisdom. I said, “I will be wise;” but it was far from me.
Kiswahili: Yote haya niliyajaribu kwa hekima, nikasema, “Nimeamua kuwa na hekima”: lakini hii ilikuwa nje ya uwezo wangu.
Ekegusii: Aya onsi ngateema koyaenekia ase enchera y’obong’aini, ngateeba, “Goika imbe nobong’aini.” Korende obong’aini obwo bokabeera aare korwa ase ’nde.

English: That which is, is far off and exceedingly deep. Who can find it out?
Kiswahili: Vyovyote hekima ilivyo, hekima iko mbali sana na imejificha, ni nani awezaye kuigundua?
Ekegusii: Amang’ana aria nigo akare aare mono, naende akare aatambe gochia inse, aatambe mono, ning’o oranyare koyatuka?

English: I turned around, and my heart sought to know and to search out, and to seek wisdom and the scheme of things, and to know that wickedness is stupidity, and that foolishness is madness.
Kiswahili: Nikageuza fikira zangu ili kuelewa, kuchunguza na kuitafuta hekima na kusudi la mambo, na ili kuelewa ujinga wa uovu, na wazimu wa upumbavu.
Ekegusii: Erio ngachaka korengereria imanye, na gotuka, na korigia obong’aini, na komanya buna ebinto bionsi bire; naende nkagania komanya obobe bw’oboriri, na oboriri obore obobarimo.

English: I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and traps, whose hands are chains. Whoever pleases God shall escape from her; but the sinner will be ensnared by her.
Kiswahili: Nimeona jambo lililo chungu kuliko mauti, mwanamke ambaye ni mtego, ambaye moyo wake ni wavu wa kutegea na mikono yake ni minyororo. Mtu ampendezaye Mungu atamkwepa, bali mwenye dhambi atanaswa naye.
Ekegusii: Erio nkanyora egento ekeroro kebuete amakweri. Egento ekio nakio omokungu enkoro yaye yarenge omotego, naende amaboko aye are chingataare. Omonto ogogetie Nyasae tari kobwatwa nomokuungu oyio, korende omonyabibe ere nigo akobwatwa.

English: “Behold, I have found this,” says the Preacher, “to one another, to find an explanation
Kiswahili: Mhubiri anasema, “Tazama, hili ndilo nililogundua: “Nimegundua kitu kimoja baada ya kingine nilipokuwa katika kusudi la mambo:
Ekegusii: Omorandia nigo agoteeba iga: Naama! Amang’ana ayio nkayamanya, ekero nabeekeranetie ring’ana erimo ase erinde koyamanya onsi.

English: which my soul still seeks, but I have not found. I have found one man among a thousand, but I have not found a woman among all those.
Kiswahili: ningali natafiti lakini sipati: nilimpata mwanaume mmoja mnyofu miongoni mwa elfu, lakini hakuna mwanamke mmoja mnyofu miongoni mwao.
Ekegusii: Aya nabeire nkona‐koyairanerera korigia komanya buna are, korende tindayamanya. Ase abanto elifu eyemo nkanyora omosacha oyomo, korende ase abwo bonsi tinanyorete omokungu nonya noyomo.

English: Behold, I have only found this: that God made mankind upright; but they search for many inventions.”
Kiswahili: Hili ndilo peke yake nililolipata: Mungu amemuumba mwanadamu mnyofu, lakini mwanadamu amebuni mambo mengi.”
Ekegusii: Naama! Egento gioka narigirie nanyorire neke: Nyasae nigo atongete Mwanyabaanto bare abaikeranu, korende barabwo batukire chinchera chinyinge chi’okobaisanekia.

English: Who is like the wise man? And who knows the interpretation of a thing? A man’s wisdom makes his face shine, and the hardness of his face is changed.
Kiswahili: Ni nani aliye kama mtu mwenye hekima? Ni nani ajuaye maelezo ya mambo? Hekima hungʼarisha uso wa mtu na kubadili ugumu wa uso wake.
Ekegusii: Ning’o onga buna omonto omong’aini? Ning’o omanyete engencho y’amang’ana? Obong’aini nigo bogokora obosio bw’omonto bwagirigenta, nigo bokoonchora obokong’u bw’okororekana kwaye.

English: I say, “Keep the king’s command!” because of the oath to God.
Kiswahili: Nawaambia, Tii amri ya mfalme, kwa sababu uliapa mbele za Mungu.
Ekegusii: Inche nigo nkogosemia: Oigwere amang’ana omorwoti achiikire, ekiagera nkwarierete Nyasae eira.

English: Don’t be hasty to go out of his presence. Don’t persist in an evil thing, for he does whatever pleases him,
Kiswahili: Usiharakishe kuondoka mbele ya mfalme. Usiendelee kutenda lililo baya, kwa maana mfalme atafanya lolote apendalo.
Ekegusii: Toayerera gotiga obokoreri ase obosio bwaye, na tobwatana nogokora okobe, ekiagera ere nigo agokora onsi ayanchete.

English: for the king’s word is supreme. Who can say to him, “What are you doing?”
Kiswahili: Kwa kuwa neno la mfalme ndilo lenye mamlaka ya mwisho, nani awezaye kumwambia, “Je, wewe unafanya nini?”
Ekegusii: Ring’ana ri’omorwoti nigo rire nokobua. Ning’o oranyare komobooria, “Aye ngento ki eke ogokora?”

English: Whoever keeps the commandment shall not come to harm, and his wise heart will know the time and procedure.
Kiswahili: Yeyote anayetii agizo lake hatadhurika, moyo wa hekima utajua wakati muafaka na jinsi ya kutenda.
Ekegusii: Omonto okoigwera amachiiko takonyorwa namabe, na enkoro y’omonto omong’aini nigo ekomanya engaki na enchera y’okonacha boronge.

English: For there is a time and procedure for every purpose, although the misery of man is heavy on him.
Kiswahili: Kwa maana kuna wakati muafaka na utaratibu wa kila jambo, ingawa huzuni ya mwanadamu huwa nzito juu yake.
Ekegusii: Kera ring’ana ndibwate engaki yaye na enchera yaye y’okonacha boronge, na emechando y’omonto nigo ekomoritoera.

English: For he doesn’t know that which will be; for who can tell him how it will be?
Kiswahili: Kwa vile hakuna mtu ajuaye siku zijazo, ni nani awezaye kumwambia linalokuja?
Ekegusii: Omonto tamanyeti ayagochia koba, na ning’o oranyare komoteebia buna amang’ana arabe?

English: There is no man who has power over the spirit to contain the spirit; neither does he have power over the day of death. There is no discharge in war; neither shall wickedness deliver those who practice it.
Kiswahili: Hakuna mwanadamu awezaye kushikilia roho yake asife, wala hakuna mwenye uwezo juu ya siku ya kufa kwake. Kama vile hakuna yeyote arudishwaye nyuma wakati wa vita, kadhalika uovu hautawaweka huru wale wautendao.
Ekegusii: Monto onde tari obwate okobua igoro y’embeo, gose igoro ye rituko ri’ogokwa kwaye; ogotooreka tikori ase esegi, gose obobe tibogotooria abwo bakobokora.

English: All this I have seen, and applied my mind to every work that is done under the sun. There is a time in which one man has power over another to his hurt.
Kiswahili: Yote haya niliyaona, nilipokuwa natafakari kila kitu kinachotendeka chini ya jua. Kuna wakati ambapo mtu hujifanya bwana juu ya wengine kwa madhara yake mwenyewe.
Ekegusii: Ayio onsi nigo nayaroche ekero nabegete ebirengererio biane kwegera aya onsi agokorwa aiga inse y’erioba, ekero omonto oyomo akogambera omonto onde na komokorera bobe ase okomochanda.

English: So I saw the wicked buried. Indeed they came also from holiness. They went and were forgotten in the city where they did this. This also is vanity.
Kiswahili: Ndipo pia, nikaona waovu wakizikwa, wale ambao walizoea kuingia na kutoka mahali patakatifu na kupewa sifa katika mji ambapo walikuwa wamefanya haya. Hili nalo ni ubatili.
Ekegusii: Nkarora abakori amabe batindekirwe batimogete, na ekero abanto bairanete korwa ase achenu nigo bare kobatogia agwo ase omochie. Ayio boigo mbosa.

English: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
Kiswahili: Wakati hukumu juu ya tendo ovu haitekelezwi upesi, mioyo ya watu hujaa mipango ya kutenda maovu.
Ekegusii: Ase engencho obobe botari konacherwa ekiina bwango, chikoro chia Mwanyabaanto nigo chikwerua gokora ayare amabe.

English: Though a sinner commits crimes a hundred times, and lives long, yet surely I know that it will be better with those who fear God, who are reverent before him.
Kiswahili: Ingawa mtu mwovu hufanya maovu mia moja na akaendelea kuishi maisha marefu, najua kwamba itakuwa bora zaidi kwa watu wanaomwogopa Mungu, wamchao Mungu.
Ekegusii: Omonyabibe nakora ebibe ara rigana, naende agenderere koba moyo ase engaki entambe; nonya naboigo, nimanyete ng’a nigo erabe buya ase abwo bamoirogete Nyasae, ekiagera bamoirogete.

English: But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he lengthen days like a shadow, because he doesn’t fear God.
Kiswahili: Lakini kwa sababu waovu hawamwogopi Mungu, hawatafanikiwa, maisha yao hayatarefuka kama kivuli.
Ekegusii: Korende abakori amabe tibakonyora amaya ayio, gose obogima bwabo tibokoba obotambe. Nigo banga buna omorengari ogoeta, ekiagera tibamoirogete Nyasae.

English: There is a vanity which is done on the earth, that there are righteous men to whom it happens according to the work of the wicked. Again, there are wicked men to whom it happens according to the work of the righteous. I said that this also is vanity.
Kiswahili: Kuna kitu kingine ambacho ni ubatili kinachotokea duniani: Watu waadilifu kupata yale yanayowastahili waovu, nao waovu kupata yale yanayowastahili waadilifu. Hili nalo pia, nasema ni ubatili.
Ekegusii: Nare amang’ana abosa kegima agokorekana aiga ase ense; mbareo abanto abanyaboronge bakonyorwa negesusuro ki’ogokora kw’abanyabibe, na boigo abanyabibe banyora obuya bw’ogokora kw’abanyaboronge. Ase ayio ngateeba, “Ayio boigo mbosa.”

English: Then I commended mirth, because a man has no better thing under the sun than to eat, to drink, and to be joyful: for that will accompany him in his labor all the days of his life which God has given him under the sun.
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo mimi ninasifu kufurahia maisha, kwa sababu hakuna kitu bora zaidi kwa mwanadamu chini ya jua kuliko kula, kunywa na kufurahi. Kisha furaha itafuatana naye kazini mwake siku zote za maisha yake ambazo amepewa na Mungu chini ya jua.
Ekegusii: Ngatogia omogooko, na nkarora ng’a Mwanyabaanto tabwati gento kende kere ekiya aiga inse y’erioba, otatiga arie na konywa, na kwegokia barabwo abanyene. Ayio naro aranyare kobeera asare ekero agendererete gokora emeremo emekong’u ase obogima obo are moyo, obo Nyasae amoeire aiga inse y’erioba.

English: When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done on the earth (even though eyes see no sleep day or night),
Kiswahili: Nilipotafakari akilini mwangu ili nijue hekima na kuangalia kazi ya mwanadamu duniani, jinsi ambavyo macho yake hayapati usingizi mchana wala usiku,
Ekegusii: Ekero nabeegete ebirengererio biane komanya obong’aini na korora emeremo emekong’u abanto bagokora aiga ase ense, batari korara chitoro omobaso gose obotuko.

English: then I saw all the work of God, that man can’t find out the work that is done under the sun, because however much a man labors to seek it out, yet he won’t find it. Yes even though a wise man thinks he can comprehend it, he won’t be able to find it.
Kiswahili: ndipo nikaona yale yote ambayo Mungu ameyafanya. Hakuna yeyote awezaye kuelewa yale yanayotendeka chini ya jua. Licha ya juhudi zake zote za kutafuta, mtu hawezi kugundua maana yake. Hata ingawa mtu mwenye hekima anadai kuwa anafahamu, kwa hakika hawezi kutambua.
Ekegusii: Erio nkarora ng’a omonto takonyara komanya emeremo ende yonsi ya Nyasae egokorekana aiga inse y’erioba. Omonto naisa gwechanda mono ase okorigia koyemanya, takonyara koyemanya. Nonya omonto omong’aini ogoteeba ng’a namanyete, takonyara koyemanya.

English: For all this I laid to my heart, even to explore all this: that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God; whether it is love or hatred, man doesn’t know it; all is before them.
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo niliyatafakari yote haya nikafikia uamuzi kwamba waadilifu na wenye hekima na yale wanayoyafanya yako mikononi mwa Mungu, lakini hakuna mtu ajuaye kama anangojewa na upendo au chuki.
Ekegusii: Nkarengereria igoro y’amang’ana aya onsi, ngateema komanya buna abanyene oboronge na abare nobong’aini bare ase okoboko kwa Nyasae, amo nogokora kwabo, gokorabe okw’obwanchani gose ogw’okogecha. Monto onde tamanyeti amang’ana are bosio.

English: All things come alike to all. There is one event to the righteous and to the wicked; to the good, to the clean, to the unclean, to him who sacrifices, and to him who doesn’t sacrifice. As is the good, so is the sinner; he who takes an oath, as he who fears an oath.
Kiswahili: Wote wanayo hatima inayofanana, mwadilifu na mwovu, mwema na mbaya, aliye safi na aliye najisi, wale wanaotoa dhabihu na wale wasiotoa. Kama ilivyo kwa mtu mwema, ndivyo ilivyo kwa mtu mwenye dhambi; kama ilivyo kwa wale wanaoapa, ndivyo ilivyo kwa wale wasioapa.
Ekegusii: Egento nekemo gekobanyora bonsi, omonyene oboronge na omonyabibe, oyore omuya na ochenegete na oyo otachenegeti, oyo okorua ebing’wanso na oyo otari kobirua. Buna ekoba ase omonto omuya, naboigo ekoba nase omonyabibe; buna ekoba ase oria okoria eira y’ogotiana, naboigo ekoba nase oria otari koria eira y’ogotiana.

English: This is an evil in all that is done under the sun, that there is one event to all. Yes also, the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.
Kiswahili: Huu ni ubaya ulio katika kila kitu kinachotendeka chini ya jua: Mwisho unaofanana huwapata wote. Zaidi ya hayo, mioyo ya watu, imejaa ubaya na kuna wazimu mioyoni mwao wangali hai, hatimaye huungana na waliokufa.
Ekegusii: Obo nabwo obobe ase aya onsi agokorekana aiga inse y’erioba, ng’a egento nekemo gekobanyora bonsi; chinkoro chia Mwanyabaanto nigo chiichire obobe na obobarimo ekero bare moyo, na magega y’ayio nigo bakogeenda ase abakuure.

English: For to him who is joined with all the living there is hope; for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
Kiswahili: Yeyote aliye miongoni mwa walio hai analo tumaini, hata mbwa hai ni bora kuliko simba aliyekufa!
Ekegusii: Korende omonto ore ase egati y’abare moyo nare nogosemeria, na esese ere moyo nigo ekonyora amaya kobua endo ekwete.

English: For the living know that they will die, but the dead don’t know anything, neither do they have any more a reward; for their memory is forgotten.
Kiswahili: Kwa maana walio hai wanajua kwamba watakufa, lakini wafu hawajui chochote, hawana tuzo zaidi, hata kumbukumbu yao imesahaulika.
Ekegusii: Ee, abare moyo mbamanyete ng’a mbakwe, korende abakuure tibamanyeti gento kende, na tibagenderereti konyora eng’eria; tibakoinyorwa nonya ndinde.

English: Also their love, their hatred, and their envy has perished long ago; neither do they any longer have a portion forever in anything that is done under the sun.
Kiswahili: Upendo wao, chuki yao na wivu wao vimetoweka tangu kitambo, kamwe hawatakuwa tena na sehemu katika lolote linalotendeka chini ya jua.
Ekegusii: Obwanchani bwabo, na okogecha, ne ribero, bionsi ebio nigo biasirete amo nabarabwo. Tibabwati nonya ng’ake egetari kende ase ayio agokorwa aiga inse y’erioba.

English: Go your way—eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart; for God has already accepted your works.
Kiswahili: Nenda, kula chakula chako kwa furaha, unywe divai yako kwa moyo wa shangwe, kwa maana sasa Mungu anakubali unachofanya.
Ekegusii: Aye bono genda, orie endagera yao nomogooko, na onywe edivai yao kore nomosasoko ase enkoro yao, ekiagera Nyasae bwanchire emeremo yao.

English: Let your garments be always white, and don’t let your head lack oil.
Kiswahili: Daima uvae nguo nyeupe na daima upake kichwa chako mafuta.
Ekegusii: Tiga chianga chiao chibe chindabu botambe, na amaguta okweakwa tamocha ase omotwe oo.

English: Live joyfully with the wife whom you love all the days of your life of vanity, which he has given you under the sun, all your days of vanity, for that is your portion in life, and in your labor in which you labor under the sun.
Kiswahili: Furahia maisha na mke wako, umpendaye, siku zote za maisha ya ubatili uliyopewa na Mungu chini ya jua, siku zote za ubatili. Kwa maana hili ndilo fungu lako katika maisha na katika kazi yako ya taabu chini ya jua.
Ekegusii: Ase amatuko onsi ay’obogima obo bore bosa, obo Nyasae akoeire omenye aiga inse y’erioba, omenye nomogooko amo nomokuungu oo bwanchete. Okomenya nomogooko, nakio egetari kiao ase obogima obo, ekero ogendererete gwechanda ase emeremo emekong’u inse y’erioba.

English: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work, nor plan, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, where you are going.
Kiswahili: Lolote mkono wako upatalo kufanya, fanya kwa nguvu zako zote, kwa kuwa huko kuzimu, unakokwenda, hakuna kufanya kazi wala mipango wala maarifa wala hekima.
Ekegusii: Gento kende gionsi okoboko kwao koranyare gokora, gekore ne chinguru chiao chionsi; ekiagera agwo aase abakuure ase oragende, meremo ende tekaiyo, gose okorengereria, gose chisemi, gose obong’aini.

English: I returned and saw under the sun that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of skill; but time and chance happen to them all.
Kiswahili: Nimeona kitu kingine tena chini ya jua: Si wenye mbio washindao mashindano au wenye nguvu washindao vita, wala si wenye hekima wapatao chakula au wenye akili nyingi wapatao mali, wala wenye elimu wapatao upendeleo, lakini fursa huwapata wote.
Ekegusii: Nkarora aiga inse y’erioba ng’a tari abwo bakominyoka bwango bakobua, gose ababwate chinguru tari barabwo bakobua esegi, gose abare nobong’aini tari barabwo bakonyora endagera, gose abare nokomanya tari barabwo babwate chinibo, gose abanyasemi tari barabwo bakonyora ogwancherwa; korende kera omonto nigo akonyorwa nengaki yaye na egesio kiaye.

English: For man also doesn’t know his time. As the fish that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare, even so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falls suddenly on them.
Kiswahili: Zaidi ya hayo, hakuna mwanadamu ajuaye wakati saa yake itakapokuja: Kama vile samaki wavuliwavyo katika wavu mkatili, au ndege wanaswavyo kwenye mtego, vivyo hivyo wanadamu hunaswa na nyakati mbaya zinazowaangukia bila kutazamia.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera Mwanyabaanto onde tamanyeti engaki ya mabe. Buna koreng’ana chinswe chikobwatwa ase ekeonga ase egesio ekebe, ne chinyoni ase obosugunia, naboigo na Mwanyabaanto bakonyorwa nengaki embe, babwatwa mobosokano.

English: I have also seen wisdom under the sun in this way, and it seemed great to me.
Kiswahili: Pia niliona chini ya jua mfano huu wa hekima ambao ulinivutia sana:
Ekegusii: Nainde amang’ana aya naro naroche igoro y’obong’aini aiga inse y’erioba, naro akarorekana ase ’nde ng’a namanene;

English: There was a little city, and few men within it; and a great king came against it, besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it.
Kiswahili: Palikuwa na mji mdogo uliokuwa na watu wachache ndani yake. Mfalme mwenye nguvu akainuka dhidi yake, akauzunguka akaweka jeshi kubwa dhidi yake.
Ekegusii: Norenge omochie omoke omenyire nabaanto abake; omorwoti orenge omonene mono agacha koyorwania esegi; akayonaaria, akaagacha chiburi chinene chi’ogwekengera ase okoyorwania.

English: Now a poor wise man was found in it, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.
Kiswahili: Katika mji huo kulikuwepo mtu mmoja maskini lakini mwenye hekima, naye akauokoa ule mji kwa hekima yake. Lakini hakuna aliyemkumbuka yule maskini.
Ekegusii: Korende ase omochie oyio akanyorekana aroro omonto omotaka orenge omong’aini, na ase obong’aini bwaye agatooria omochie oria. Nonya naboigo, monto onde tari oinyorete omotaka oria.

English: Then I said, “Wisdom is better than strength.” Nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
