Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo, nikasema, “Hekima ni bora kuliko nguvu.” Lakini hekima ya maskini imedharauliwa, wala hakuna anayesikiliza maneno yake.
Ekegusii: Erio ngateeba, “Obong’aini nigo bore obuya mbobuete chinguru, nonya obong’aini bw’omonto oria omotaka bwachayetwe, na amang’ana aye tarenge koigwerwa.”

English: The words of the wise heard in quiet are better than the cry of him who rules among fools.
Kiswahili: Maneno ya utulivu ya mwenye hekima husikiwa kuliko makelele ya mtawala wa wapumbavu.
Ekegusii: Nigo ere buya gotegerera amang’ana omonto omong’aini agokwana ase obotoereru kobua gotegerera amang’ana ’omogambi ogoaka eriogi ase egati y’abanto abariri.

English: Wisdom is better than weapons of war; but one sinner destroys much good.
Kiswahili: Hekima ni bora kuliko silaha za vita, lakini mwenye dhambi mmoja huharibu mema mengi.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini nigo bore obuya kobua ebirwanero bi’esegi; korende omonyabibe oyomo nigo agosaria amaya amange.

English: Dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to produce an evil odor; so does a little folly outweigh wisdom and honor.
Kiswahili: Kama vile nzi waliokufa huacha harufu mbaya kwenye manukato, ndivyo upumbavu kidogo huzidi nguvu hekima na heshima.
Ekegusii: Chingi chikwete nigo chikogundia amaguta akweakwa atioka bobe; naboigo na oboriri obosinini bokobua obong’aini na amasikani.

English: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand, but a fool’s heart at his left.
Kiswahili: Moyo wa mwenye hekima huelekea kuume, lakini moyo wa mpumbavu huelekea kushoto.
Ekegusii: Enkoro y’omonto omong’aini nigo ekomoraa gochia borio, korende ey’omoriri nigo ekomoraa gochia bomosi.

English: Yes also when the fool walks by the way, his understanding fails him, and he says to everyone that he is a fool.
Kiswahili: Hata anapotembea barabarani, mpumbavu hukosa ufahamu na kudhihirisha kwa kila mmoja jinsi alivyo mpumbavu.
Ekegusii: Nonya nekero omonto omoriri agotaara inchera nigo akoborwa okomanya, na igo omanyia kera omonto ng’a ere nomoriri.

English: If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, don’t leave your place; for gentleness lays great offenses to rest.
Kiswahili: Kama hasira ya mtawala ikiwaka dhidi yako, usiache mahali pako, utulivu huweza kuzuia makosa mengi.
Ekegusii: Omogambi karabe nendamwamu asore, tobaisa gotiga emeremo yao, ekiagera oboremereria nigo boragere ebibe ebinene biaberwe.

English: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, the sort of error which proceeds from the ruler.
Kiswahili: Kuna ubaya niliouona chini ya jua, aina ya kosa litokalo kwa mtawala:
Ekegusii: Aiga inse y’erioba narorire obobe, na obobe obo nigo bokorentwa nabagaambi:

English: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a low place.
Kiswahili: Wapumbavu kuwekwa kwenye nafasi nyingi za juu, wakati matajiri hushika nafasi za chini.
Ekegusii: Omoriri nigo akoegwa amasikani amanene, ekero abanto abanda bagendererete goikaransa aase a inse.

English: I have seen servants on horses, and princes walking like servants on the earth.
Kiswahili: Mimi nimeona watumwa wamepanda farasi, wakati wakuu wakitembea kwa miguu kama watumwa.
Ekegusii: Narorire abasomba bariinete chibarasi, na abagaambi bagotaara namagoro buna abasomba.

English: He who digs a pit may fall into it; and whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
Kiswahili: Yeye achimbaye shimo aweza kutumbukia ndani yake, yeyote abomoaye ukuta anaweza kuumwa na nyoka.
Ekegusii: Omonto ogokunya engoro, nere oragwe imeo, na oyo okobochora enyasi, eng’iti engenda inse nemorome.

English: Whoever carves out stones may be injured by them. Whoever splits wood may be endangered by it.
Kiswahili: Yeyote apasuaye mawe inawezekana yakamuumiza, yeyote apasuaye magogo inawezekana yakamuumiza.
Ekegusii: Oyo ogwatia amagena nigo araakwe naro, na oyo ogwatia emete, ande nanyore obokong’u asero.

English: If the ax is blunt, and one doesn’t sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength; but skill brings success.
Kiswahili: Kama shoka ni butu na halikunolewa, nguvu nyingi zinahitajika, lakini ustadi utaleta mafanikio.
Ekegusii: Onye omonto tagotieria ekioma ekero giatuire, rirorio goika abeeke chinguru chinyinge ase ogokora emeremo nakerokio, korende obong’aini nigo bogokonya omonto abue.

English: If the snake bites before it is charmed, then is there no profit for the charmer’s tongue.
Kiswahili: Kama nyoka akiuma kabla ya kufanyiwa uaguzi, mwaguzi hatahitajika tena.
Ekegusii: Omoebia ching’iti ching’enda inse aise gotiga eng’iti emorome ritang’ani atarayeebia, rirorio omoebia oyio nigo arabe bosa.

English: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but a fool is swallowed by his own lips.
Kiswahili: Maneno yatokayo kinywani mwa mtu mwenye hekima yana neema, bali mpumbavu huangamizwa na midomo yake mwenyewe.
Ekegusii: Amang’ana akorua ase omonto omong’aini nigo akogera bwanchwa, korende aya akorua ase ebikoba bi’omoriri nigo akomosiria.

English: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
Kiswahili: Mwanzoni maneno yake ni upumbavu, mwishoni ni wazimu mbaya,
Ekegusii: Oyio omoriri nigo agochaka gokwana amang’ana ’oboriri, naende oyakoora nobobarimo obobe.

English: A fool also multiplies words. Man doesn’t know what will be; and that which will be after him, who can tell him?
Kiswahili: naye mpumbavu huzidisha maneno. Hakuna yeyote ajuaye linalokuja, ni nani awezaye kueleza ni jambo gani litakalotokea baada yake?
Ekegusii: Omoriri nigo are omonyamang’ana mange. Monto onde tamanyeti aya agochia koba. Ning’o oranyare komoteebia ekegochia koba korwa magega yaye.

English: The labor of fools wearies every one of them; for he doesn’t know how to go to the city.
Kiswahili: Kazi ya mpumbavu humchosha mwenyewe, hajui njia iendayo mjini.
Ekegusii: Emeremo y’omoriri nigo ekomoorosia, goika osinywa komanya enchera ekogenda ase omochie.

English: Woe to you, land, when your king is a child, and your princes eat in the morning!
Kiswahili: Ole wako, ee nchi ambayo mfalme wako alikuwa mtumwa na ambayo wakuu wako hufanya karamu asubuhi.
Ekegusii: Obobe nobwao, aye ense, ekero omorwoti oo are omwana, na abagaambi bao bakobeera ase emeyega y’okwegokia ase chingaki chia mambia.

English: Happy are you, land, when your king is the son of nobles, and your princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
Kiswahili: Heri wewe, ee nchi ambayo mfalme wako ni wa uzao wenye kuheshimika na ambayo wakuu wako hula chakula kwa wakati unaofaa: ili kupata nguvu na si kwa ajili ya ulevi.
Ekegusii: Nosesenirie aye ense, ekero omorwoti oo are omonto omosike na omosibore; na abarai bao bakoragera ase engaki egwenerete, ase okonyora chinguru, korende tari ase ogotinda.

English: By slothfulness the roof sinks in; and through idleness of the hands the house leaks.
Kiswahili: Kama mtu ni mvivu paa la nyumba huinama, kutokana na mikono milegevu, nyumba huvuja.
Ekegusii: Ekero omonto are omworo ekerama ki’enyomba yaye nigo gekogwa, na ase engencho y’obworo obwo embura nigo egotwa imeo.

English: A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes the life glad; and money is the answer for all things.
Kiswahili: Karamu hufanywa kwa ajili ya kicheko, nao mvinyo hufurahisha maisha, lakini fedha ni jawabu la mambo yote.
Ekegusii: Emeyega ye chindagera nigo ekorenta omogooko, na edivai nigo egokora omonto bweigwa buya, na ase chitaabu nonyare kogora ebinto bionsi.

English: Don’t curse the king, no, not in your thoughts; and don’t curse the rich in your bedroom, for a bird of the sky may carry your voice, and that which has wings may tell the matter.
Kiswahili: Usimshutumu mfalme hata ikiwa ni katika mawazo yako, au kumlaani tajiri katika chumba chako cha kulala, kwa sababu ndege wa angani wanaweza kuchukua maneno yako, naye ndege anayeruka anaweza kutoa taarifa ya yale uliyosema.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koragereria omorwoti nonya nase ebirengererio biao, gose tobaisa koragereria omonto omonda ekero ore ase akanyomba kao g’okorara. Oise gokora bo, enyoni nebaise koira amang’ana ao, gose egetongwa kere ne chimbaaba ngetebe amang’ana ayio.

English: Cast your bread on the waters; for you shall find it after many days.
Kiswahili: Tupa mkate wako juu ya maji, kwa maana baada ya siku nyingi utaupata tena.
Ekegusii: Eteria endagera yao igoro ye chinyancha, na magega y’amatuko amange nekoiranere.

English: Give a portion to seven, yes, even to eight; for you don’t know what evil will be on the earth.
Kiswahili: Wape sehemu watu saba, naam hata wanane, kwa maana hujui ni baa gani litakalokuwa juu ya nchi.
Ekegusii: Atanana ebi obwate oe abanto batano na babere, gose batano na batato, ekiagera tomanyeti amabe agochia konyora ense.

English: If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves on the earth; and if a tree falls toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falls, there shall it be.
Kiswahili: Kama mawingu yamejaa maji, hunyesha mvua juu ya nchi. Kama mti ukianguka kuelekea kusini au kuelekea kaskazini, mahali ulipoangukia, hapo ndipo utakapolala.
Ekegusii: Amare gaichoire nembura, nigo embura eyio egotwa igoro ase ense, na omote koragwe ororie ensemo ya Irianyi gose eya sugusu, nigo oragenderere kobeera inse agwo ase ogwete.

English: He who observes the wind won’t sow; and he who regards the clouds won’t reap.
Kiswahili: Yeyote atazamaye upepo hatapanda, yeyote aangaliaye mawingu hatavuna.
Ekegusii: Omonto okona‐korigereria komanya igoro y’embeo tagosimeka, na oyo okona‐korigereria amare buna are takogesa.

English: As you don’t know what is the way of the wind, nor how the bones grow in the womb of her who is with child; even so you don’t know the work of God who does all.
Kiswahili: Kama vile usivyofahamu njia ya upepo, au jinsi mwili uumbwavyo ndani ya tumbo la mama, vivyo hivyo huwezi kufahamu kazi ya Mungu, Muumba wa vitu vyote.
Ekegusii: Buna otamanyeti ase embeo ekogusa gochia, gose buna amauga ’omwana ore ase enda ya ng’ina agokina, naboigo tokonyara komanya emeremo ya Nyasae oyio ogokora amang’ana onsi.

English: In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening don’t withhold your hand; for you don’t know which will prosper, whether this or that, or whether they both will be equally good.
Kiswahili: Panda mbegu yako asubuhi, nako jioni usiruhusu mikono yako ilegee, kwa maana hujui ni ipi itakayofanikiwa, kwamba ni hii au ni ile, au kwamba zote zitafanikiwa sawasawa.
Ekegusii: Busura embusuro yao mambia, nonya mogoroba totiga koyebusura, ekiagera tomanyeti eye erame, neye gose neria, gose nchionsi amo chirame buya.

English: Truly the light is sweet, and it is a pleasant thing for the eyes to see the sun.
Kiswahili: Nuru ni tamu, tena inafurahisha macho kuona jua.
Ekegusii: Omobaso nigo ore omwansu, na amaiso nigo akogokigwa korora erioba.

English: Yes, if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all; but let him remember the days of darkness, for they shall be many. All that comes is vanity.
Kiswahili: Hata kama mtu ataishi miaka mingi kiasi gani, na aifurahie yote. Lakini na akumbuke siku za giza, kwa maana zitakuwa nyingi. Kila kitu kitakachokuja ni ubatili.
Ekegusii: Omonto karagenderere koba moyo ase engaki y’emiaka emenge, tiga agokere engaki eyio yonsi, korende goika ainyore ng’a amatuko ’omosunte nabe amange mono. Onsi aya agochi‐gocha nigo are bosa.

English: Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth, and walk in the ways of your heart, and in the sight of your eyes; but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
Kiswahili: Furahi ewe kijana, wakati ungali kijana, moyo wako na ukupe furaha katika siku za ujana wako. Fuata njia za moyo wako na chochote macho yako yaonayo, lakini ujue kwamba kwa ajili ya haya yote Mungu atakuleta hukumuni.
Ekegusii: Aye omosae, gokera engaki y’obosae bwao, tiga enkoro yao ekorentere omogooko ase amatuko ’obosae bwao; bwatia chinchera chi’okogania gw’enkoro yao, na aya amaiso ao akorora. Korende oinyore ng’a ase ayio onsi Nyasae nakorangerie ase ekiina.

English: Therefore remove sorrow from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh; for youth and the dawn of life are vanity.
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo basi, ondoa wasiwasi moyoni mwako na utupilie mbali masumbufu ya mwili wako, kwa kuwa ujana na nguvu ni ubatili.
Ekegusii: Ase ayio tiga aya akogochanda arue ase enkoro yao, na aya akorenta obororo ase omobere oo arue boigo, ekiagera obosae na obuya bw’obogima nigo bore bosa.

English: Remember also your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come, and the years draw near, when you will say, “I have no pleasure in them;”
Kiswahili: Mkumbuke Muumba wako siku za ujana wako, kabla hazijaja siku za taabu, wala haijakaribia miaka utakaposema, “Mimi sifurahii hiyo”:
Ekegusii: Moinyore Omotongi oo ekero ore omosae, ekero amatuko amabe ataracha, na emiaka eyio emebe etaraika ang’e ekero oratebe, “Tindi nomogooko koba moyo ase engaki buna eye!”

English: Before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars are darkened, and the clouds return after the rain;
Kiswahili: kabla jua na nuru, nao mwezi na nyota havijatiwa giza, kabla ya kurudi mawingu baada ya mvua;
Ekegusii: Omoinyore ekero erioba, na omobaso, na omotienyi, ne ching’enang’eni, bitarabekwa omosunte, gose amare atarairanerana embura koyature.

English: in the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those who look out of the windows are darkened,
Kiswahili: siku ile walinzi wa nyumba watakapotetemeka, nao watu wenye nguvu watakapojiinamisha, wakati wasagao watakapokoma kwa sababu ya uchache, nao wachunguliao madirishani kutiwa giza;
Ekegusii: Engaki eyio abarendi b’enyomba mbaiguswe, na abasacha bare ne chinguru bekumbe, na abagosia batige gosia ekiagera bare abake ase omobaro, na abwo batengerete korwa ase ebibao, batubwe norotutu tibarora buya.

English: and the doors shall be shut in the street; when the sound of the grinding is low, and one shall rise up at the voice of a bird, and all the daughters of music shall be brought low;
Kiswahili: wakati milango ya kuingia barabarani itakapofungwa na sauti ya kusaga kufifia; wakati watu wataamshwa kwa sauti ya ndege, lakini nyimbo zao zote zikififia;
Ekegusii: Ebisieri birochie ase chinchera mbisiekwe, na amariogi ay’ogosia nakee; amariogi e chinyoni natabobore omonto korwa ase chitoro, na amariogi ’abaiseke bagotera nakee.

English: yes, they shall be afraid of heights, and terrors will be on the way; and the almond tree shall blossom, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail; because man goes to his everlasting home, and the mourners go about the streets;
Kiswahili: wakati watu watakapoogopa kilichoinuka juu na hatari zitakazokuwepo barabarani; wakati mlozi utakapochanua maua na panzi kujikokota nawe usiwe na shauku ya kitu chochote. Ndipo mwanadamu aiendea nyumba yake ya milele nao waombolezaji wakizunguka barabarani.
Ekegusii: Abanto nigo barabe nobwoba ase ebitiiro, na okogoswa kobe ase chinchera. Emelozi nesiche, na ebisase bibe bikwagura ng’ora ng’ora, na okogania gwonsi ngosire. Eyio nengaki Mwanyabaanto aragende ase obomenyo bwaye bwa kare na kare; abakona‐korera mbabe bakomochiera ekero ase ekero.

English: before the silver cord is severed, or the golden bowl is broken, or the pitcher is broken at the spring, or the wheel broken at the cistern,
Kiswahili: Mkumbuke Muumba wako: kabla haijakatika kamba ya fedha, au bakuli la dhahabu halijavunjika; kabla mtungi kuvunjika kwenye chemchemi, au gurudumu kuvunjika kisimani,
Ekegusii: Engori eroisirie korwa ase efeta nebutorwe, na egetaabo keroisirie korwa ase etaabu ngiatwe, na enyongo yatwe agwo ase ensoko y’amaache, na ekebara‐bara nkebunwe agwo ase egesima ki’amaache.

English: and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
Kiswahili: nayo mavumbi kurudi ardhini yalikotoka, na roho kurudi kwa Mungu aliyeitoa.
Ekegusii: Erio orotu ndoirane, ase riroba buna rwarenge, na omoika oirane gochia ase Nyasae oria oyoruete.

English: “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher. “All is vanity!”
Kiswahili: Mhubiri asema, “Ubatili! Ubatili! Kila kitu ni ubatili!”
Ekegusii: Ase ayio omorandia nigo agoteeba. Aya mbosa, bosa; onsi mbosa kegima.

English: Further, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge. Yes, he pondered, sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
Kiswahili: Mhubiri hakuwa tu na hekima, bali aliwagawia watu maarifa pia. Alitafakari na kutafiti na akaweka katika utaratibu mithali nyingi.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera omorandia oria arenge omong’aini, akagenderera kworokereria abanto chisemi na korua ogosemia okuya. Agasangereria na gotuka, naende akaroisia emereng’anio emenge.

English: The Preacher sought to find out acceptable words, and that which was written blamelessly, words of truth.
Kiswahili: Mhubiri alitafiti ili kupata maneno sahihi na kila alichoandika kilikuwa sawa na kweli.
Ekegusii: Akarigia konyora amang’ana arenge kogokia, akarika amang’ana ’ekeene ase oboronge.

English: The words of the wise are like goads; and like nails well fastened are words from the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.
Kiswahili: Maneno ya wenye hekima ni kama mchokoro, mithali zao zilizokusanywa pamoja ni kama misumari iliyogongomewa ikawa imara, yaliyotolewa na Mchungaji mmoja.
Ekegusii: Amang’ana abanto abang’aini bagokwana nigo anga buna chimbambo chinyoge, na aya basangereirie anga buna emesumari eakeire bokong’u. Ayio onsi nebiegwa korwa ase Omorisia oyomo.

English: Furthermore, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
Kiswahili: Tena zaidi ya hayo, mwanangu, kubali maonyo, hakuna mwisho wa kutunga vitabu vingi, nako kusoma sana huuchosha mwili.
Ekegusii: Aye omwana one, kobua ase aya onsi, igwera ogokuurerwa oko. Okorika ebitabu ebinge tikori nomoerio; ogosoma okonge nigo gokorosia omobere.

English: This is the end of the matter. All has been heard. Fear God and keep his commandments; for this is the whole duty of man.
Kiswahili: Hii ndiyo jumla ya maneno; yote yamekwisha sikiwa: Mche Mungu, nawe uzishike amri zake, maana kwa jumla ndiyo impasayo mtu.
Ekegusii: Amang’ana onsi aigurwe, Omoerio bw’amang’ana onsi noyo: Omoiroke Nyasae na obwate amachiiko aye, ekiagera ayio naro abanto bonsi bagwenerete bakore.

English: For God will bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether it is good, or whether it is evil.
Kiswahili: Kwa maana Mungu ataleta hukumuni kila kazi, pamoja na kila neno la siri, likiwa jema au baya.
Ekegusii: Nyasae narente kera ogokora ase ekiina ekero aranachere obobisi bwonsi ekiina, karabe amaya gose amabe.

English: The Song of songs, which is Solomon’s.
Kiswahili: Wimbo ulio bora wa Solomoni.
Ekegusii: Ogoteera gwa Sulemani okwo kore okuya goetania amatera onsi.

English: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth; for your love is better than wine.
Kiswahili: Unibusu kwa busu la kinywa chako, kwa maana upendo wako unafurahisha kuliko divai.
Ekegusii: Tiga anyunyunte nokonyunyunta kw’omonwa oye. Ekiagera obwanchani bwao nobuya kobua edivai.

English: Your oils have a pleasing fragrance. Your name is oil poured out, therefore the virgins love you.
Kiswahili: Manukato yako yananukia vizuri, jina lako ni kama manukato yaliyomiminwa. Ndiyo sababu wanawali wanakupenda!
Ekegusii: Amaguta ao akweakwa nigo are ne rimisu rigiya; erieta riao nigo ringa buna amaguta aumoirwe, ase ayio abakungu nigo bagwanchete.

English: Take me away with you. Let’s hurry. The king has brought me into his rooms. Friends We will be glad and rejoice in you. We will praise your love more than wine! Beloved They are right to love you.
Kiswahili: Nichukue twende nawe, na tufanye haraka! Mfalme na anilete ndani ya vyumba vyake. Marafiki Tunakushangilia na kukufurahia, tutasifu upendo wako zaidi kuliko divai. Mpendwa Tazama jinsi ilivyo bora wakupende!
Ekegusii: Ing’use nkobwatie, tominyoke kogenda. Omorwoti ondetire ase enyomba yaye. Ntokogokere na kogochengera, ntotogie obwanchani bwao kobua edivai. Ekeene, nakio abakungu bagwancherete.

English: I am dark, but lovely, you daughters of Jerusalem, like Kedar’s tents, like Solomon’s curtains.
Kiswahili: Mimi ni mweusi, lakini napendeza, enyi binti za Yerusalemu, mweusi kama mahema ya Kedari, kama mapazia ya hema la Solomoni.
Ekegusii: Inwe abakungu ba Yerusalemu, inche nigo inde omomwamu ti, noyo bw’okogokia. Nigo inga buna chiema chia Kedari, naende buna ebitambaa bi’ogosungwa bia Sulemani.

English: Don’t stare at me because I am dark, because the sun has scorched me. My mother’s sons were angry with me. They made me keeper of the vineyards. I haven’t kept my own vineyard.
Kiswahili: Usinikazie macho kwa sababu mimi ni mweusi, kwa sababu nimefanywa mweusi na jua. Wana wa mama yangu walinikasirikia na kunifanya niwe mtunza mashamba ya mizabibu. Shamba langu mwenyewe la mizabibu nimeliacha.
Ekegusii: Timobaisa kondigereria, ekiagera inde omomwamu ti; nomobaso bw’erioba onsambire. Abamura ba baba nigo bambeete, bakambeeka korenda emegondo y’emesabibu, korende omogondo one bw’emesabibu tinarendete.

English: Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you graze your flock, where you rest them at noon; for why should I be as one who is veiled beside the flocks of your companions?
Kiswahili: Niambie, wewe ambaye ninakupenda, unalisha wapi kundi lako la kondoo na ni wapi unapowapumzisha kondoo wako adhuhuri. Kwa nini niwe kama mwanamke aliyefunikwa shela karibu na makundi ya rafiki zako?
Ekegusii: Aye omwanchi bw’omoyo one, nteebie ng’ai okorisia riicho riao. Ng’ai okoriira riakenderera mobaso gati? Nase ki ndabe nkona‐gotayaya ase egati y’amaicho ’abagisangio bao?

English: If you don’t know, most beautiful among women, follow the tracks of the sheep. Graze your young goats beside the shepherds’ tents.
Kiswahili: Kama hujui, ewe mwanamke mzuri kuliko wote, fuata nyayo za kondoo, na kulisha wana-mbuzi wako karibu na hema za wachungaji.
Ekegusii: Aye ore omoseera kobua abakungu bonsi; onye tomanyeti, bwatia amabarato e riicho, obe gokorisia chimanwa chiao chie chimbori ang’e ne chiema chi’abarisia.

English: I have compared you, my love, to a steed in Pharaoh’s chariots.
Kiswahili: Mpenzi wangu, ninakufananisha na farasi jike aliyefungwa katika mojawapo ya magari ya vita ya Farao.
Ekegusii: Aye omwanchi one, nigo ngokoreng’ania nebarasi eaberi ekong’usa egari ya Farao.

English: Your cheeks are beautiful with earrings, your neck with strings of jewels.
Kiswahili: Mashavu yako yanapendeza yakiwa na vipuli, shingo yako ikiwa na mikufu ya vito.
Ekegusii: Chinsea chiao nechinseera, chichabeire n’ebinto bi’oboseera, ne rigoti riao nigo richabeire ne chisonoi.

English: We will make you earrings of gold, with studs of silver.
Kiswahili: Tutakufanyia vipuli vya dhahabu, vyenye kupambwa kwa fedha.
Ekegusii: Intwe ntokoroiserie ebinyuri bie chitaabu bi’ogwechabera, ebitonire ne chifeta.

English: While the king sat at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.
Kiswahili: Wakati mfalme alipokuwa mezani pake, manukato yangu yalisambaza harufu yake nzuri.
Ekegusii: Ekero omorwoti arenge aase aye agotimokera, amaguta aane akorokwa narada agatioka rimisu rigiya.

English: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh, that lies between my breasts.
Kiswahili: Mpenzi wangu kwangu mimi ni kifuko cha manemane kati ya matiti yangu.
Ekegusii: Omwanchi one nigo are ase ’nde buna omobuko o manemane, oyo nkobeeka ase egekuba kiane gati gati yechimbeere chiane.

English: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms from the vineyards of En Gedi.
Kiswahili: Mpenzi wangu kwangu mimi ni kama kishada cha maua ya mhina kutoka mashamba ya mizabibu ya En-Gedi.
Ekegusii: Omwanchi one nigo are ase ’nde buna egesago ki’ebisicha bikorokwa hena, bire ase emegondo y’emesabibu y’Eni‐Gedi.

English: Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves.
Kiswahili: Tazama jinsi ulivyo mzuri, mpenzi wangu! Tazama jinsi ulivyo mzuri! Macho yako ni kama ya hua.
Ekegusii: Naama! Aye omwanchi one, naki ore omoseera mono! Ee, nabo ore omoseera mono. Ekieni ki’amaiso ao nigo kenga eki’amaruma.

English: Behold, you are beautiful, my beloved, yes, pleasant; and our couch is verdant.
Kiswahili: Tazama jinsi ulivyo mzuri, mpenzi wangu! Ee, tazama jinsi unavyopendeza! Na kitanda chetu ni cha majani mazuri.
Ekegusii: Aye omwanchi one, nigo ore omoseera. Ee, aye nigo ore oyo bw’okogokia, oborere bwaito nigo borabe obonyansi bore machani.

English: The beams of our house are cedars. Our rafters are firs.
Kiswahili: Nguzo za nyumba yetu ni mierezi, na mapao yetu ni miberoshi.
Ekegusii: Ebisigisa bi’enyomba yaito nebi’emecharake, ne chindote nechi’emetarakwa.

English: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.
Kiswahili: Mimi ni ua la Sharoni, yungiyungi ya bondeni.
Ekegusii: Inche nigo inga egesicha gia Saroni gekorokwa rosi, naende egesicha ekiya kie rikura.

English: As a lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
Kiswahili: Kama yungiyungi katikati ya miiba ndivyo alivyo mpenzi wangu katikati ya wanawali.
Ekegusii: Ee, koreng’ana buna egesicha ekiya kere ase egati y’amagwa, naboigo omwanchi one are ase egati y’abaiseke.

English: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, his fruit was sweet to my taste.
Kiswahili: Kama mti wa mtofaa miongoni mwa miti ya msituni ndivyo alivyo mpenzi wangu miongoni mwa wanaume vijana. Ninafurahia kuketi kivulini mwa mwanaume huyu, na tunda lake ni tamu kwangu.
Ekegusii: Koreng’ana buna omote bw’amapera osimekire ase egati y’emete y’orosana, naboigo omwanchi one are ase egati y’abamura. Nigo ngokirie goikaransa ase ekiriri kiaye, na amatunda aye akanyansera.

English: He brought me to the banquet hall. His banner over me is love.
Kiswahili: Amenichukua mpaka kwenye ukumbi wa karamu, na bendera ya huyu mwanaume juu yangu ni upendo.
Ekegusii: Ere akang’ira ase enyomba y’omoyega, na obwanchani bwaye nigo bore buna ebendera igoro yane.

English: Strengthen me with raisins, refresh me with apples; for I am faint with love.
Kiswahili: Nitie nguvu kwa zabibu kavu, niburudishe kwa matofaa, kwa maana ninazimia kwa mapenzi.
Ekegusii: Inyigotie na amasabibu amomo na ongokie na amapera, ekiagera amaiga ’obwanchani anyarire.

English: His left hand is under my head. His right hand embraces me.
Kiswahili: Mkono wake wa kushoto uko chini ya kichwa changu, na mkono wake wa kuume unanikumbatia.
Ekegusii: Okoboko kwaye kwa bomosi nigo kore inse y’omotwe one, na okwa borio nigo komboanetie.

English: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.
Kiswahili: Binti za Yerusalemu, ninawaagiza kwa paa na kwa ayala wa shambani: Msichochee wala kuamsha mapenzi hata yatakapotaka yenyewe.
Ekegusii: Inwe abakungu ba Yerusalemu, nigo nkobasorora, nkobatiania ase chingabi ne chinsune chi’orosana ng’a timobaisa gotabobora obwanchani, gose koboichania, goika bobe Engaki yaye yaikeranire.

English: The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes, leaping on the mountains, skipping on the hills.
Kiswahili: Sikiliza! Mpenzi wangu! Tazama! Huyu hapa anakuja, akirukaruka juu milimani akizunguka juu ya vilima.
Ekegusii: Tegerera moigwe eriogi ri’omwanchi one! Rora oyio ogocha! Nigo agocharoka‐charoka igoro ase ebitunwa, na gocharara ase ebigoro.

English: My beloved is like a roe or a young deer. Behold, he stands behind our wall! He looks in at the windows. He glances through the lattice.
Kiswahili: Mpenzi wangu ni kama paa au ayala kijana. Tazama! Anasimama nyuma ya ukuta wetu, akitazama kupitia madirishani, akichungulia kimiani.
Ekegusii: Omwanchi one nigo anga engabi gose ensune ensae. Rora, bono nigo ateneine magega y’enyasi y’enyomba yaito. Origereretie gocha ime goetera ase chitirisa, goetera ase ekebao kiabekire ebitange.

English: My beloved spoke, and said to me, “Rise up, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.
Kiswahili: Mpenzi wangu alizungumza na kuniambia, “Inuka, mpenzi wangu, mrembo wangu, tufuatane.
Ekegusii: Omwanchi ngokwana are na gonteebia. (Omonyuomi) Aye omwanchi one, nigo ore omuya, imoka, inchwo togende,

English: For behold, the winter is past. The rain is over and gone.
Kiswahili: Tazama! Wakati wa masika umepita, mvua imekwisha na ikapita.
Ekegusii: ekiagera bono engaki y’etoigo yaerire, boigo engaki y’embura yaerire ne mbura yachiire.

English: The flowers appear on the earth. The time of the singing has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.
Kiswahili: Maua yanatokea juu ya nchi; majira ya kuimba yamewadia, sauti za njiwa zinasikika katika nchi yetu.
Ekegusii: Ebisicha biasichire ase ense, engaki y’amatera yaikire, ee, eriogi ri’amatera ’amaruma riaigurwe ase ense yaito.

English: The fig tree ripens her green figs. The vines are in blossom. They give out their fragrance. Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.”
Kiswahili: Mtini unatunga matunda yake ya mwanzoni, zabibu zinazochanua zaeneza harufu nzuri. Inuka, njoo mpenzi wangu. Mrembo wangu, tufuatane.”
Ekegusii: Emeko yachakire kwama amako, na emesabibu yachakire gosicha, nigo egotioka rimisu rigiya. Aye omosani one omuya, imoka togende!

English: My dove in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding places of the mountainside, let me see your face. Let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet and your face is lovely.
Kiswahili: Hua wangu penye nyufa za majabali, mafichoni pembezoni mwa mlima, nionyeshe uso wako, na niisikie sauti yako, kwa maana sauti yako ni tamu, na uso wako unapendeza.
Ekegusii: Aye riruma riane ore ase omwenya bw’egetare, agwo ase obwebiso bw’egetare, tiga indore obosio bwao, naende inyigwe eriogi riao, ekiagera eriogi riao neriansu, na obosio bwao noboseera.

English: Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that plunder the vineyards; for our vineyards are in blossom.
Kiswahili: Tukamatie mbweha, mbweha wale wadogo wanaoharibu mashamba ya mizabibu, mashamba yetu ya mizabibu yaliyochanua.
Ekegusii: Tobwatere ebibwe, ebibwe biria ebike, ebio bigosaria emegondo y’emesabibu, korwa ekero emesabibu yaito yasichete.

English: My beloved is mine, and I am his. He browses among the lilies.
Kiswahili: Mpenzi wangu ni wangu, nami ni wake, yeye hujilisha katikati ya yungiyungi.
Ekegusii: Inche nigo inde oyo bw’omwanchi one, nere noyone; nigo akorisia riicho riaye ase egati y’ebisicha ebiya.

English: Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be like a roe or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.
Kiswahili: Mpaka jua linapochomoza, na vivuli vikimbie, rudi, mpenzi wangu, na uwe kama paa, au kama ayala kijana juu ya vilima vya Betheri.
Ekegusii: Ekero rigochia kogoroba na emerengari egochia gosira, aye omwanchi one, onchoka gocha ase ’nde, ominyoke buna engabi, gose buna ensune ensae igoro ase egetunwa kere chinchwara.

English: By night on my bed, I sought him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.
Kiswahili: Usiku kucha kwenye kitanda changu nilimtafuta yule moyo wangu umpendaye; nilimtafuta, lakini sikumpata.
Ekegusii: Botuko ekero naraire borere bwane, nkamorigia oria omoyo one bwanchete, nkamorigia, korende tinamonyora.

English: I will get up now, and go about the city; in the streets and in the squares I will seek him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.
Kiswahili: Sasa nitaondoka na kuzunguka mjini, katika barabara zake na viwanja; nitamtafuta yule moyo wangu umpendaye. Kwa hiyo nilimtafuta lakini sikumpata.
Ekegusii: “Erio nkaimoka nkagenda ase omochie, ng’aeta ase chinchera chiaye na ase ebiooreri biaye, nkarigia omwanchi bw’omoyo one.” Nkamorigia, korende tinamonyora.

English: The watchmen who go about the city found me; “Have you seen him whom my soul loves?”
Kiswahili: Walinzi walinikuta walipokuwa wakizunguka mji. Nikawauliza, “Je, mmemwona yule moyo wangu umpendaye?”
Ekegusii: Ekero abarendi barenge goetanana omochie koyorata, bakanyoora inche, na inche nkababooria, “Mwarora omwanchi bw’omoyo one?”

English: I had scarcely passed from them, when I found him whom my soul loves. I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother’s house, into the room of her who conceived me.
Kiswahili: Kitambo kidogo tu baada ya kuwapita nilimpata yule moyo wangu umpendaye. Nilimshika na sikumwachia aende mpaka nilipomleta katika nyumba ya mama yangu, katika chumba cha yule aliyenichukua mimba.
Ekegusii: Ase obwango obwo naruete ase abarendi abwo, nkanyora omwanchi bw’omoyo one. Nkamotarera tinamotiga agende; nigo namorentete mwa baba, nkamosoyia gochia ase akanyomba gokorara.

English: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up nor awaken love, until it so desires.
Kiswahili: Binti za Yerusalemu, ninawaagiza kwa paa na kwa ayala wa shambani: Msichochee wala kuamsha mapenzi hata yatakapotaka yenyewe.
Ekegusii: Inwe abakungu ba Yerusalemu, nigo nkobasorora, nkobatiania ase chingabi na ase chinsune chi’orosana ng’a timobaisa gotabobora obwa’nchani gose koboichania, goika bobe bwancheranire obonyene.

English: Who is this who comes up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all spices of the merchant?
Kiswahili: Ni nani huyu anayekuja kutoka jangwani kama nguzo ya moshi, anayenukia manemane na uvumba iliyotengenezwa kwa vikolezo vyote vya mfanyabiashara?
Ekegusii: Ngeto ki keria kegocha korwa ase erooro kenga buna rikundesi ri’erioki? Ninki eke keagete amaguta a manemane na ubani, ebinto ebio bikoonigwa nabakori ebiasara.

English: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage! Sixty mighty men are around it, of the mighty men of Israel.
Kiswahili: Tazama! Ni gari la Solomoni lisindikizwalo na mashujaa sitini, walio wakuu sana wa Israeli,
Ekegusii: Rora aaria, ekerogo gi’okobogoreria Sulemani, geetananire nabasaacha emerongo etano nomo, abare chituoni chi’Abaisraeli.

English: They all handle the sword, and are expert in war. Every man has his sword on his thigh, because of fear in the night.
Kiswahili: wote wamevaa panga, wote wazoefu katika vita, kila mmoja na upanga wake pajani, wamejiandaa kwa ajili ya hofu za usiku.
Ekegusii: Abwo bonsi nigo beboeranetie emeyio ya birende, na nigo bare abanto bamanyete korwana esegi. Kera oyomo nigo abogoreti omoyio obirende, orendete ase okogoswa kwa botuko.

English: King Solomon made himself a carriage of the wood of Lebanon.
Kiswahili: Mfalme Solomoni alijitengenezea gari; alilitengeneza kwa mbao kutoka Lebanoni.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti Sulemani nigo eroiseretie ekerogo keria korwa ase emete ya Lebanoni.

English: He made its pillars of silver, its bottom of gold, its seat of purple, the middle of it being paved with love, from the daughters of Jerusalem.
Kiswahili: Nguzo zake alizitengeneza kwa fedha, kitako chake kwa dhahabu. Kiti chake kilipambwa kwa zambarau, gari lake likanakshiwa njumu kwa upendo na binti za Yerusalemu.
Ekegusii: Amagoro aye kegotenenera nigo aroiseirie chifeta, na ekiegeko kiaye nigo kiaroiseirie chitaabu; egeikaransero kiaye nigo giatubire negetambaa kere monyinga. Abakungu ba Yerusalemu nigo bagechaberete ime, bare nomoyo bw’ogwancha.

English: Go out, you daughters of Zion, and see King Solomon, with the crown with which his mother has crowned him, in the day of his weddings, in the day of the gladness of his heart.
Kiswahili: Tokeni nje, ninyi binti za Sayuni, mkamtazame Mfalme Solomoni akiwa amevaa taji, taji ambalo mama yake alimvika siku ya arusi yake, siku ambayo moyo wake ulishangilia.
Ekegusii: Inwe abasubati ba Sayoni, inchwo morore Sulemani omorwoti obegeete ekiore keria ng’ina amobeekerete ase rituko riria Sulemani akoreretwe enyangi, rituko riria ri’omogooko bw’enkoro yaye.

English: Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is as a flock of goats, that descend from Mount Gilead.
Kiswahili: Tazama jinsi ulivyo mzuri, mpenzi wangu! Ee, jinsi ulivyo mzuri! Macho yako nyuma ya shela yako ni kama ya hua. Nywele zako ni kama kundi la mbuzi zikishuka kutoka Mlima Gileadi.
Ekegusii: Aye omwanchi one, naki ore omoseera! Naama! Nigo ore omoseera! Korwa ime y’egietubo kiao ekieni ki’amaiso ao nigo kenga eki’amaruma; etukia yao nigo enga buna riicho rie chimbori, nigo chigotirimboka ase ebitirimboko bia Gileadi.

English: Your teeth are like a newly shorn flock, which have come up from the washing, where every one of them has twins. None is bereaved among them.
Kiswahili: Meno yako ni kama kundi la kondoo waliokatwa manyoya sasa hivi, watokao kuogeshwa. Kila mmoja ana pacha lake, hakuna hata mmoja aliye peke yake.
Ekegusii: Amaino ao nigo anga ching’ondi chiaaberi chianachirwe amarionya, chiarure gosibigwa chiarabire se, chionsi nigo chikobiara chisare, na manwa ende teri gokwa.

English: Your lips are like scarlet thread. Your mouth is lovely. Your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind your veil.
Kiswahili: Midomo yako ni kama uzi mwekundu, kinywa chako kinapendeza. Mashavu yako nyuma ya shela yako ni kama vipande viwili vya komamanga.
Ekegusii: Ebikoba biao nigo binga eusi embariri, omonwa oo nigo ore oyo bw’okogokia, chinsea chiao chitubire ime ase egietubo kiao; nigo chinga buna ebing’ese bie ritunda rikorokwa rikomomanga.

English: Your neck is like David’s tower built for an armory, on which a thousand shields hang, all the shields of the mighty men.
Kiswahili: Shingo yako ni kama mnara wa Daudi, uliojengwa kwa madaha, juu yake zimetundikwa ngao elfu, zote ni ngao za mashujaa.
Ekegusii: Rigoti riao nigo ringa buna omoorobiri o Daudi, oyio oagachetwe nao ebirwanero bw’esegi biare kogachwa. Agwo nao chinguba elifu eyemo chisungire, chionsi nigo chire echi’abasikari bare chituoni.

English: Your two breasts are like two fawns that are twins of a roe, which feed among the lilies.
Kiswahili: Matiti yako mawili ni kama wana-paa wawili, kama wana-paa mapacha wajilishao katikati ya yungiyungi.
Ekegusii: Chimbeere chiao ibere nigo chinga buna chimanwa ibere buna chisare chi’engabi chikorisia agwo ase egati y’ebisicha ebiya.

English: Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, I will go to the mountain of myrrh, to the hill of frankincense.
Kiswahili: Hata kupambazuke na vivuli vikimbie, nitakwenda kwenye mlima wa manemane na kwenye kilima cha uvumba.
Ekegusii: Ekero bogochi koira na emerengari egochia gosira, ningende ase egetunwa ase manemane ekoruerwa na ase ekegoro ki’ogosambera ubani.

English: You are all beautiful, my love. There is no spot in you.
Kiswahili: Wewe ni mzuri kote, mpenzi wangu, hakuna hitilafu ndani yako.
Ekegusii: Aye omwanchi one, nigo ore omoseera bori, tori na kemoa kende!

English: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, with me from Lebanon. Look from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the lions’ dens, from the mountains of the leopards.
Kiswahili: Enda nami kutoka Lebanoni, bibi arusi wangu, enda nami kutoka Lebanoni. Shuka kutoka ncha ya Amana, kutoka juu ya Seniri, kilele cha Hermoni, kutoka mapango ya simba na kutoka mlima wapendapo kukaa chui.
Ekegusii: Aye omoriakari one, togende torue aa Lebanoni, torue Lebanoni, togende komo. Otirimboke korwa ase egechuria ki’egetunwa ki’Amana, na ekia Seniri na Herimoni. Orue ase amakuruma e chindo, na ase ebitunwa chingo chimenyete.

English: You have ravished my heart, my sister, my bride. You have ravished my heart with one of your eyes, with one chain of your neck.
Kiswahili: Umeiba moyo wangu, dada yangu, bibi arusi wangu; umeiba moyo wangu kwa mtazamo mmoja wa macho yako, kwa kito kimoja cha mkufu wako.
Ekegusii: Aye moiseke ominto, omoriakari one, kwang’usire enkoro yane na kwangokirie, okorigereria kw’amaiso ao kwang’usire enkoro yane, ee, esonoi eyemo yoka ye chisonoi chia igoti riao yang’usire.

English: How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! How much better is your love than wine, the fragrance of your perfumes than all kinds of spices!
Kiswahili: Tazama jinsi pendo lako linavyofurahisha, dada yangu, bibi arusi wangu! Pendo lako linafurahisha aje zaidi ya divai, na harufu ya manukato yako zaidi ya kikolezo chochote!
Ekegusii: Aye moiseke ominto, omoriakari one, obwanchani bwao naki bore obuya mono! Naki bore obuya mono kobua edivai! Ne rimisu ri’amaguta ao ogweaka nigo ribuete ebinsari bionsi!

English: Your lips, my bride, drip like the honeycomb. Honey and milk are under your tongue. The smell of your garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
Kiswahili: Midomo yako inadondosha utamu kama sega la asali, bibi arusi wangu; maziwa na asali viko chini ya ulimi wako. Harufu nzuri ya mavazi yako ni kama ile ya Lebanoni.
Ekegusii: Aye omoriakari one, ebikoba biao nigo bikonyororokia obooke; obooke na amabeere nigo bire inse y’oromeme rwao. Rimisu rie chianga chiao nigo ringa eria Lebanoni.

English: My sister, my bride, is a locked up garden; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain.
Kiswahili: Wewe ni bustani iliyofungwa, dada yangu, bibi arusi wangu; wewe ni chanzo cha maji kilichozungushiwa kabisa, chemchemi yangu peke yangu.
Ekegusii: Moiseke ominto, omoriakari one, naye omogondo ogiteire, naye ensoko y’amaache egiteire, na entuboka emumekire na ebekire ekemanyererio.

English: Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, with precious fruits, henna with spikenard plants,
Kiswahili: Mimea yako ni bustani ya mikomamanga yenye matunda mazuri sana, yenye hina na nardo,
Ekegusii: Buna omogondo ore namakomomanga aye nigo okwama amatunda amaya mono, na ebisicha bikorokwa hena mbireo, na ebimeri bikorokwa narada,

English: spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of incense tree; myrrh and aloes, with all the best spices,
Kiswahili: nardo na zafarani, mchai na mdalasini, pamoja na kila aina ya mti wa uvumba, manemane na udi, na aina zote za vikolezo bora kuliko vyote.
Ekegusii: na ebimeri bigosegwa safarani; boigo kalamusi, na omodalasini, na emete yonsi ya ubani, na manemane, na omogaka, amo nebinsari ebiya mono.

English: a fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, flowing streams from Lebanon.
Kiswahili: Wewe ni chemchemi ya bustani, kisima cha maji yatiririkayo, yakitiririka kutoka Lebanoni.
Ekegusii: Aye nigo onga buna ensoko y’amaache are moyo ere mogondo, naende nigo onga buna chindooche chikorwa Lebanoni.

English: Awake, north wind, and come, you south! Blow on my garden, that its spices may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and taste his precious fruits.
Kiswahili: Amka, upepo wa kaskazini, na uje, upepo wa kusini! Vuma juu ya bustani yangu, ili harufu yake nzuri iweze kuenea mpaka ngʼambo. Mpendwa wangu na aje bustanini mwake na kuonja matunda mazuri sana.
Ekegusii: Aye embeo ekorwa sugusu, imoka! Na aye eyekorwa Irianyi, inchwo! Gusa igoro y’omogondo one, tiga rimisu riaye rigiya rirurukigwe rirande. Tiga omwanchi one ache ase omogondo oye, arie amatunda are amaya mono.

English: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Friends Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved.
Kiswahili: Nimekuja kwenye bustani yangu, dada yangu, bibi arusi wangu; nimekusanya manemane yangu pamoja na kikolezo changu. Nimekula sega langu la asali na asali yangu; nimekunywa divai yangu na maziwa yangu. Marafiki Kuleni, enyi marafiki, mnywe; kunyweni ya kutosha, ee wapenzi.
Ekegusii: Aye moiseke ominto, omoriakari one, nasoire ase omogondo one, ngosangereria inde manemane amo nebinsari biane bigotioka buya; nkoria inde eriana amo nobooke bwane, nkonywa inde edivai yane amo namabeere aane. (Abakungu ba Yerusalemu) Inwe abasani, ragera na monywe! Inwe abanchani, kanywe mono goika moichorwe nobwanchani!

English: I was asleep, but my heart was awake. It is the voice of my beloved who knocks: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; for my head is filled with dew, and my hair with the dampness of the night.”
Kiswahili: Nililala lakini moyo wangu ulikuwa macho. Sikiliza! Mpenzi wangu anabisha: “Nifungulie, dada yangu, mpenzi wangu, hua wangu, asiye na hitilafu. Kichwa changu kimeloa umande, na nywele zangu manyunyu ya usiku.”
Ekegusii: Inche nigo narenge indaire, korende enkoro yane nigo yategesetie. Igwa! Omwanchi one oyio ogokongonta egesieri ogontura. (Omonyuomi) Moiseke ominto, omwanchi one, riruma riane na omoikeranu one, inyigorere! Inyigorere, ekiagera omotwe one otoorire riime, na etukia yane yanyiire nembura ya botuko.

English: I have taken off my robe. Indeed, must I put it on? I have washed my feet. Indeed, must I soil them?
Kiswahili: Nimevua joho langu: je, ni lazima nivae tena? Nimenawa miguu yangu: je, ni lazima niichafue tena?
Ekegusii: Narusirie eanga, inee, inyebeeke naende? Nesibirie amagoro, inee, inyabeeke eubi naende?

English: My beloved thrust his hand in through the latch opening. My heart pounded for him.
Kiswahili: Mpenzi wangu aliweka mkono wake kwenye tundu la komeo; moyo wangu ulianza kugonga kwa ajili yake.
Ekegusii: Erio omwanchi one akabeeka okoboko kwaye ase ekebao, erio nkaba nomosasoko omonene ime ase enkoro yane.

English: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the handles of the lock.
Kiswahili: Niliinuka kumfungulia mpenzi wangu, mikono yangu ikidondosha manemane, vidole vyangu vikitiririka manemane, penye vipini vya komeo.
Ekegusii: Nkaimoka gochia koigorera omwanchi one, amaboko aane akanyororokia manemane, na ebiara biane bigatonyia manemane ekero nabwatete echabi yegesieri.

English: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved left, and had gone away. My heart went out when he spoke. I looked for him, but I didn’t find him. I called him, but he didn’t answer.
Kiswahili: Nilimfungulia mpenzi wangu, lakini mpenzi wangu alishaondoka; alikuwa amekwenda zake. Moyo wangu ulishuka kwa kuondoka kwake. Nilimtafuta lakini sikumpata. Nilimwita lakini hakunijibu.
Ekegusii: Ngachia koigorera omwanchi one, korende nkanyora ng’a ochiire. Omoyo one okairianyeka ekero akwanete. Nkaba nkomorigia, korende tinamonyorete. Nkamorangeria, korende taitabete.

English: The watchmen who go about the city found me. They beat me. They bruised me. The keepers of the walls took my cloak away from me.
Kiswahili: Walinzi walinikuta walipokuwa wakifanya zamu za ulinzi mjini. Walinipiga, wakanijeruhi, wakaninyangʼanya joho langu, hao walinzi wa kuta!
Ekegusii: Ekero abarendi barenge goetanana omochie koyorata, bakanyoora inche, bakang’aka chingoma; bakang’ura egetambaa gi’okwambara, abarendi baria barendete chindwaki.

English: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, that you tell him that I am faint with love.
Kiswahili: Enyi binti za Yerusalemu, ninawaagiza: kama mkimpata mpenzi wangu, mtamwambia nini? Mwambieni ninazimia kwa mapenzi.
Ekegusii: Inwe abasubati ba Yerusalemu, nigo nkobasorora ng’a mokonyora omwanchi one, momoteebie ng’a amaiga ’obwanchani anyaarire.

English: How is your beloved better than another beloved, you fairest among women? How is your beloved better than another beloved, that you do so adjure us?
Kiswahili: Je, mpendwa wako ni bora kuliko wengine namna gani, wewe uliye mzuri kupita wanawake wote? Je, mpendwa wako ni mzuri kuliko wengine, namna gani, hata unatuagiza hivyo?
Ekegusii: Aye ore omoseera kobua abakungu bonsi, inee, omwanchi oyio oo, naki abuete abanchi bande? Ee, omwanchi oyio oo, naki abuete abanchi bande, goika gwatosoroire iga?

English: My beloved is white and ruddy. The best among ten thousand.
Kiswahili: Mpenzi wangu anangʼaa, tena ni mwekundu, wa kuvutia miongoni mwa wanaume kumi elfu.
Ekegusii: Omwanchi one nigo are omorabu se okomeka‐meka, naende omobariri; nigo are nogwatananekana korwa ase abanto chilifu ikomi.

English: His head is like the purest gold. His hair is bushy, black as a raven.
Kiswahili: Kichwa chake ni dhahabu safi kuliko zote, nywele zake ni za mawimbi na ni nyeusi kama kunguru.
Ekegusii: Omotwe oye nigo ore omuya onga etaabu echenire, etukia yaye nigo ere omosamugoku bw’obwari; nigo ere emwamu ti buna amarionya ’ekegonkoru.

English: His eyes are like doves beside the water brooks, washed with milk, mounted like jewels.
Kiswahili: Macho yake ni kama ya hua kandokando ya vijito vya maji, aliyeogeshwa kwenye maziwa, yaliyopangwa kama vito vya thamani.
Ekegusii: Amaiso aye nigo agwekaine amaruma are ase chindooche, ee, nigo anga amaruma asibigwe namabeere, naende nigo anga amagena akomeka‐meka achokire buya.

English: His cheeks are like a bed of spices with towers of perfumes. His lips are like lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.
Kiswahili: Mashavu yake ni kama matuta ya vikolezo yakitoa manukato. Midomo yake ni kama yungiyungi inayodondosha manemane.
Ekegusii: Chinsea chiaye nigo chinga buna ebigondo bi’ebimeri bi’ebinsari, bigotioka rimisu rigiya. Ebikoba biaye nigo binga buna ebisicha ebiya, nigo bigotonyia manemane.

English: His hands are like rings of gold set with beryl. His body is like ivory work overlaid with sapphires.
Kiswahili: Mikono yake ni fimbo za dhahabu iliyopambwa kwa krisolitho. Mwili wake ni kama pembe ya ndovu iliyongʼarishwa iliyopambwa na yakuti samawi.
Ekegusii: Amaboko aye nigo anga buna etaabu ebombire buya, echabeire amagena akomeka‐meka. Omobere oye nigo onga buna amaino e chinchogu aroisirie buya, na gochaberwa namagena e rigori rinene akorokwa safiro.

English: His legs are like pillars of marble set on sockets of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
Kiswahili: Miguu yake ni nguzo za marmar zilizosimikwa katika vitako vya dhahabu safi. Sura yake ni kama Lebanoni, bora kama miti yake ya mierezi.
Ekegusii: Amagoro aye nigo anga chisiiro chi’amagena amarabu se akomeka‐meka, abeekire ase chinterekerero chi’echitaabu chingiya. Okororekana kwaye nigo konga buna okwa Lebanoni, ekieni kiaye nigo kere ekiya buna eki’emecharake,

English: His mouth is sweetness; yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.
Kiswahili: Kinywa chake chenyewe ni utamu, kwa ujumla yeye ni wa kupendeza. Huyu ndiye mpenzi wangu, huyu ndiye rafiki yangu, ee binti za Yerusalemu.
Ekegusii: Chinkwana chiaye nigo chire chinyansu mono, chingencho chiaye chionsi nigo chire echi’ogosanerwa mono. Inwe abasubati ba Yerusalemu, naboigo omwanchi one are, oyio ore omosani one.

English: Where has your beloved gone, you fairest among women? Where has your beloved turned, that we may seek him with you?
Kiswahili: Mpenzi wako amekwenda wapi, ewe mzuri kupita wanawake wote? Mpenzi wako amegeukia njia ipi, tupate kumtafuta pamoja nawe?
Ekegusii: Aye ore omoseera kobua abakungu bonsi, ng’ai omwanchi oo achiire? Omwanchi oyio oo, ng’ai aonchokire gochia? Togende amo naye tomorigie.

English: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
Kiswahili: Mpenzi wangu amekwenda bustanini mwake, kwenye vitalu vya vikolezo, kujilisha bustanini na kukusanya yungiyungi.
Ekegusii: Omwanchi one mogondo agenda, ogendire ase ebigondo bi’ebimeri bi’ebinsari. Ogendire korisia riicho riaye ase emegondo, naende nao akare kona‐gosangereria ebisicha ebiya.

English: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine. He browses among the lilies.
Kiswahili: Mimi ni wake mpenzi wangu, na mpenzi wangu ni wangu; yeye hujilisha katikati ya yungiyungi.
Ekegusii: Inche nigo inde oyo bw’omwanchi one, nere nigo are oyone; nigo akorisia riicho riaye agwo ase ebisicha ebiya bire.

English: You are beautiful, my love, as Tirzah, lovely as Jerusalem, awesome as an army with banners.
Kiswahili: Wewe ni mzuri, mpenzi wangu, kama Tirsa, upendezaye kama Yerusalemu, umetukuka kama jeshi lenye bendera.
Ekegusii: Aye omwanchi one, nigo ore omoseera buna omochie o Tirisa; nigo ore bw’okogokia buna Yerusalemu, na oyo bw’okoirokia buna abasikari babogoretie ebendera.

English: Turn away your eyes from me, for they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats, that lie along the side of Gilead.
Kiswahili: Uyageuze macho yako mbali nami, yananigharikisha. Nywele zako ni kama kundi la mbuzi wanaoteremka kutoka Gileadi.
Ekegusii: Onchora amaiso ao otige kondigereria, ekiagera ambuire; etukia yao nigo enga buna riicho rie chimbori, chigotirimboka ase ebitirimboko bia Gileadi.

English: Your teeth are like a flock of ewes, which have come up from the washing, of which every one has twins; not one is bereaved among them.
Kiswahili: Meno yako ni kama kundi la kondoo watokao kuogeshwa. Kila mmoja ana pacha lake, hakuna hata mmoja aliye peke yake.
Ekegusii: Amaino ao nigo anga riicho rie ching’ondi chiabeeri chianachirwe amarionya, chiarure gosibigwa chiarabire se, chionsi nigo chikobiara chisare, na manwa ende teri egokwa.

English: Your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind your veil.
Kiswahili: Mashavu yako nyuma ya shela yako ni kama vipande viwili vya komamanga.
Ekegusii: Chinsea chiao nigo chitubire ime ase egietubo kiao, nigo chinga buna chimbaara chie ritunda rikorokwa rikomomanga.

English: There are sixty queens, eighty concubines, and virgins without number.
Kiswahili: Panaweza kuwepo malkia sitini, masuria themanini na mabikira wasiohesabika;
Ekegusii: Mbareo abakungu chiting’ana chi’omorwoti emerongo etano nomo, na abakungu ba sere‐sere emerongo etano na etato, boigo mbareo abaiseke abekungi abange batari kobareka.

English: My dove, my perfect one, is unique. She is her mother’s only daughter. She is the favorite one of her who bore her. The daughters saw her, and called her blessed. The queens and the concubines saw her, and they praised her.
Kiswahili: lakini hua wangu, mkamilifu wangu, ni wa namna ya pekee, binti pekee kwa mama yake, kipenzi cha yeye aliyemzaa. Wanawali walimwona na kumwita aliyebarikiwa; malkia na masuria walimsifu.
Ekegusii: Korende oyomo bweka nere omwanchi one, nere riruma riane omoikeranu. Ere nigo are omwana omomoima ng’ina abwate, oyo omoiborete nigo amwanchete. Abaiseke abwo bakamorora, bakamoroka oyosesenirie; abakungu baria chiting’ana na baria ba sere‐sere boigo bakamorora, bakamotogia.

English: Who is she who looks out as the morning, beautiful as the moon, clear as the sun, and awesome as an army with banners?
Kiswahili: Ni nani huyu atokeaye kama mapambazuko, mzuri kama mwezi, mwangavu kama jua, ametukuka kama nyota zifuatanazo?
Ekegusii: Ning’o oyio okorigereria buna erioba rigotonga mambia? Ning’o oyio ore omuya buna omotienyi, na okomeka‐meka buna erioba? Ere nigo are oyo bw’okoirokia buna abasikari babogoretie chibendera chiabo.

English: I went down into the nut tree grove, to see the green plants of the valley, to see whether the vine budded, and the pomegranates were in flower.
Kiswahili: Niliteremka kwenye bustani ya miti ya milozi ili kutazama machipuko ya bondeni, kuona kama mizabibu imechipua au kama mikomamanga imechanua maua.
Ekegusii: Inche nigo natirimbogete gochia ase omogondo bw’emete enga buna emelozi; nkagenda ase rikura korora ebimeri ebiya buna bikoreereta, na korora gose emesabibu yachakire goseboka. Na emekomomanga gose yachakire gosicha.

English: Without realizing it, my desire set me with my royal people’s chariots.
Kiswahili: Kabla sijangʼamua, shauku yangu iliniweka katikati ya magari ya kifalme ya kukokotwa na farasi ya watu wangu.
Ekegusii: Ekero konya ntaramanya, omoyo one okang’ira, okambeka ase egari y’omogambi bw’abaanto baane.

English: Return, return, Shulammite! Return, return, that we may gaze at you. Lover Why do you desire to gaze at the Shulammite, as at the dance of Mahanaim?
Kiswahili: Rudi, rudi, ee Mshulami; rudi, rudi ili tupate kukutazama! Mpenzi Kwa nini kumtazama Mshulami, kama kutazama ngoma ya Mahanaimu?
Ekegusii: Irana! Irana, aye Omosulamiti! Irana! Irana, erinde tokorigererie! (Omoriakari) Nase ki mokondigereria inche Omosulamiti, buna mokorigereria ogotenga kw’ebiombe bibere bi’abasikari?

English: How beautiful are your feet in sandals, prince’s daughter! Your rounded thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a skillful workman.
Kiswahili: Ee binti wa mwana wa mfalme, tazama jinsi inavyopendeza miguu yako katika viatu! Miguu yako yenye madaha ni kama vito vya thamani, kazi ya mikono ya fundi stadi.
Ekegusii: Aye omoiseke bw’omogambi, naki ebisanyi bi’amagoro ao bire ebiya ase ebikoroto ime! Naki ebibwato biao bimerete buya, nigo bire buna emeremo y’omooroisia omong’aini.

English: Your body is like a round goblet, no mixed wine is wanting. Your waist is like a heap of wheat, set about with lilies.
Kiswahili: Kitovu chako ni kama bilauri ya mviringo ambayo kamwe haikosi divai iliyochanganywa. Kiuno chako ni kichuguu cha ngano kilichozungukwa kwa yungiyungi.
Ekegusii: Ekenyobu kiao nigo keborongosire buya buna egetaabo getari koererwa edivai yochoganirie. Enda yao nigo ere buna etui y’engano, eetananeirie ebisicha ebiya.

English: Your two breasts are like two fawns, that are twins of a roe.
Kiswahili: Matiti yako ni kama wana-paa wawili, mapacha wa paa.
Ekegusii: Chimbeere chiao nigo chinga buna chimanwa ibere chire chisare chi’engabi.

English: Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are like the pools in Heshbon by the gate of Bathrabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.
Kiswahili: Shingo yako ni kama mnara wa pembe ya ndovu. Macho yako ni vidimbwi vya Heshboni karibu na lango la Beth-Rabi. Pua lako ni kama mnara wa Lebanoni ukitazama kuelekea Dameski.
Ekegusii: Rigoti riao nigo ringa buna omoorobiri oroiseirie amaino e chinchogu, amaiso ao nigo anga buna amatibo a Hesiboni, ang’e negeita kia Bati‐Rabimu. Emioro yao nigo enga buna omoorobiri o Lebanoni orochie Damesiki.

English: Your head on you is like Carmel. The hair of your head like purple. The king is held captive in its tresses.
Kiswahili: Kichwa chako kinakuvika taji kama mlima Karmeli. Nywele zako ni kama zulia la urujuani; mfalme ametekwa na mashungi yake.
Ekegusii: Omotwe oo nigo osongoire buna egetunwa gia Karimeli. Etukia y’omotwe oo ekona‐gosanyoka nigo ere ekieni kemonyinga; eyio yang’usire omorwoti.

English: How beautiful and how pleasant you are, love, for delights!
Kiswahili: Tazama jinsi ulivyo mzuri na unavyopendeza, ee pendo, kwa uzuri wako!
Ekegusii: Naki aye ore omoseera naende oyo bw’okogokia mono! Aye omwanchi bw’okogokia!

English: This, your stature, is like a palm tree, your breasts like its fruit.
Kiswahili: Umbo lako ni kama la mtende, nayo matiti yako kama vishada vya matunda.
Ekegusii: Aye nigo okinete buna omokendo, ne chimbeere chiao nigo chire buna ebisago bi’amasabibu.

English: I said, “I will climb up into the palm tree. I will take hold of its fruit.” Let your breasts be like clusters of the vine, the smell of your breath like apples.
Kiswahili: Nilisema, “Nitakwea mtende, nami nitayashika matunda yake.” Matiti yako na yawe kama vishada vya mzabibu, harufu nzuri ya pumzi yako kama matofaa,
Ekegusii: Nkarengereria: Nkoriina inde omokendo oyo, imbwaterere chinsagia chiaye. Naki yare koba buya onye chimbeere chiao nchiaba buna ebisago bi’amasabibu, ne rimisu ri’omonwa oo ribe buna eri’amapera,

English: Your mouth is like the best wine, that goes down smoothly for my beloved, gliding through the lips of those who are asleep.
Kiswahili: na kinywa chako kama divai bora kuliko zote. Mpendwa Divai na iende moja kwa moja hadi kwa mpenzi wangu, ikitiririka polepole juu ya midomo na meno.
Ekegusii: na omonwa oo obe buna edivai ere engiya mono. (Omoriakari) Ee, edivai eyio nigo egetirimboka gochia ime y’omwanchi one, naende yanyororoka ng’ora ng’ora, yakuna ebikoba bi’abwo baraire.

English: I am my beloved’s. His desire is toward me.
Kiswahili: Mimi ni mali ya mpenzi wangu, nayo shauku yake ni juu yangu.
Ekegusii: Inche nigo inde oyo bw’omwanchi one, ere nigo are namaiga ase ’nde.

English: Come, my beloved! Let’s go out into the field. Let’s lodge in the villages.
Kiswahili: Njoo, mpenzi wangu, twende mashambani, twende tukalale huko vijijini.
Ekegusii: Aye omwanchi one, inchwo togende ase amaremo aito, tobeere ase emechie botuko,

English: Let’s go early up to the vineyards. Let’s see whether the vine has budded, its blossom is open, and the pomegranates are in flower. There I will give you my love.
Kiswahili: Hebu na twende mapema katika mashamba ya mizabibu tuone kama mizabibu imechipua, kama maua yake yamefunguka, na kama mikomamanga imetoa maua: huko nitakupa penzi langu.
Ekegusii: toimoke mambia chuni togende ase emegondo y’emesabibu, torore gose yachakire goseboka, naende gose amasabibu amanokire na gosicha, boigo gose amakomomanga asichire. Aroro agwo ninkoboanie nobwanchani bwane.

English: The mandrakes produce fragrance. At our doors are all kinds of precious fruits, new and old, which I have stored up for you, my beloved.
Kiswahili: Mitunguja hutoa harufu zake nzuri, kwenye milango yetu kuna matunda mazuri, mapya na ya zamani, ambayo nimekuhifadhia wewe, mpenzi wangu.
Ekegusii: Aye omwanchi one, amatunda amansu nigo agotioka rimisu rigiya mono, na igoro y’ebisieri biaito nareo amatunda ao ao are amaya mono, amakoro na amayia; ayio nasangereirie ase ogokogachera.

English: Oh that you were like my brother, who nursed from the breasts of my mother! If I found you outside, I would kiss you; yes, and no one would despise me.
Kiswahili: Laiti ungelikuwa kwangu kama ndugu wa kiume, ambaye aliyanyonya matiti ya mama yangu! Kisha, kama ningekukuta huko nje, ningelikubusu, wala hakuna mtu yeyote angelinidharau.
Ekegusii: Onye ndiria kwarenge koba momura ominto, kwagongete orobeere rwa baba! Onye ndiria naumeranete naye isiko, nanga nigo nare gokonyunyunta, na onde tare gonchaya.

English: I would lead you, bringing you into the house of my mother, who would instruct me. I would have you drink spiced wine, of the juice of my pomegranate.
Kiswahili: Ningelikuongoza na kukuleta katika nyumba ya mama yangu, yeye ambaye amenifundisha. Ningelikupa divai iliyokolezwa unywe, asali ya maua ya mikomamanga yangu.
Ekegusii: Nigo nanga nakorentete mwa baba, obe gokonyorokereria. Nigo nare gocha gokoa onywe edivai yochoganirie ebinsari, naende nkoe amaache amitire korwa ase amakomomanga aane.

English: His left hand would be under my head. His right hand would embrace me.
Kiswahili: Mkono wake wa kushoto uko chini ya kichwa changu, na mkono wake wa kuume unanikumbatia.
Ekegusii: Okoboko kwaye kwa bomosi nigo kore inse y’omotwe one, na okwa borio komboanetie.

English: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.
Kiswahili: Binti za Yerusalemu, ninawaagiza: msichochee wala kuamsha mapenzi hata yatakapotaka yenyewe.
Ekegusii: Inwe abasubati ba Yerusalemu, nigo nkobasorora na kobatiania ng’a timobaisa gotabobora obwanchani na koboichania, goika bobe bwancheranire obonyene.

English: Who is this who comes up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? Beloved Under the apple tree I awakened you. There your mother conceived you. There she was in labor and bore you.
Kiswahili: Ni nani huyu anayekuja kutoka nyikani akimwegemea mpenzi wake? Mpendwa Nilikuamsha chini ya mtofaa, huko mama yako alipotunga mimba yako, huko yeye alipata utungu akakuzaa.
Ekegusii: Monto ki oria ogotiira gocha aa korwa ase erooro, oyio bweegegete omwanchi oye? (Omoriakari) Agwo inse y’omote bw’amapera inche nigo nagoturete oboke. Aroro agwo nyoko nigo arenge nobororo bw’okobina akoibore, ee, agwo nao nyoko akoiborerete ore nobororo.

English: Set me as a seal on your heart, as a seal on your arm; for love is strong as death. Jealousy is as cruel as Sheol. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a very flame of Yah.
Kiswahili: Nitie kama muhuri moyoni mwako, kama muhuri kwenye mkono wako; kwa maana upendo una nguvu kama mauti, wivu wake ni mkatili kama kuzimu. Unachoma kama mwali wa moto, kama mwali mkubwa wa moto wa Bwana hasa.
Ekegusii: Imbeke ase enkoro yao imbe buna ebonyi ere nekemanyererio, ee, buna ebonyi ere nekemanyererio ase okoboko kwao. Obwanchani nigo bore ne chinguru buna amakweri, ne ribero nigo rire ritindi buna embeera. Ogwoka kw’obwanchani nigo konga ebibemberi bi’omorero, ee, nekebemberi gekorwa ase Omonene.

English: Many waters can’t quench love, neither can floods drown it. If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned.
Kiswahili: Maji mengi hayawezi kuuzimisha upendo, mito haiwezi kuugharikisha. Kama mtu angelitoa mali yote ya nyumbani mwake kwa ajili ya upendo, angelidharauliwa kabisa.
Ekegusii: Amaache are amange mono takonyara gokendia obwanchani, gose chindooche tichikonyara koboiranana. Omonto naisa korua obotenenku bwonsi bw’enyomba yaye konyora obwanchani, oyio nigo arachaywe.

English: We have a little sister. She has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister in the day when she is to be spoken for?
Kiswahili: Tunaye dada mdogo, matiti yake hayajakua bado. Tutafanya nini kwa ajili ya dada yetu wakati atakapokuja kuposwa?
Ekegusii: Intwe ntobwate omoiseke ominto ore omoke, korende tabwati mbeere; ekero engaki yaye erache akorigigwa anyuomwe, ninki torakorere omoiseke oyio ominto?

English: If she is a wall, we will build on her a turret of silver. If she is a door, we will enclose her with boards of cedar.
Kiswahili: Kama yeye ni ukuta, tutajenga minara ya fedha juu yake. Na kama yeye ni mlango, tutamzungushia mbao za mierezi.
Ekegusii: Ere karabe orwaki, ntoagache igoro yaye omoorobiri oroiseirie efeta, korende karabe egesieri, rirorio ntomosiekere ne chibao chi’emecharake.

English: I am a wall, and my breasts like towers, then I was in his eyes like one who found peace.
Kiswahili: Mimi ni ukuta, nayo matiti yangu ni kama minara. Ndivyo ambavyo nimekuwa machoni pake kama yule anayeleta utoshelevu.
Ekegusii: Inche nigo inde orwaki, ne chimbeere chiane nigo chinga buna emerobiri; ase ayio nkaba ase amaiso aye buna oyo onyorire omorembe.

English: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal Hamon. He leased out the vineyard to keepers. Each was to bring a thousand shekels of silver for its fruit.
Kiswahili: Solomoni alikuwa na shamba la mizabibu huko Baal-Hamoni; alikodisha shamba lake la mizabibu kwa wapangaji. Kila mmoja angeleta kwa ajili ya matunda yake shekeli 1,000 za fedha.
Ekegusii: Sulemani nabwate omogondo bw’emesabibu agwo Baali‐Hamoni, akayotigera abarendi, na kera omorendi nigo arenge korenta chitaabu chi’echifeta elifu eyemo goakanera amatunda.

English: My own vineyard is before me. The thousand are for you, Solomon, two hundred for those who tend its fruit.
Kiswahili: Lakini shamba langu la mizabibu ambalo ni langu mwenyewe ni langu kutoa; hizo shekeli 1,000 ni kwa ajili yako, ee Solomoni, na shekeli mia mbili ni kwa ajili ya wale wanaotunza matunda yake.
Ekegusii: Korende omogondo bw’emesabibu oyore oyone bori ninche omonyene nyorendete. Aye Sulemani, ira chilifu chiao, na abarendi b’amatunda baire amagana abere.

English: You who dwell in the gardens, with friends in attendance, let me hear your voice!
Kiswahili: Wewe ukaaye bustanini pamoja na marafiki mliohudhuria, hebu nisikie sauti yako!
Ekegusii: Aye oria omenyete ase emegondo, abagisangio baane nigo bategererete baigwe eriogi riao, tiga nainche indiigwe.

English: Come away, my beloved! Be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices!
Kiswahili: Njoo, mpenzi wangu, uwe kama swala au kama ayala kijana juu ya milima iliyojaa vikolezo.
Ekegusii: Aye omwanchi one, minyoka bwango, obe buna engabi gose ensune ensae ekominyoka igoro ase ebitunwa bire nebimeri bigotioka buya.

English: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Kiswahili: Maono kuhusu Yuda na Yerusalemu ambayo Isaya mwana wa Amozi aliyaona wakati wa utawala wa Uzia, Yothamu, Ahazi na Hezekia, wafalme wa Yuda.
Ekegusii: Aya namaroro Isaya, mosinto bw’Amosi, aroche igoro y’ense y’Abayuda na omochie o Yerusalemu ekero Usia, na Yotamu, na Ahasi, na Hezekia, baarenge abarwoti ase ense y’Abayuda.

English: Hear, heavens, and listen, earth; for Yahweh has spoken: “I have nourished and brought up children and they have rebelled against me.
Kiswahili: Sikieni, enyi mbingu! Sikilizeni, enyi dunia! Kwa maana Bwana amesema: “Nimewalisha watoto na kuwalea, lakini wameniasi mimi.
Ekegusii: Inwe igoro, na aye ense, tegerera moigwe, ekiagera Omonene okwanire, ogoteeba: “Abana nabeire nkorera na kobakinia basaririe ase ’nde.

English: The ox knows his owner, and the donkey his master’s crib; but Israel doesn’t know. My people don’t consider.”
Kiswahili: Ngʼombe anamjua bwana wake, naye punda anajua hori la mmiliki wake, lakini Israeli hajui, watu wangu hawaelewi.”
Ekegusii: Eng’ombe nigo emanyete omonyene, na etigere nigo emanyete aase omonene oye akoyeera endagera, korende Abaisraeli tibamanyeti kende, ee, amaene, abanto baane tibamanyeti kende gionsi.”

English: Ah sinful nation, a people loaded with iniquity, offspring of evildoers, children who deal corruptly! They have forsaken Yahweh. They have despised the Holy One of Israel. They are estranged and backward.
Kiswahili: Lo! Taifa lenye dhambi, watu waliolemewa na uovu, uzao wa watenda mabaya, watoto waliozoelea upotovu! Wamemwacha Bwana, Wamemkataa kwa dharau yeye Aliye Mtakatifu wa Israeli na kumgeuzia kisogo.
Ekegusii: Obobe nobwaino inwe egesaku kere nebibe ebinge, inwe abanto moritoeire nobobe, inwe oroiboro rw’abasaria, abanto abakorekanu, mogokora ogosaria. Mwangire Omonene, mwachayire Omochenu bw’Abaisraeli, mwairanire magega na mwamotigire kegima.

English: Why should you be beaten more, that you revolt more and more? The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.
Kiswahili: Kwa nini mzidi kupigwa? Kwa nini kudumu katika uasi? Kichwa chako chote kimejeruhiwa, moyo wako wote ni mgonjwa.
Ekegusii: Nase ki mogendererete gosaria? Nigo moganetie konyora egesusuro goetania? Omotwe bwonsi orwarire, na enkoro yanyarekire.

English: From the sole of the foot even to the head there is no soundness in it, but wounds, welts, and open sores. They haven’t been closed, bandaged, or soothed with oil.
Kiswahili: Kutoka wayo wako wa mguu hadi kwenye utosi wa kichwa chako hakuna uzima: ni majeraha matupu na makovu na vidonda vitokavyo damu, havikusafishwa au kufungwa wala kulainishwa kwa mafuta.
Ekegusii: Korwa egesanyi gi’okogoro inse goika omotwe igoro, aande tari are buya. Chingoma nchireo, na obobimbu, na amaote akorua amaira. Amaote ayio tasibiri na kobogwa, gose taakiri amaguta ororobe.

English: Your country is desolate. Your cities are burned with fire. Strangers devour your land in your presence and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.
Kiswahili: Nchi yenu imekuwa ukiwa, miji yenu imeteketezwa kwa moto; nchi yenu imeachwa tupu na wageni mbele ya macho yenu, imeharibiwa kama vile imepinduliwa na wageni.
Ekegusii: Ense yaino yasarigwe yatigaire ere bosa, emechie yaino yasambirwe nomorero; abanto b’egesaku ekeao barire okwama kw’emegondo yaino ase amaiso aino. Ense yasarigwe na koonchoranwa nabarabwo.

English: The daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a field of melons, like a besieged city.
Kiswahili: Binti Sayuni ameachwa kama kipenu katika shamba la mizabibu, kama kibanda katika shamba la matikitimaji, kama mji uliohusuriwa.
Ekegusii: Omoiseke oria Sayoni otigirwe buna egesa gi’okorendera kere ase omogondo bw’emesabibu giatigirwe bosa; nigo anga buna ekegutu kere ase omogondo bw’amasosa, na buna omochie oboeire.

English: Unless Yahweh of Armies had left to us a very small remnant, we would have been as Sodom. We would have been like Gomorrah.
Kiswahili: Kama Bwana Mungu Mwenye Nguvu Zote asingelituachia walionusurika, tungelikuwa kama Sodoma, tungelifanana na Gomora.
Ekegusii: Onye Omonene bw’Emeganda atatotigerete abatigari bake, nanga nigo twabeete buna Sodomu na Gomora.

English: Hear Yahweh’s word, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah!
Kiswahili: Sikieni neno la Bwana, ninyi watawala wa Sodoma; sikilizeni sheria ya Mungu wetu, enyi watu wa Gomora!
Ekegusii: Inwe abagaambi ba Sodomu, igwa ring’ana ri’Omonene! Inwe abanto ba Gomora, tegerera moigwe amorokererio a Nyasae oito!

English: “What are the multitude of your sacrifices to me?”, says Yahweh. “I have had enough of the burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fed animals. I don’t delight in the blood of bulls, or of lambs, or of male goats.
Kiswahili: Bwana anasema, “Wingi wa sadaka zenu, ni kitu gani kwangu? Ninazo sadaka za kuteketezwa nyingi kupita kiasi, za kondoo dume na mafuta ya wanyama walionona. Sipendezwi na damu za mafahali wala za wana-kondoo na mbuzi.
Ekegusii: Omonene nigo agoteeba iga: “Ebing’wanso biaino ebinge mokorua ase ’nde, ninki ndakore nabirobio? Nigo narosire n’ebing’wanso bi’ogosambwa bie chimingichi, na ebitinya bie ching’iti chinoru. Tingokiri namanyinga e chieri, gose aye chimanwa chi’eching’ondi, gose aye chigoree.

English: When you come to appear before me, who has required this at your hand, to trample my courts?
Kiswahili: Mnapokuja kujihudhurisha mbele zangu, ni nani aliyewataka ninyi mfanye hivyo, huku kuzikanyaga nyua zangu?
Ekegusii: Ning’o okobaboria ng’a morentane ebinto ebio bionsi ekero mogocha ase obosio bwane na gotaara‐taara ase chiraaro chiane?

English: Bring no more vain offerings. Incense is an abomination to me. New moons, Sabbaths, and convocations— I can’t stand evil assemblies.
Kiswahili: Acheni kuniletea sadaka zisizokuwa na maana! Uvumba wenu ni chukizo kwangu. Miandamo ya Mwezi, Sabato na makusanyiko ya ibada: siwezi kuvumilia makusanyiko yenu maovu.
Ekegusii: Tiga korenta ase ’nde ebing’wanso bi’obong’ainereria; ogosambwa kwa ubani kwabeire okogechia ase ’nde, naboigo nemeyega y’Emetienyi Emeyia, ne Chisabato, na emesangererekano mokorangeria. Tinkonyara koremereria emesangererekano buna eyio yasarigwe nebibe.

English: My soul hates your New Moons and your appointed feasts. They are a burden to me. I am weary of bearing them.
Kiswahili: Sikukuu zenu za Miandamo ya Mwezi, na sikukuu zenu zilizoamriwa: moyo wangu unazichukia. Zimekuwa mzigo kwangu, nimechoka kuzivumilia.
Ekegusii: Inche nigo ngechete emeyega y’Amatuko Amanene na ey’Emetienyi Emeyia; eyio yabeire egurube endito ase ’nde, narosire ase okona‐koyeremereria.

English: When you spread out your hands, I will hide my eyes from you. Yes, when you make many prayers, I will not hear. Your hands are full of blood.
Kiswahili: Mnaponyoosha mikono yenu katika maombi, nitaficha macho yangu nisiwaone; hata mkiomba maombi mengi sitasikiliza. Mikono yenu imejaa damu;
Ekegusii: “Ekero morarambore amaboko aino ase ogosaba, inche nigo ndatube amaiso aane timbarora, na ekero morabe mogosaba mono, tinkobaigwa ekiagera amaboko aino nigo aichire amanyinga.

English: Wash yourselves. Make yourself clean. Put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes. Cease to do evil.
Kiswahili: jiosheni na mkajitakase. Yaondoeni matendo yenu maovu mbele zangu! Acheni kutenda mabaya,
Ekegusii: Esibie na mwechene; rusia ogokora kwaino okobe korwa ase amaiso aane; tiga gokora ayare amabe.

English: Learn to do well. Seek justice. Relieve the oppressed. Defend the fatherless. Plead for the widow.”
Kiswahili: jifunzeni kutenda mema! Tafuteni haki, watieni moyo walioonewa. Teteeni shauri la yatima, wateteeni wajane.
Ekegusii: Mweorokererie gokora ayare amaya, rigia ay’oboronge; bakonye abwo bagokorerwa bobe; rwanerera chintaaka, na monyorere ababoraka oboronge bwabo.”

English: “Come now, and let’s reason together,” says Yahweh: “Though your sins are as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow. Though they are red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
Kiswahili: “Njooni basi tuhojiane,” asema Bwana. “Ingawa dhambi zenu ni kama rangi nyekundu, zitakuwa nyeupe kama theluji; ingawa ni nyekundu sana kama damu, zitakuwa nyeupe kama sufu.
Ekegusii: Omonene nigo agoteeba iga: “Inchuo togaamberane nonya ebibe biaino biabariirire, mbisibigwe birabe se, bibe buna amagena ’embura; nonya biabeire ebibariri burure, mbirabe se bibe buna amarionya amarabu e ching’ondi.

English: If you are willing and obedient, you will eat the good of the land;
Kiswahili: Kama mkikubali na kutii, mtakula mema ya nchi,
Ekegusii: Komoranche koigwera, rirorio morie amaya ay’ense,

English: but if you refuse and rebel, you will be devoured with the sword; for Yahweh’s mouth has spoken it.”
Kiswahili: lakini kama mkikataa na kuasi, mtaangamizwa kwa upanga.” Kwa kuwa kinywa cha Bwana kimenena.
Ekegusii: korende komoraange koigwera naende komorasarie, goika moitwe nemioro. Nabo inche Omonene nateebire nomonwa one.”

English: How the faithful city has become a prostitute! She was full of justice. Righteousness lodged in her, but now there are murderers.
Kiswahili: Tazama jinsi mji uliokuwa mwaminifu umekuwa kahaba! Mwanzoni ulikuwa umejaa unyofu, haki ilikuwa inakaa ndani yake, lakini sasa ni wauaji!
Ekegusii: Omochie oyio orenge omwegenwa obeire buna omokungu omotayayi. Agwo kare nigo orenge konacha ebiina bia boronge, na oboronge nigo bwarenge ime yaye, korende bono abanto baye babeire abaiti.

English: Your silver has become dross, your wine mixed with water.
Kiswahili: Fedha yenu imekuwa takataka, divai yenu nzuri imechanganywa na maji.
Ekegusii: Chifeta chiao chiabeire bosa buna amabiria, na edivai yao yochoganigwe namaache.

English: Your princes are rebellious and companions of thieves. Everyone loves bribes and follows after rewards. They don’t defend the fatherless, neither does the cause of the widow come to them.
Kiswahili: Watawala wenu ni waasi, rafiki wa wevi, wote wanapenda rushwa na kukimbilia hongo. Hawatetei yatima, shauri la mjane haliletwi mbele yao lisikilizwe.
Ekegusii: Abatang’ani bao nigo bare abasaria, naende babeire abagisangio b’abaibi. Kera oyomo obo nigo anchete riaaki, na nigo are omwango kwerigeria ebitoki. Tibari korwanerera chintaakana, nigo bakwanga koigwa amang’ana ’ababoraka.

English: Therefore the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel, says: “Ah, I will get relief from my adversaries, and avenge myself on my enemies.
Kiswahili: Kwa hiyo Bwana, Bwana Mwenye Nguvu Zote, Mwenye Nguvu wa Israeli, asema hivi: “Lo, nitapata faraja kutoka kwa adui zangu na kujilipizia kisasi juu ya watesi wangu.
Ekegusii: Ase ayio Omonene, oyore Omonene bw’Emeganda, ore Omobui ase egati y’Abaisraeli, oteebire iga: “Naama! Ning’itere endamwamu yane ase ababisa baane, naende inche omonyene ninyeruserie egesiomba ase bare.

English: I will turn my hand on you, thoroughly purge away your dross, and will take away all your tin.
Kiswahili: Nitauelekeza mkono wangu dhidi yenu, nitawasafisha takataka zenu zote na kuwaondolea unajisi wenu wote.
Ekegusii: Ning’onchore okoboko kwane kobe igoro yao, konyititore, korusie amabiria ao buna ogosisikerigwa kwe ribu na korusia ayatakogwenereti.

English: I will restore your judges as at the first, and your counselors as at the beginning. Afterward you shall be called ‘The city of righteousness, a faithful town.’
Kiswahili: Nitawarudishia waamuzi wenu kama ilivyokuwa siku za zamani, nao washauri wenu kama ilivyokuwa mwanzoni. Baadaye utaitwa, Mji wa Haki, Mji Mwaminifu.”
Ekegusii: Nimbae naende abagaambi ebiina buna baria b’eritang’ani, na abasemia buna baria ba kare. Magega y’ayio norokwe Omochie bw’oboronge, na Omochie bw’obwegenwa.”

English: Zion shall be redeemed with justice, and her converts with righteousness.
Kiswahili: Sayuni itakombolewa kwa haki, wale waliomo ndani yake waliotubu kwa uaminifu.
Ekegusii: Omochie o Sayoni nigo oraboorigwe goetera ase ekiina kia boronge na abaonchokire ime yaye mbaboorigwe goetera ase oboronge.

English: But the destruction of transgressors and sinners shall be together, and those who forsake Yahweh shall be consumed.
